functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans on separate pylons produce thrust; each engine fails independently, left/right pairs in separate zones (SDD §5.1.2, §5.1.5).
functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).

functions.subDef: Thrust reversers on the two inboard engines, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement (SDD §5.1.2).
functions.funcDef: Produce and control propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).

functions.subDef: Dedicated collector per engine with two parallel AC boost pumps and a gravity path below FL150 (SDD §5.2.2).
functions.funcDef: Store fuel and deliver it to the engines and APU at required pressure and flow, and manage mass distribution (SDD §5.2.1).

functions.subDef: Scheduled transfer and single spanwise cross-feed gallery hold CG and wing bending within limits; imbalance annunciated at 1,200 kg (SDD §5.2.2, §5.2.3).
functions.funcDef: Store fuel and deliver it to the engines and APU at required pressure and flow, and manage mass distribution (SDD §5.2.1).

functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers, ailerons on hydraulic systems B and C (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators on hydraulic systems A and C, plus mechanical trim reversion (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments on hydraulic systems A and B respectively, with mechanical reversion on the lower segment; sized by outboard engine-out at V1 (SDD §5.3.2, §5.3.3).
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span slats via two power drive units on a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (SDD §5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: One nose unit and six main bogies (twenty tyres) sized for semi-prepared flotation; retraction/extension on HYD A with free-fall alternate (SDD §5.6.2).
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support aircraft and absorb ground loads
functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on ground

functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking normally from HYD B, alternate from HYD A, with accumulator emergency braking and per-wheel-pair anti-skid (SDD §5.6.2).
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on ground

functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals with mechanical disconnect for towing (SDD §5.6.2).
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads on semi-prepared surfaces, and provide braking and ground directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on ground

functions.subDef: Upward-hinging nose visor on HYD A with electric backup; twelve latches on a common torque shaft, eight independent pins on a separate supply, dual dissimilar lock sensing and a pressure interlock (SDD §5.7.2).
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the hold and restrain a single unitised blade through all load cases (SDD §5.7.1, §5.8.1).
functions.subName: Provide nose loading access and pressure boundary closure

functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two electric-winch tension straps each and a single instrumented tension monitoring loop; loss of tension annunciated in flight (SDD §5.8.2).
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access to the hold and restrain a single unitised blade through all load cases (SDD §5.7.1, §5.8.1).

functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs fed from four engine bleeds via a cross-bleed manifold, conditioning two separate zones (SDD §5.9.2).
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).
functions.subName: Condition flight deck and hold air

functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves with pneumatic backup and independent mechanical positive/negative relief; hold differential preliminary (SDD §5.9.2).
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Bleed-air protection of wing leading edges and engine cowls, and electrically heated stabiliser leading edges in six independent zones (SDD §5.10.2).
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes across the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect surfaces and inlets from ice

functions.subDef: Electrically heated probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors of the same type, individually monitored (SDD §5.10.2).
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes across the icing envelope of the certification basis (SDD §5.10.1).

functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs driven by three display processors on dual networks; three air data inertial reference units; independent standby instrument on DC essential (SDD §5.11.2).
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host failure alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Acquire and present flight and navigation data

functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, on two independent processing channels (SDD §5.11.2).
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host failure alerting (SDD §5.11.1).

functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU with AND logic degrading to single-loop; bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat; nine-station hold smoke detection (SDD §5.12.2).
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair and one dedicated APU bottle discharged automatically when unattended; hold has no suppression (SDD §5.12.2).
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feeding four quick-donning demand-regulator masks; no passenger oxygen (SDD §5.13.2).
functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for depressurisation, smoke and fume events and the ensuing descent and diversion (SDD §5.13.1).

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi
fha.effAc: No forward thrust available; aircraft remains on the ground and the take-off is not commenced.
fha.effCrew: Crew abort ground operation; no timed task yet — level recorded as assumed pending the HF workload analysis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect not realised in flight; the aircraft stops on the ground. "failure conditions that would have no effect on safety" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.1). [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. Effect not realised in these phases and the flight can be escaped (stop on the ground), which this failure does not defeat — No Safety Effect by rule (4 Sep 2026 ruling); the drafted levels (none / none / none or slight inconvenience) describe the end effect and are recorded here, not on the row. — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Rejected Takeoff

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the total loss becomes evident and the reject is initiated before V1; if the loss occurs at/after V1 in the take-off roll the escape is defeated and the row carries the airborne end effect. Confirm against the RTO timeline.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation
fha.phases: Initial Climb, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Go-around
fha.effAc: All forward thrust lost with the aircraft airborne; outside the MAC — no thrust from any engine and no means to arrest the descent; loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities; the crew are aboard and hull loss is credited as not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew aboard sustain fatalities with loss of the aircraft.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Airborne loss of all thrust prevents continued safe flight and landing. "A failure condition that would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Outside the MAC (the rule at least 1 of [Engine 1 (left outboard), Engine 2 (left inboard)] AND at least 1 of [Engine 3 (right inboard), Engine 4 (right outboard)] is breached) — the aircraft level is the loss itself, with the escape rule on top. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-001-TL — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust generation
fha.phases: Takeoff, Initial Climb, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing, Rejected Takeoff, Go-around
fha.effAc: One engine lost, inside the MAC (at least one of engines 1/2 and one of engines 3/4 remain); a significant reduction in functional capabilities; the aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage the engine-out case; no timed task yet — level recorded as assumed pending the HF workload analysis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: MAC — partial loss: degraded, but the minimum acceptable configuration for this function still holds. Rule: at least 1 of [Engine 1 (left outboard), Engine 2 (left inboard)] AND at least 1 of [Engine 3 (right inboard), Engine 4 (right outboard)] (AEO-SDD-0001 §5.1.3). | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Design continues on the remaining engines; "a significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3). [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). Aircraft level derived from the MAC — MAC at least 1 of [Engine 1 (left outboard), Engine 2 (left inboard)] AND at least 1 of [Engine 3 (right inboard), Engine 4 (right outboard)]: 1 lost, 1 spare above the floor → significant. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-001-PL — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust generation
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust on the ground managed within nose-wheel steering and braking authority; take-off not commenced.
fha.effCrew: Crew arrest the yaw and withhold take-off; no timed task yet — level recorded as assumed pending the HF workload analysis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Ground asymmetry countered with steering; "a slight reduction in safety margins" / slight workload increase (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2). [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). Malfunction — the MAC governs configuration, not erroneous operation; the aircraft level is the drafter's. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-001-M — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust generation
fha.phases: Takeoff, Rejected Takeoff
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm during the take-off roll on a semi-prepared strip; the directional-control sizing case, with a large reduction in directional safety margin before the crew arrests the excursion.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply rudder/steering to hold the runway; physical distress or excessive workload possible in this regime; level assumed pending the HF workload analysis.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew aboard.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the outboard-engine asymmetry at the 28 m arm during the take-off roll reduces directional margin to the Hazardous band before the crew arrests it; the SDD names this as the sizing case but gives no handling-quality result. Rudder authority analysis and the RTO handling data would confirm or lower this to Major.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes the outboard-engine asymmetry at the 28 m arm during the take-off roll reduces directional margin to the Hazardous band before the crew arrests it; the SDD names this as the sizing case but gives no handling-quality result. Rudder authority analysis and the RTO handling data would confirm or lower this to Major. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Directional-control sizing case at the 28 m arm on a semi-prepared surface; "a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4). Malfunction — the MAC governs configuration, not erroneous operation; the aircraft level is the drafter's. fha.effAc: On the ground with no rotation demand, total loss of pitch control has no effect on the ground path; no reduction in functional capabilities or safety margins.
fha.effCrew: No effect on flight-crew workload on the ground; the condition is detected and the take-off not commenced.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect.
fha.comments: MAC — total loss: the loss takes the aircraft outside the minimum acceptable configuration for this function. Rule: not yet defined for this function — to be set from the systems design. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "Failure conditions that would have no effect on safety", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.1 — the aircraft is stopped on the ground and the take-off is not commenced. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. fha.effAc: Pitch control remains available at reduced authority; the crew retain control but with a significant reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities, most acute at forward centre-of-gravity with the full-length blade payload.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload to manage the flightpath with degraded pitch authority within crew capability.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no injury credited at this level.
fha.judgementNote: No MAC rule for pitch control yet — aircraft level assumed pending the MAC; crew workload level assumed pending the HF task analysis. Grading assumes sufficient residual pitch authority for continued controlled flight and landing; a MAC showing the partial loss can degrade to insufficient authority (e.g. at the forward-CG blade case) would raise this toward Hazardous.

fha.effAc: Pressurisation control drives an erroneous cabin altitude or rate; independent positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure, but an erroneous schedule can drive flight-deck cabin altitude off-target before crew intervention. Large reduction in safety margins at cruise altitudes.
fha.effCrew: Flight crew detect the abnormal cabin altitude/rate, select manual mode, and don oxygen if cabin altitude climbs; workload increase is not yet timed against an HF task analysis.
fha.effPax: None directly — no passengers; risk is to the flight crew, mitigated by manual reversion and crew oxygen.
fha.judgementNote: Class assumes the crew detect and revert to manual before cabin altitude becomes incapacitating, and that mechanical relief bounds structural risk; if detection is unreliable the undetected variant would be more severe. Crew-workload level is assumed (large) pending a timed HF task analysis. Confirm alerting coverage for erroneous cabin altitude/rate.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Class assumes the crew detect and revert to manual before cabin altitude becomes incapacitating, and that mechanical relief bounds structural risk; if detection is unreliable the undetected variant would be more severe. Crew-workload level is assumed (large) pending a timed HF task analysis. Confirm alerting coverage for erroneous cabin altitude/rate. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4 — an erroneous pressurisation schedule at altitude, bounded by mechanical relief and manual reversion with crew oxygen. Crew axis is an assumed level pending the HF workload. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Hazardous (aircraft and crew axes govern). Malfunction — the MAC governs configuration, not erroneous operation; the aircraft level is the drafter's. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-015-M — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

Rule: at least 1 of [Ice detector 1 (left forward fuselage), Ice detector 2 (right forward fuselage)] (AEO-SDD-0001 §5.10.2). | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "a significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3 — loss of detection removes automatic cueing but manual selection of ice protection remains. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). Outside the MAC (the rule at least 1 of [Ice detector 1 (left forward fuselage), Ice detector 2 (right forward fuselage)] is breached) — the aircraft level is the loss itself, with the escape rule on top. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-017-TL — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of probe protection
fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: Slight reduction in functional capabilities: reduced probe/heater coverage during approach and landing; remaining probe protection and monitoring continue to support air data.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload to monitor affected probe status during landing.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect.
fha.comments: MAC — partial loss: degraded, but the minimum acceptable configuration for this function still holds. Rule: at least 1 of [Ice detector 1 (left forward fuselage), Ice detector 2 (right forward fuselage)] (AEO-SDD-0001 §5.10.2). | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "a slight reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2 — partial probe protection loss with probes monitored individually and remaining coverage intact. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Hazardous (aircraft axis governs). Model proposed Minor; the class is derived from the levels. Aircraft level derived from the MAC — MAC at least 1 of [Ice detector 1 (left forward fuselage), Ice detector 2 (right forward fuselage)]: 1 lost, 0 spare above the floor → large. (drafter proposed slight). No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-017-PL — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous icing detection
fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: Slight reduction in functional capabilities: erroneous icing detection may command wing anti-ice on approach, applying an automatic performance penalty when not required, or fail to indicate icing; ice protection remains manually selectable and detection is advisory.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload to cross-check erroneous detection against conditions during landing.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed erroneous detection either nuisance-activates anti-ice (performance penalty applied automatically) or gives a false clear the crew can cross-check; if a false 'clear' in actual icing on final leaves the aircraft unprotected without crew recognition, the class rises. Confirm crew cross-check credit and the false-negative case with IPS analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumed erroneous detection either nuisance-activates anti-ice (performance penalty applied automatically) or gives a false clear the crew can cross-check; if a false 'clear' in actual icing on final leaves the aircraft unprotected without crew recognition, the class rises. Confirm crew cross-check credit and the false-negative case with IPS analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "a slight increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2 — detection is advisory with manual selection available, so an erroneous indication is a workload/performance-penalty item. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). Malfunction — the MAC governs configuration, not erroneous operation; the aircraft level is the drafter's. No crew task in the Task Analysis is tied to SF-017-M — the crew level is the drafter's, assumed pending the human-factors workload. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi, Rejected Takeoff
fha.effAc: On the ground the aircraft is stopped or can be stopped on the runway before the excursion develops; no reduction in functional capability results.
fha.effCrew: Crew stop or hold the aircraft on the ground; no increase in workload beyond normal.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "no effect on safety", NSE-1 — effect not realised in ground phases and the flight is stopped on the ground. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. Effect not realised in these phases and the flight can be escaped (stop on the ground / stop on the runway), which this failure does not defeat — No Safety Effect by rule (4 Sep 2026 ruling); the drafted levels (none / none / none or slight inconvenience) describe the end effect and are recorded here, not on the row. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi, Rejected Takeoff
fha.effAc: On the ground the reduced pitch authority is not demanded and the aircraft is stopped or held; no functional-capability reduction results.
fha.effCrew: No crew action required; no workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "no effect on safety", NSE-1 — pitch authority not demanded on the ground. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. Effect not realised in these phases and the flight can be escaped (stop on the ground / stop on the runway), which this failure does not defeat — No Safety Effect by rule (4 Sep 2026 ruling); the drafted levels (none / none / none or slight inconvenience) describe the end effect and are recorded here, not on the row. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi, Rejected Takeoff
fha.effAc: On the ground pitch command is not flown; the aircraft is stopped or held on the runway; no reduction in functional capability results.
fha.effCrew: No corrective action required on the ground; no workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "no effect on safety", NSE-1 — erroneous pitch response not realised in ground phases. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. Effect not realised in these phases and the flight can be escaped (stop on the ground / stop on the runway), which this failure does not defeat — No Safety Effect by rule (4 Sep 2026 ruling); the drafted levels (none / none / none or slight inconvenience) describe the end effect and are recorded here, not on the row. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected uncommanded pitch motion
fha.phases: Standing, Taxi, Rejected Takeoff
fha.effAc: On the ground the aircraft is stopped or held; an uncommanded pitch input does not develop into an excursion; no reduction in functional capability results.
fha.effCrew: No action required; no workload increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: "no effect on safety", NSE-1 — uncommanded pitch not realised in ground phases. [anchor NSE-1 — No Safety Effect] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew none · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → No Safety Effect (all three axes at the catastrophic step). Model proposed No Safety Effect; the class is derived from the levels. Effect not realised in these phases and the flight can be escaped (stop on the ground / stop on the runway), which this failure does not defeat — No Safety Effect by rule (4 Sep 2026 ruling); the drafted levels (none / none / none or slight inconvenience) describe the end effect and are recorded here, not on the row. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The four systems the SDD labels as resources (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are treated as consumed resources, not aircraft functions, except that fuel DELIVERY to engines is retained as a behaviour the aircraft accomplishes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants hydraulic/electrical distribution captured as functions rather than resources, additional top functions and sub-functions would be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of HYD/EPS/EWS top functions; retention of 'Deliver fuel to engines' with its two sub-functions

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS as resources but §5.2.1 describes fuel delivery as an active behaviour; the modeling rule forbids authoring power supplies as functions, forcing a judgment on where fuel sits.

assumptions.text: The nose door and hold hard-point structure are structural load paths (PRA/structural substantiation), not functional-FHA items, so only the access/restraint BEHAVIOURS are authored as functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants structural integrity captured functionally it would move to structural analysis rather than the FHA, changing nothing in this decomposition but affecting downstream tracing.
assumptions.usedFor: 'Provide nose loading access and pressure boundary closure' and 'Restrain payload' sub-functions

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.rationale: §5.7.3 and §5.8.3 explicitly call the door and hard points structure with no functional redundancy, but the systems also perform access/latching/restraint behaviours; the FUNCTION-vs-STRUCTURE rule forces separating them.

assumptions.text: Decomposition granularity was set one level below each aircraft function at the point where the SDD shows independent means/channels/surfaces (e.g. roll/pitch/yaw/high-lift as separate sub-functions).
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants a coarser or finer level the sub-function count changes; merged siblings would lose independence resolution and finer splits would introduce implementation detail.
assumptions.usedFor: All sub-function rows under Control aircraft trajectory, Support and control aircraft on ground, and Protect against ice accretion

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes redundancy and separation but does not enumerate functions (App A), so the split point had to be judged from where independent failure is documented.

assumptions.text: No aircraft-level MAC rule is frozen, so the Total/Partial split for these functions is read conservatively pending a defined minimum acceptable configuration.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a MAC rule is later defined, some conditions now split Total/Partial would move across the line, changing which capability phrase carries the condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001…SF-005 Total loss and Partial loss cells

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states configuration and gear/bogie count are preliminary and not frozen, so the line between within-MAC and outside-MAC cannot yet be fixed.

assumptions.text: Indication and mitigation detail is left empty because the AFHA effects that would substantiate detection sufficiency do not yet exist in the model.
assumptions.ifWrong: If effects and detection means are established, the indication/mitigation fields would be populated rather than left amber.
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM feeds the AFHA; effects/detection sufficiency are downstream outputs not yet present, so those fields cannot be grounded.

assumptions.text: The crew-unaware roll and thrust malfunction rows assume some erroneous/uncommanded behaviour can develop below the annunciation thresholds described in the SDD.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all such behaviour is intrinsically annunciated, the crew-Unaware rows for SF-001, SF-004 and SF-005 would collapse into the Aware rows.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 Unaware, SF-004 Unaware, SF-005 Unaware rows

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: Awareness-dismissal reasoning is filed here, not in a matrix cell; the SDD lists discretes/annunciations but not their detection coverage.

assumptions.text: Erroneous and uncommanded pitch/yaw behaviour can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying a distinct crew-Unaware row for those axes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all pitch/yaw malfunctions are intrinsically annunciated, the Unaware rows for SF-006 and SF-007 collapse into the Aware rows.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 Unaware row, SF-007 Unaware row

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes control architecture and degraded-law annunciation but does not state detection thresholds for slow or small erroneous surface motion, so the undetectable variant cannot be dismissed.

assumptions.text: High-lift asymmetry can be arrested by the asymmetry brakes and annunciated, but a below-threshold asymmetry variant cannot yet be excluded pending detection-coverage substantiation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry detection covers all credible cases, the SF-008 Unaware row is removed.

citations.quote: a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry brakes at each section but gives no detection threshold, so a small undetected asymmetry cannot be dismissed for the whole function.

assumptions.text: Loss of downlock indication is a distinct un-annunciated failure condition separable from loss of the gear function itself.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dual dissimilar sensing makes loss of both indications non-credible for the FCIM, the SF-009 Unaware row is removed.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.rationale: AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 treats loss of a failure annunciation as a failure condition in its own right; the SDD provides dual downlock sensing but the loss-of-indication case must be carried.

assumptions.text: Brake anti-skid and temperature monitoring may not detect a slowly developing per-wheel-pair asymmetry, so an undetected deceleration-asymmetry variant is carried.
assumptions.ifWrong: If monitoring covers all credible asymmetry, the SF-010 Unaware row is removed.

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes continuous brake-temperature monitoring and per-wheel-pair anti-skid but no coverage statement for latent asymmetry, so the undetected case cannot be dismissed.

assumptions.text: Ground directional control failures that develop erroneously below a heading-deviation threshold can occur without an immediate crew cue, so the SF-011 erroneous-response condition carries its own crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any erroneous ground-steering onset is intrinsically evident, the SF-011 Unaware row collapses and only the Aware row remains.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-011 Unaware row (Erroneous response to ground directional command)

citations.quote: Nose wheel steering is hydraulic, commanded from tillers and rudder pedals

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives ground directional control as a function but does not describe a dedicated failure annunciation, so the undetected-onset case cannot be dismissed.

assumptions.text: Nose door lock status is continuously annunciated, so an inadvertent loss of closure is normally crew-Aware, but an erroneous lock indication showing locked when unlocked defeats that cue and keeps its own crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the indication cannot fail misleadingly, the SF-012 Unaware misleading-indication row is removed and only the annunciated Aware conditions remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware row (Undetected loss of pressure boundary closure; Erroneous lock status indication)

citations.quote: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states lock status is displayed at all times; the failure of that indication itself is the undetectable case that must be retained.

assumptions.text: Payload restraint tension is monitored by a single instrumented loop, so a restraint loss coincident with loss of that loop can go undetected, justifying the SF-013 crew-Unaware conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If monitoring coverage is complete and non-single-point, the SF-013 Unaware row is removed and restraint loss is Aware only.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-013 Unaware row (Undetected loss / Undetected partial loss of payload restraint)

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the tension monitoring loop as a single instrumented loop with recorded coverage limits, so undetected coverage gaps cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: Cabin altitude is reported to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic, so a slow erroneous pressure schedule can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying the SF-015 crew-Unaware conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If cabin-altitude alerting reliably annunciates any off-schedule condition, the SF-015 Unaware row collapses to Aware only.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015 Unaware row (Erroneous cabin pressure control; Undetected cabin pressure change)

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms cabin-altitude signalling but does not establish a detection threshold, so a slow undetected drift cannot be dismissed.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight-deck conditioning (e.g. off-nominal temperature/flow) may not be self-evident until distress develops, so the SF-014 erroneous-conditioning condition retains a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If conditioning faults are annunciated or intrinsically evident, the SF-014 Unaware row is removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014 Unaware row (Erroneous flight deck air conditioning)

citations.quote: conditions and distributes air to the flight deck and the hold

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes conditioning function and status output but no dedicated conditioning-fault annunciation, so an undetected erroneous state cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: The crew-unaware variant of SF-016 (ice protection) is inapplicable at aircraft-function level because ice protection status and lost-zone loss are annunciated, so no separate Unaware row is emitted for that function.
assumptions.ifWrong: An SF-016 crew-Unaware row would be added carrying an undetected loss-of-protection condition, changing the awareness split for that function.

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states lost zones are annunciated and status is shown, but does not confirm every degradation mode is annunciated; only a single Aware row was groundable.

assumptions.text: Icing detection and probe heating can fail without an intrinsic self-evident cue before accretion begins, so SF-017 carries a distinct crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all such failures are annunciated the SF-017 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes elements as individually monitored but does not confirm the monitoring covers every silent-failure mode before ice accretes.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/navigation data can develop below the three-way ADIRU cross-comparison threshold and reach the crew undetected, justifying an SF-018 crew-Unaware malfunction row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If cross-comparison detects all erroneous data the SF-018 Unaware row is removed and the malfunction is fully Aware.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: Three reference units support comparison monitoring, but the SDD does not state the comparison thresholds, so slow common-mode drift below them cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: Loss of the crew-alerting function is itself a failure condition and can be latent, so SF-019 carries a crew-Unaware total-loss row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a monitor annunciates total loss of alerting the SF-019 Unaware row becomes Aware.

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 treats loss of annunciation as a failure condition in its own right; the SDD does not confirm the alerting channels self-monitor for total loss.

assumptions.text: A fire or overheat can be present while detection has silently failed, so SF-020 carries a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection-system loss is annunciated the SF-020 Unaware row folds into the Aware row.

citations.quote: degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.rationale: AND logic degrading to single-loop covers partial loss detection, but the SDD does not confirm total dual-loop loss is itself annunciated before a fire occurs.

assumptions.text: Fire extinguishing availability (charged bottles, valid discharge path) can degrade latently between the crew's demand and the moment of use, so an undetected-loss variant is retained for SF-021.
assumptions.ifWrong: If bottle availability is continuously monitored and annunciated, the SF-021 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Unaware row (Undetected loss of fire extinguishing availability)

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states extinguishing is a crew action through the fire handles but does not describe continuous bottle-availability monitoring, so the undetected variant cannot be dismissed.

assumptions.text: A partial (single-cylinder) loss of crew oxygen with the crossover still capable of supplying reduced reserve stays within the required duration, so total and partial loss are distinct SF-022 conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single cylinder cannot meet the required diversion duration, the partial-loss condition merges into total loss.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022 Aware row (Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply)

citations.quote: either being capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states either cylinder can supply the crew at reduced reserve, which distinguishes a partial from a total loss, but the reserve adequacy is not quantified here.

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen supply loss can occur below the crew's detection threshold when the demand event has not yet begun (system is passive in normal flight), so an undetected variant is retained for SF-022.
assumptions.ifWrong: If low-pressure alerting reliably detects any depletion, the SF-022 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022 Unaware row (Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply)

citations.quote: The system is passive in normal flight and its only routine interaction is the pre-flight pressure check

assumptions.rationale: The SDD shows the system is passive with only a routine pre-flight pressure check and continuous pressure display; whether that display alerts on slow depletion is not stated.

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1, so a single-engine partial thrust loss is within the design dispatch case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If one-engine-out continuation is not assured, SF-001-PL and SF-001-M would rise toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: The aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.rationale: The FHA has no design data of its own; the one-engine-out continuation case comes only from the SDD and sets whether partial/asymmetric thrust loss is Major rather than Hazardous.

assumptions.text: The asymmetric-thrust case is a single-engine asymmetry within the rudder authority the flight-control sizing provides at the 28 m outboard moment arm.
assumptions.ifWrong: An asymmetry beyond the sized case, or a second same-side engine loss, would reduce control margins and could move SF-001-M to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine 28 m case as the directional-control sizing case but does not state the maximum credible asymmetry or a runaway-thrust case.

assumptions.text: The certified landing distance on the semi-prepared surface is achievable on wheel braking alone, with reverse thrust credited as margin rather than as a required means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the requirement cannot be met without reverse on a degraded strip, SF-002-TL rises toward Hazardous (overrun risk).

citations.quote: The landing distance requirement is 1,800 m (6,000 ft) on such a surface. Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout but does not state whether that rollout assumes reverse thrust.

assumptions.text: An undetected partial thrust loss is bounded at single-engine scale and its end effect leaves the crew able to reach a suitable aerodrome once inferred.
assumptions.ifWrong: A larger undetected loss combined with a non-escapable phase could push the end state beyond Major.

citations.quote: engine parameter data to the avionics display system

assumptions.rationale: The SDD shows engine parameter data to the displays but no coverage/threshold data on the smallest undetectable thrust decrement.

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is credited only as a supplementary ground-deceleration means and the wheel-brake system alone satisfies the 1,800 m landing requirement.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-PL rises from Minor toward Major if reverse is credited in the certified landing distance on the semi-prepared surface.

citations.quote: Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the landing margin (1,080 m predicted vs 1,800 m required) and describes dual-hydraulic accumulator-backed braking, but does not state whether reverse thrust is credited in the certified landing distance.

assumptions.text: The classifying case for inadvertent reverse thrust is an in-flight deployment producing thrust opposite to command, notwithstanding the WOW + radio-altimeter inhibits and mechanical sleeve lock.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no credible path defeats all in-flight inhibits, the classifying case becomes an on-ground inadvertent deployment during rollout and SF-002-M drops below Hazardous.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight inhibits and a mechanical lock but does not enumerate the deployment paths that could defeat them, so the more severe in-flight case is taken as the function's classifying condition.

assumptions.text: An undetected reverse asymmetry during landing rollout produces a controllable ground directional excursion that the crew arrests with steering and asymmetric braking, not a departure from the semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the asymmetry drives an unrecoverable lateral departure from the strip, SF-002-M2 rises above Major.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not state reverser asymmetry magnitude, the deceleration split between inboard engines, or the runway lateral margin on the semi-prepared strip.

assumptions.text: A partial loss of fuel feed starves a bounded subset of the four engines (not all four) and the crew can reconfigure cross-feed, boost pumps and the gravity path to sustain flight to a suitable aerodrome.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single partial-feed failure (e.g. gallery loss with concurrent tank isolation) can starve all engines, SF-003-PL escalates toward the Catastrophic total-loss case.

citations.quote: Cross-feed is by a single gallery running spanwise through the wing box

assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not bound how many engines a partial feed failure can starve, and the single spanwise cross-feed gallery is the only cross-side path whose loss could expand starvation toward the total case.

assumptions.text: An erroneous fuel feed pressure is contained to the affected engine and does not propagate to multiple engines through the cross-feed gallery.
assumptions.ifWrong: If erroneous feed pressure can affect multiple engines simultaneously, SF-003-M rises above Major toward Hazardous or Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Cross-feed is by a single gallery running spanwise through the wing box with four isolation valves, permitting any tank to feed any engine.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes lost/low feed and FADEC protection but does not state the engine or cross-feed response to erroneous (mis-scheduled) feed pressure.

assumptions.text: The crew can detect and arrest an erroneous fuel distribution before the 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit or an uncontrollable CG is reached, using the 1,200 kg annunciation and manual cross-feed/isolation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the erroneous drive can exceed the structural limit or reach an uncontrollable CG faster than crew action, SF-004-M rises from Hazardous to Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg and is limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the annunciation and structural limit but not the transfer rate, CG authority, or the time available for crew arrest.

assumptions.text: The 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit bounds an undetected fuel imbalance short of a hazardous wing-bending exceedance before the crew recognises the asymmetry.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected imbalance can reach a structural exceedance before recognition, SF-004-M2 moves from Major to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M2 — Undetected erroneous fuel distribution — imbalance

citations.quote: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg and is limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the annunciation and structural limits but gives no bending analysis or time-to-limit, which the SF-004-M2 class turns on once the annunciation is lost.

assumptions.text: The three dissimilar voting flight control computers bound an erroneous or uncommanded roll input to a transient the crew can detect and arrest without loss of control.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an unbounded roll hardover is credible at low altitude, SF-005-M and SF-005-M2 move from Major to Hazardous or Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-M — Erroneous roll response to crew command; SF-005-M2 — Uncommanded roll motion

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the voting architecture but does not quantify command-monitoring coverage or the maximum credible surface runaway, which the SF-005-M and -M2 classes depend on.

assumptions.text: After a partial loss of pitch control authority the residual authority leaves the aircraft controllable at a large margin reduction rather than uncontrollable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If residual pitch authority is insufficient to keep the aircraft controllable, SF-006-PL moves from Hazardous to Catastrophic (hull loss on all three axes).
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-PL — Partial loss of pitch control authority
assumptions.rationale: The aircraft function objective states pitch control but does not quantify the authority remaining after a partial loss, and no fault tree or architecture count is available at aircraft level.

assumptions.text: For an erroneous pitch response the crew detect the malfunction and successfully arrest it before loss of control in every flight phase.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection or response time is inadequate in a critical phase, SF-006-M moves from Hazardous to Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-M — Erroneous pitch response to crew command
assumptions.rationale: No human-factors detection-and-response record for pitch-response malfunctions was provided, so the credited crew recovery could not be grounded from the inputs.

assumptions.text: The undetected roll malfunctions have no crew annunciation, so the crew take no corrective action and the condition develops to loss of control.
assumptions.ifWrong: If some independent cue or annunciation exists that would prompt correction, these conditions could be less severe than Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-M3 — Undetected erroneous roll response to crew command; SF-005-M4 — Undetected uncommanded roll motion
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM rows are the crew-unaware variants (SF-005-M3/M4); the unaware case assumes the crew continue duties normally and take no action, which the provided context does not contradict.

assumptions.text: An uncommanded or undetected-erroneous pitch excursion is, in the worst case, not always arrestable by the fly-by-wire law or the mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion before departure from controlled flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a survivable arrest is always credited, SF-006-M2/M3/M4 drop from Catastrophic to Hazardous or Major.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the reversion path and voting architecture but gives no handling/failure-transient data on the recoverable envelope of an uncommanded runaway.

assumptions.text: Following total loss of yaw control the aircraft cannot maintain a survivable heading against the sizing asymmetry case and the flight is not recoverable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If residual directional control (e.g. differential thrust) is credited as survivable, SF-007-TL could reduce to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names outboard-engine asymmetry as the directional-control sizing case but does not state whether any survivable control exists with all yaw authority lost.

assumptions.text: A significant partial loss of pitch authority is survivable short of loss of control when encountered undetected.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected partial loss can reach an unrecoverable authority shortfall, SF-006-PL2 rises above Major.

citations.quote: the elevators from A and C

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives dual actuation of the elevators (HYD A and C) but no degraded pitch-handling margin, so the surviving authority is assumed adequate.

assumptions.text: The split-rudder architecture retains sufficient directional authority after a single rudder segment/supply loss to cover the V1 outboard-engine-out with maximum blade payload, so partial loss is a controllable degradation.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-007-PL and SF-007-PL2 move from Major/Hazardous toward Hazardous/Catastrophic if the residual authority does not cover the sizing demand.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of yaw control authority; Undetected partial loss of yaw control authority

citations.quote: a single rudder supply loss must still leave sufficient authority

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states this case sizes the rudder but does not quantify the residual margin after a single supply loss, which is what separates Major from Hazardous for the partial-loss rows.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or uncommanded yaw input is bounded and arrestable by crew action (not a full-authority, uncountered hardover) so the malfunction rows are credited as recoverable rather than as immediate loss of control.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-007-M, SF-007-M2 and SF-007-M3 escalate from Hazardous to Catastrophic if the erroneous/uncommanded motion is a rapid full-authority excursion the crew cannot arrest.
assumptions.usedFor: Erroneous yaw response to crew command; Uncommanded yaw motion; Undetected erroneous yaw response to crew command

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes three dissimilar voting FCCs and split-segment actuation but gives no failure-transient magnitude or rate, which is the fact that decides Hazardous versus Catastrophic.

assumptions.text: The undetected variants correctly credit loss of the yaw asymmetry/jam annunciation, leaving the crew to rely on direct aircraft motion cues only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If annunciation is in fact retained, SF-007-PL2 and SF-007-M3 collapse into their aware counterparts and their standalone Hazardous classification is unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected partial loss of yaw control authority; Undetected erroneous yaw response to crew command

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM lists undetected rows for SF-007; classifying them requires assuming the alerting path is lost, per the AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 un-annunciated combination rule.

assumptions.text: An uncommanded, unannunciated yaw input builds into a divergent sideslip/heading excursion the crew cannot promptly attribute and counter, especially near the ground.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the input is slow, self-limiting or readily countered, SF-007-M4 drops from Hazardous (HAZ-1) toward Major.

citations.quote: yaw by a split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes yaw architecture but gives no magnitude, divergence rate, or crew time-to-detect for an undetected uncommanded yaw source.

assumptions.text: A flapless/reduced-flap landing at 318,000 kg maximum landing weight remains achievable within the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing-distance requirement, at reduced margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the elevated approach speed exceeds the strip's landing-distance capability at max landing weight, SF-008-TL (and possibly SF-008-PL) rises toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL Total loss of high-lift; SF-008-PL Partial loss of high-lift

citations.quote: The landing distance requirement is 1,800 m (6,000 ft) on such a surface.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the landing-distance requirement and predicted normal rollout but gives no flapless/degraded-high-lift landing performance.

assumptions.text: The per-section asymmetry brakes bound a high-lift mismatch, but a credible worst-case asymmetry can still develop near the ground before the brakes arrest it, producing a roll/yaw the crew must counter with limited margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the brakes bound the asymmetry to a readily-countered level, SF-008-M drops from Hazardous (HAZ-1) to Major.

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry brakes at each section but does not state the residual asymmetry magnitude after brake action or its handling consequence.

assumptions.text: Uncommanded high-lift motion is annunciated and the crew arrest it before a high-speed airload exceedance or a low-speed near-ground lift loss departs controlled flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an uncommanded near-ground retraction departs controlled flight before crew action, SF-008-M2 rises from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists high-lift position and asymmetry/jam discretes as FCS outputs but gives no timing or consequence for an uncommanded motion event.

assumptions.text: For undetected partial high-lift loss, the eroded approach/landing margin without a crew speed correction is a moderate (not large) degradation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected loss is large and flown to the flare, SF-008-PL2 could rise from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the high-lift architecture but gives no annunciation coverage or handling data for a degraded/undetected high-lift configuration.

assumptions.text: The high-lift asymmetry brakes do not fully arrest an undetected asymmetry before it produces a large low-altitude rolling moment.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the asymmetry brakes reliably arrest the asymmetry, SF-008-M3 drops below Hazardous.

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names asymmetry brakes at each section but gives no coverage or effectiveness data for the undetected-asymmetry case.

assumptions.text: Partial loss of ground load support leaves a residual footprint that still permits a landing without collapse on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the residual configuration cannot support a survivable landing, SF-009-PL rises from Major toward Hazardous or Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009-PL (Partial loss of ground load support)

citations.quote: six three-wheel main bogies, three per side

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the bogie count but no substantiation of degraded-gear flotation/load-spreading on the semi-prepared surface.

assumptions.text: Failure to extend and lock for landing is credited only when the free-fall alternate extension has also failed, leaving no locked support path at touchdown.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the free-fall alternate remains available, SF-009-M is not Catastrophic — it reduces to a recoverable extension abnormal.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009-M (Failure to extend and lock for landing)

citations.quote: Uplocks and downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released

assumptions.rationale: The SDD provides a free-fall alternate independent of hydraulic pressure; the failure condition as stated must be the full loss for the Catastrophic end state to hold.

assumptions.text: The undetected loss in SF-009-M2 is of downlock indication only, with the second independent proximity circuit and any monitor still able to reveal a gear-not-locked state.
assumptions.ifWrong: If total sensing loss is undetected and can mask a gear-not-locked landing, SF-009-M2 combines with SF-009 loss-of-extend and must meet the un-annunciated objective, raising the effective classification.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two independent proximity circuits but does not say whether a total loss of both sensing paths is itself detected, which decides whether the annunciation loss can coincide undetected with an unsafe gear state.

assumptions.text: Residual reverse thrust and accumulator-supported braking arrest the total-loss-of-deceleration case short of a hull-loss overrun on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust and accumulator braking cannot arrest the aircraft within the available surface, SF-010-TL becomes a hull-loss overrun and the classification rises toward Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Brake accumulator capacity is sized to six full brake applications with all three systems lost.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m rollout and states accumulator capacity for six applications, but does not present stopping-performance analysis for the all-braking-lost case.

assumptions.text: Partial loss of deceleration leaves sufficient braking to stop within the 1,800 m available given the ~1,080 m nominal rollout.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the degradation is severe enough to threaten the overrun margin, SF-010-PL rises from Major toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: landing distance requirement of 1,800 m ... predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual-supply plus accumulator braking but gives no degraded-case stopping distance, so the surviving margin is assumed rather than shown.

assumptions.text: The crew can detect and counter braking asymmetry with tiller/pedal steering and rudder before the aircraft departs the semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a large asymmetry is unrecoverable at speed on the semi-prepared surface, SF-010-M rises from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD notes anti-skid per wheel pair and steering means but provides no directional-control analysis of the asymmetric-braking excursion on the narrow surface.

assumptions.text: Aerodynamic rudder and differential (asymmetric) braking provide an independent ground directional-control alternate to nose-wheel steering.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no independent directional alternate remains after steering loss, SF-011-TL and SF-011-M escalate toward Catastrophic (potential loss of the aircraft in a runway excursion).

citations.quote: provides braking and directional control on the ground

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists steering, braking and rudder but does not state whether they form an independent directional alternate after a steering loss; the Hazardous (not Catastrophic) call for SF-011-TL and SF-011-M leans on that alternate.

assumptions.text: The ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout absorbs a partial (not total) deceleration loss without overrun.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected shortfall exceeds the margin, SF-010-PL2 escalates to Hazardous (overrun of the semi-prepared strip).

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the requirement and predicted rollout but no braking-degradation curve, so the escalation threshold for a partial loss is not stated; the Major call for SF-010-PL2 rests on the margin absorbing the shortfall.

assumptions.text: The destination semi-prepared strip is narrow with limited lateral run-off, so a lateral excursion is a credible and adverse ground outcome.
assumptions.ifWrong: If ample lateral run-off exists, the occupant/aircraft consequence of an excursion is milder and SF-011-TL/M and SF-010-M3 may reduce toward Major.

citations.quote: a semi-prepared strip constructed for the project and not maintained to commercial

assumptions.rationale: Strip width, run-off and obstacle environment are not given; the severity of the directional-control and asymmetric-braking rows depends on the consequence of leaving the prepared surface.

assumptions.text: An erroneous ground steering input occurs at a ground speed and lateral margin where an aware crew can detect and arrest the deviation on the surface.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-011-M2 rises from Major to Hazardous if the deviation cannot be arrested within available width.

citations.quote: provides braking and directional control on the ground

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes ground directional control but does not state achievable ground speed at the point of the erroneous command or the excursion margin on the semi-prepared strip.

assumptions.text: A genuinely crew-unaware erroneous ground steering input exists (no immediate heading/yaw cue) and the uncorrected excursion carries non-benign energy.
assumptions.ifWrong: If steering errors are always accompanied by detectable cues the unaware case is inapplicable; if excursion energy is low SF-011-M3 falls to Major.

citations.quote: Nose wheel steering is hydraulic, commanded from tillers and rudder pedals

assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not state steering-fault annunciation coverage or whether heading/side-force cues always accompany an erroneous input.

assumptions.text: The take-off configuration monitor and displayed lock status reliably prevent dispatch with the visor pressure boundary not made.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dispatch with the boundary not made were possible, SF-012-TL would carry an in-flight pressure-boundary/structural consequence of far higher severity than No Safety Effect.

citations.quote: included in the take-off configuration check

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states lock status is displayed and in the take-off configuration check but does not state the monitor's integrity.

assumptions.text: An inadvertent in-flight loss of the nose visor pressure boundary is physically credible despite the in-flight inoperability and pressure interlock defences.
assumptions.ifWrong: If in-flight unlock is architecturally precluded, SF-012-M is a very-low-probability condition dispositioned by interlock/structural substantiation rather than a live Catastrophic FHA driver.

citations.quote: a pressure interlock vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes an interlock requiring residual differential below 0.1 psi and states the door cannot be operated in flight; whether inadvertent in-flight loss remains credible is not settled.

assumptions.text: The nose door's dual dissimilar lock sensing and pressure interlock do not guarantee that a false-secure LOCKED indication is contradicted before take-off, so the erroneous indication can defeat the configuration check.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-012-M2 and SF-012-M3 would drop from Hazardous to Major (a detected/arrested mis-indication is a workload item, not a defeated boundary defence).

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits: a proximity sensing harness

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual dissimilar sensing and a pressure interlock but does not state whether they force disagreement to the crew in the mis-indication case.

assumptions.text: Undetected loss of the nose-door pressure-boundary closure produces a large reduction in structural safety margins at the preliminary hold differential.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-012-PL2 could fall to Major if the low differential and independent relief make an undetected boundary loss non-critical.

citations.quote: Hold pressurisation Low differential, ≈ 8,800 m hold altitude equivalent (preliminary)

assumptions.rationale: The hold differential is preliminary and the structural consequence of an undetected boundary loss is not quantified in the SDD.

assumptions.text: An in-flight total loss of restraint of the 72.6 t single blade is not recoverable by crew action, since there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.
assumptions.ifWrong: If some means limited blade travel to a recoverable CG range, SF-013-TL could fall below Catastrophic.

citations.quote: In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight the crew has indication only with no in-flight adjustment, and does not describe any means to arrest a shifted payload.

assumptions.text: An undetected single or adjacent strap-tension loss on SF-013 remains within the sized "neighbours carry the load" redundancy and does not cascade to an uncontrollable CG excursion.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-013-PL2 rises from Major toward Hazardous, and SF-013-TL2 would be classifiable (likely Catastrophic) rather than left blank.

citations.quote: load paths sized such that the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states single-strap loss is carried by neighbours but gives no restraint loads or CG-migration case, so the boundary between Major partial loss and a hull-threatening excursion is not established.

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen is available and independent of the flight-deck air-supply loss, and the emergency-descent diversion time from FL260 is within crew oxygen endurance.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-014-TL rises from Major to Hazardous if oxygen shares a common cause with the air-supply loss or diversion time exceeds oxygen reserve.

citations.quote: The system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD credits crew oxygen for loss of pressurisation and the ensuing descent/diversion but provides no endurance figure or common-cause exclusion versus ECS.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight-deck conditioning is detectable and recoverable by the crew via manual mode / alternate pack before it impairs crew task performance.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-014-M rises from Major toward Hazardous if the erroneous state is undetectable or extreme enough to impair the crew before recovery.

citations.quote: Pressurisation is fully automatic with a manual mode available.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD provides manual mode but no bound on how extreme an erroneous thermal/flow state can become, so crew recoverability is assumed rather than grounded.

assumptions.text: The flight deck is the only occupied pressurised space in flight and the hold carries no occupants.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold or any other space is occupied in flight the occupant axis on SF-014-PL2, SF-015-TL, SF-015-PL and SF-015-M could rise from none, raising several classes.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014-PL2, SF-014-M2, SF-015-TL, SF-015-PL, SF-015-M occupant axes

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant axis needs to know who is aboard the pressurised volumes; the SDD states the hold is unoccupied and the crew are the only occupants.

assumptions.text: Quick-donning crew oxygen and cabin-altitude alerting are available and are credited for detection and protection in a depressurisation from up to FL260.
assumptions.ifWrong: If time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260 is shorter than mask-don time, the crew axis on SF-015-TL and SF-015-M reaches incapacitation and those rows become Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015-TL and SF-015-M crew axis and Hazardous classification

citations.quote: four quick-donning full-face masks with integral smoke goggles and demand regulators

assumptions.rationale: The cabin-pressure severity turns on whether the crew can detect and don oxygen before incapacitation; the SDD describes quick-donning masks and cabin-altitude signalling but no timing data is given.

assumptions.text: Independent positive/negative mechanical relief valves bound the achievable differential/cabin-altitude excursion for control-system and erroneous-command failures.
assumptions.ifWrong: If relief authority cannot bound an erroneous-command excursion, SF-015-TL and SF-015-M could progress to hull-loss-level structural or crew outcomes and become Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015-TL and SF-015-M aircraft axis and Hazardous classification

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.rationale: Crediting a Hazardous rather than Catastrophic class for total-loss and erroneous control relies on relief limiting the excursion; the SDD states relief is independent but gives no authority limits.

assumptions.text: The flight crew have quick-donning oxygen and no passengers or hold occupants are exposed, so every SF-015 pressurisation condition lands only on the two-to-four flight crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant were carried in a pressurised occupied volume, the occupant axis on SF-015-M2/M3/M4 would rise and could drive the class above the crew axis.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015-M2, SF-015-M3, SF-015-M4 occupant axis (effPaxLevel none or slight inconvenience)

citations.quote: There is no passenger oxygen: the hold is not occupied in flight.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the hold is unoccupied and there is no passenger oxygen, but the occupant-effect axis must be grounded to classify the pressurisation rows.

assumptions.text: At FL260 with the preliminary low hold/cabin differential the crew can detect a cabin-pressure excursion and don oxygen before it becomes physiologically incapacitating, but an UNDETECTED excursion can develop far enough to distress the crew before natural cues appear.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the low differential cannot produce a physiologically significant excursion, SF-015-M4 drops to Major; if it can incapacitate the aware crew before revert, SF-015-M2/M3 rise to Hazardous.

citations.quote: the hold is pressurised to a low differential only, currently sized to approximately 8,800 m hold altitude equivalent

assumptions.rationale: The maximum cabin altitude reachable and the time-to-symptom margin are not quantified; the split between Major (aware) and Hazardous (unaware) turns on them.

assumptions.text: Loss of ice-protection results in a large (total loss) or significant (partial loss) reduction in safety margins in the icing envelope rather than an unrecoverable handling loss, given the crew can exit icing on annunciation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If unprotected accretion could preclude continued safe flight, SF-016-TL moves to Catastrophic; if partial loss removed a critical surface's only protection, SF-016-PL moves to Hazardous.

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis

assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not quantify the handling/performance degradation from unprotected ice accretion, which sets the aircraft axis for SF-016-TL/PL.

assumptions.text: The flight crew reliably recognise icing conditions and select ice protection manually when automatic detection or scheduling is degraded or lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manual recognition cannot be credited, Total loss of icing detection and the false-negative case of Erroneous icing detection rise from Minor/Major toward Hazardous per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-TL (Total loss of icing detection), SF-017-M (Erroneous icing detection)

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually at any time.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is advisory with a manual path but does not quantify crew recognition of icing without the detectors, which the SF-017-TL and SF-017-M classes depend on.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or lost protection schedule that leaves a surface or probe unheated in icing is annunciated to the crew or otherwise detectable in time to reselect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an unprotected surface or probe in icing is not annunciated, Erroneous ice protection scheduling and Partial loss of probe protection rise from Major toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016-M2 (Erroneous ice protection scheduling), SF-017-PL (Partial loss of probe protection)

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms electrical zone loss is annunciated but does not confirm annunciation of an erroneous bleed-side schedule or of a probe left unheated, which the SF-016-M2 and SF-017-PL classes depend on.

assumptions.text: Individual probe protection loss affects a single air-data source at a time and is isolable against the three independent air-data reference units.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common route or supply removes protection from multiple air-data sources simultaneously in icing, Partial loss of probe protection rises from Major toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states probes are monitored individually and three ADIRUs exist but does not map which probes share a heater route or electrical source, which the SF-017-PL isolation-based Major class depends on.

assumptions.text: Independent icing cues remain available to the crew after undetected loss of the ice detectors, so accretion is eventually recognised.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no independent recognition means exists, SF-017-TL2 escalates toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-TL2 — Undetected loss of icing detection

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually at any time.
