assumptions.rationale: The SDD says detection is advisory with manual activation but does not quantify how reliably the crew recognises icing without the detector, which sets Major vs Hazardous.

assumptions.text: Probe heating is individually monitored, so undetected loss is limited and air-data reversion to standby remains available.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a broad probe-heat loss can go undetected and corrupt all air data, SF-017-M2 escalates toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-M2 — Undetected loss of probe protection

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states probes are monitored individually, which conflicts with an 'undetected' loss; the extent of undetectable loss governs the class.

assumptions.text: The independent standby instrument is adequate for continued flight and landing across the relevant phases after total loss of primary flight/nav data.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby is inadequate in the driving phases/conditions, SF-018-TL rises toward Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL — Total loss of flight and navigation data

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts the standby shares nothing with the primaries but does not establish its sufficiency envelope; this credit holds the class at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.

assumptions.text: The triple dissimilar reference units and independent standby detect and isolate a single erroneous data source before the crew commits an unrecoverable action.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single misleading source can defeat the cross-check undetected in a critical phase, SF-018-M rises toward Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M — Erroneous flight and navigation data

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists three reference units and an independent standby but does not state the voting/monitoring that arrests a misleading source; the credit holds SF-018-M at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic.

assumptions.text: The flight crew perform a credited, timely cross-check of primary flight/navigation data against the independent standby instrument, but this is not shown reliably to catch undetected erroneous data before loss of control.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a timely standby cross-check IS substantiated as reliable, the aircraft effect of SF-018-M2 reduces below hull loss and the severity could fall from Catastrophic to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected erroneous flight and navigation data

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes an independent standby instrument but states no crew procedure or detection timing for catching erroneous-but-valid-looking primary data; the class hinges on whether that cross-check is credited.

assumptions.text: The credited partial loss of crew alerting removes only a non-safety-critical subset of alerts, leaving the alerting of the most severe failure conditions intact.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a partial loss can remove an alert whose absence is itself Major under §5.4.2, SF-019-PL is Major rather than Minor.

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives two independent alerting channels but does not scope which alerts survive a representative partial degradation, so the extent of the partial loss is undefined.

assumptions.text: A single erroneous alert does not by itself command the crew into an irreversible incorrect procedure (e.g. shutting down a needed system) with no recovery.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a false alert can drive an irreversible unsafe crew action, SF-019-M rises from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: The SDD couples alerts to associated procedures but does not identify the worst-case procedure an erroneous alert could invoke, which sets whether the effect stops at Major or reaches Hazardous.

assumptions.text: The standalone undetected loss of crew alerting, un-combined with any concurrent annunciated failure, is classified Major per the §5.4.2 default.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a specific concurrent failure whose un-annunciated effect is Hazardous is credited, the SF-019-TL2 combination severity rises to Hazardous.
assumptions.rationale: The AFHA gives no probability for a coincident second failure and no combination table, so the standalone class must be taken from the loss-of-annunciation default rule.

assumptions.text: An undetected fire in a monitored fire zone (nacelle, APU, bleed duct, gear bay, hold) leads to a large — not necessarily catastrophic — reduction in safety margins given the aircraft's segregation and extinguishing provisions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an undetected uncontained nacelle fire propagates to fuel or primary structure, SF-020-TL and SF-020-TL2 rise to Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-TL and SF-020-TL2 (total and undetected loss of fire and overheat detection)

citations.quote: Each engine nacelle and the APU compartment carry dual-loop continuous fire detection

assumptions.rationale: The AFHA does not credit the coincident fire probability or the propagation path into the detection-loss condition, so the credited end state of an undetected fire had to be judged.

assumptions.text: A single erroneous fire/overheat indication drives at most one engine shutdown and diversion on a four-engine aircraft that continues after loss of one engine.
assumptions.ifWrong: If erroneous detection triggers multiple simultaneous shutdowns or an in-flight bottle discharge into a live engine, SF-020-M rises to Hazardous.

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine

assumptions.rationale: The AFHA does not state how many simultaneous responses an erroneous detection can trigger, so the crew-response scope had to be assumed to classify SF-020-M.

assumptions.text: The partial loss of detection is annunciated (dual-loop degrading to single-loop is annunciated) and the retained zones include the higher-consequence engine and APU zones.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the partial loss removes all engine-nacelle detection while retaining only hold smoke detection, or is unannunciated, SF-020-PL rises toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-PL (Partial loss of fire and overheat detection)

citations.quote: degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.rationale: The AFHA does not fix which zones are lost in the partial case, so the annunciation and retained-coverage assumptions had to be made to classify SF-020-PL.

assumptions.text: An unsuppressed engine-nacelle or APU fire in this configuration can be contained by crew isolation and land the aircraft without propagating to hull loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-021-TL and SF-021-TL2 rise from Hazardous (HAZ-1) to Catastrophic (CAT-1), carrying crew and occupant axes to their top step.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021-TL (Total loss of fire extinguishing), SF-021-TL2 (Undetected loss of fire extinguishing availability)

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives detection and two-bottle cross-plumbed suppression but no fire-containment or burn-through substantiation, so the end effect of an unsuppressed fire is not fixed by the provided material.

assumptions.text: The crew can complete an emergency descent to a breathable altitude from FL260 before hypoxia or smoke incapacitates them when no breathing oxygen is available.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-022-TL rises from Hazardous (HAZ-2) to Catastrophic (CAT-1) if crew incapacitation before reaching breathable altitude is credited.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-TL (Total loss of crew breathing oxygen supply)

citations.quote: The system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD sizes crew oxygen for the diversion time at max operating altitude but states neither that time nor the descent capability with oxygen absent, so the crew-incapacitation outcome is not settled.

assumptions.text: An undetected total loss of crew oxygen produces a survivable, workload-driven crew-incapacitation risk (Hazardous) rather than certain incapacitation before descent (Catastrophic).
assumptions.ifWrong: If TUC at the operative cabin altitude is too short for a descent without oxygen, SF-022-TL2 rises to Catastrophic (CAT-1) with the crew axis at fatalities or incapacitation.

citations.quote: The system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the maximum operating altitude and a preliminary hold differential but no time-of-useful-consciousness or diversion-time figure to settle whether the crew can descend before incapacitation with no supplemental oxygen.

assumptions.text: The flight deck cylinder-pressure indication and low-pressure alerting make a partial loss detectable, keeping SF-022-PL an aware condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If low-pressure alerting is not credited, a partial loss could become latent and its severity would be reassessed under the un-annunciated combination rule.

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item.

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM lists SF-022-PL only under the Aware row; the aware/unaware split for the partial case is inferred from the SDD indication description.

assumptions.text: HYD, EPS and EWS resource functions are traced only to the systems that consume them, not directly to the aircraft sub-functions those consumers deliver.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer wants resource-to-aircraft-function visibility, HYD would trace to SF-005..SF-012 and EPS broadly, and the interdependence columns widen.
assumptions.usedFor: Supply hydraulic motive power; Generate and distribute electrical power; Carry electrical power and signals

citations.quote: Three independent 3,000 psi hydraulic systems supply motive power to the flight control actuators

assumptions.rationale: The SDD routes roll/pitch/yaw/gear/door delivery through FCS/LDG/NZD, which consume HYD and EPS; the granularity rule bars collapsing an enabling resource into a consumer's aircraft-function trace.

assumptions.text: FADEC dual channels are countable configuration items at the level the MAC reasons over for each of the four engines.
assumptions.ifWrong: The eight FADEC-channel items collapse to four FADEC items (one per engine) or are dropped as sub-unit detail.
assumptions.usedFor: FADEC channel A/B items on engines 1–4 under Propulsion (PRP)

citations.quote: digital engine control with dual redundant channels and independent power feeds

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual redundant channels per engine but does not confirm the MAC counts channels rather than treating the FADEC as one unit per engine.

assumptions.text: The two alerting processing channels are countable configuration items distinct from the display processors.
assumptions.ifWrong: The two alerting-channel items are removed or merged into the display-processor items.
assumptions.usedFor: Alerting processing channel 1/2 items under Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI)

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names two independent alerting channels but does not say whether they are separate LRUs or logical partitions within the display processors.

assumptions.text: The four generators, APU generator, RAT emergency generator, TRUs, batteries and bleed sources belong to EPS/FUE/PRP resource systems not in the five requested and are therefore excluded here.
assumptions.ifWrong: Additional add_item actions are required once EPS/HYD/FUE/OXY systems are created in the project.
assumptions.usedFor: Scope boundary of this item list

citations.quote: Four engine-driven 150 kVA variable-frequency generators supply four main AC buses

assumptions.rationale: The task scoped the request to five function systems (PRP, ECS, IPS, AVI, FPR); EPS, HYD, FUE and OXY copies live under systems not present in the project state.

assumptions.text: Continued flight after loss of any ONE engine (not two) is the CSFL floor for forward thrust, applied symmetrically per side.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a two-engine-out case must be survivable, SF-001 minima and the per-side clause structure change.

citations.quote: continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the one-engine-out design case and that a second same-side engine loss is outside dispatch, but does not itself set the MAC floor.

assumptions.text: FCS, FUE, HYD, LDG, NZD, CRG and OXY redundant copies named in the SDD are the correct MAC members, pending creation of matching configuration items in the project.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the eventual item decomposition differs, every clause referencing a placeholder member must be re-pointed to real item ids.

citations.quote: Every primary surface is driven by at least two actuators supplied from different hydraulic systems

assumptions.rationale: The project item register lists countable copies only for PRP, ECS, IPS, AVI and FPR; the other systems hold no items, so members are placeholder names from the SDD text.

assumptions.text: The three flight control computers are arbitrated by 2-of-3 voting (two erroneous copies defeat the vote).
assumptions.ifWrong: If a monitored-pair or different voting scheme applies, the arbitration k on SF-005/006/007 changes and the malfunction lane derivation shifts.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three dissimilar computers vote on command but does not state the exact voting order (k).

assumptions.text: Ground reverse thrust is not required for continued safe flight and landing; the reverser clause is a conservative placeholder.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse is credited in the landing distance case, SF-002 minima and phase must be reconsidered.

citations.quote: the margin between those two numbers is the operating margin on which the braking and flotation design rests

assumptions.rationale: The SDD rests landing distance on braking margin, not reverse, and does not state a reverse-thrust minimum for CSFL.

assumptions.text: The MAC rule SF-001 requiring at least one of two item-pairs is met so long as sufficient engines remain to continue to a suitable aerodrome, so total loss = all thrust lost and partial loss = one or more but not all engines lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Total-vs-Partial boundary for forward thrust would move, reclassifying which asymmetric or multi-engine losses breach the MAC.

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.rationale: The MAC rule identifies items ITM-001..004 by placeholder id only; the SDD substantiates continuation on loss of one engine but the exact item-to-engine mapping is not given.

assumptions.text: Forward-thrust total loss and asymmetry are intrinsically evident to the crew through deceleration, yaw and thrust-lever/parameter cues, so no crew-unaware variant exists for the fully-lost or asymmetric conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: The N/A awareness on SF-023 would require an additional crew-unaware row for the evident conditions.
assumptions.rationale: Detection means and alerting are not enumerated in the SDD; the awareness-dismissal rests on physical cues rather than a documented annunciation.

assumptions.text: A slow or small partial thrust shortfall can develop below crew detection thresholds absent a dedicated shortfall annunciation, sustaining a crew-unaware partial-loss variant.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-023 Unaware partial-loss row is removed if all partial shortfalls are reliably annunciated.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not state that a gradual thrust degradation is annunciated, forcing a conservative crew-unaware row.

assumptions.text: Reverse-thrust MAC rule SF-002 (Landing) is met so long as at least one reverser item remains, so total loss = both reverser items lost and partial loss = one reverser lost while the other remains.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Total-vs-Partial boundary for ground reverse thrust would move.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: SF-002 names items ITM-005/ITM-006 by placeholder id; the SDD states reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only, but item-to-engine mapping is not given.

assumptions.text: Inadvertent reverse deployment and gross reverser asymmetry produce immediate yaw/deceleration cues on the ground, so those conditions are intrinsically evident; only a subtle undetected asymmetry sustains a crew-unaware variant.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-024 N/A awareness would require an additional evident-condition unaware row, or the Unaware asymmetry row would be removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024 malfunction rows, SF-024 Unaware row

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement

assumptions.rationale: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, but detection means for a subtle ground asymmetry are not enumerated.

assumptions.text: SF-025 total loss (both packs failed) is worse when crew are unaware because delayed recognition denies timely descent and pack reconfiguration.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-025 Unaware row collapses and the awareness split is not required; a single Both/Aware row would carry the conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025 Unaware row; Undetected erroneous air conditioning

citations.quote: Single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes indication of differential/cabin altitude but does not confirm a dedicated pack-loss or conditioning-loss annunciation with adequate salience, so awareness effect on outcome cannot be grounded.

assumptions.text: A slow or misleading cabin pressure error can develop below crew detection thresholds, making the unaware case the dimensioning one for SF-026.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-026 Unaware malfunction rows would not be separately required and would fold into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026 Unaware row; Undetected erroneous/uncommanded cabin pressure conditions

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states differential pressure and cabin altitude are sent to avionics and to crew oxygen logic but does not specify alerting thresholds or annunciation adequacy, so the detectability of a slow error is not grounded.

assumptions.text: For SF-026, TOTAL LOSS is loss breaching MAC SF-015 (no working controller/outflow-valve pairing), PARTIAL LOSS is degraded operation with at least one valid controller and one valid outflow valve retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: The line between SF-026 total and partial loss shifts; conditions may need re-partitioning if independent relief/pneumatic backup is credited into the MAC.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026 Total loss / Partial loss rows

citations.quote: Pressurisation control is by two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient.

assumptions.rationale: The MAC rule SF-015 requires at least one of the two controllers AND at least one of the two outflow valves; the item-to-configuration mapping (ITM-017..020) is not spelled out in the SDD text, so the split is read against the two-controller/two-valve architecture.

assumptions.text: For SF-025, TOTAL LOSS is loss breaching MAC SF-014 (neither conditioning item ITM-015/016 available), PARTIAL LOSS is single-pack/reduced-schedule operation with at least one item retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: The total/partial boundary for conditioning shifts if the ITM items are not the two packs.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025 Total loss / Partial loss rows

citations.quote: Two air cycle packs are supplied with bleed air from the four engines

assumptions.rationale: MAC rule SF-014 requires at least one of ITM-015/016; the SDD confirms two packs with single-pack operation permitted but does not map ITM identifiers to packs, so the split is read against the two-pack architecture.

assumptions.text: Crew-Aware detection means, indication salience and mitigating procedures for all ECS conditions cannot be grounded from the SDD and are left empty for the engineer.
assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting proves inadequate, some Aware rows would need re-evaluation as effectively unaware.
assumptions.usedFor: all crew-indication and mitigation fields (left empty)
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes what data crosses the ECS boundary but not the crew alerting design or procedures, so indication/mitigation fields are not populated.

assumptions.text: SF-028 icing detection is advisory only, so an undetected loss or a misleading detection output can develop below crew detection thresholds and denies timely activation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dedicated detector-health annunciation exists and is guaranteed, the SF-028 Unaware rows collapse and only the Aware rows remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-028 Unaware rows (undetected total/partial loss, undetected erroneous icing detection)

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually at any time.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is advisory with automatic or manual activation but gives no dedicated failure annunciation for the detection channel itself, forcing an assumption about whether the crew is alerted.

assumptions.text: SF-027 loss of a single electrically heated stabiliser zone or a bleed-side degradation is annunciated, but a slow or partial protection shortfall in icing can develop before it is evident to the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all surface/inlet protection shortfalls are reliably annunciated, the SF-027 Unaware rows collapse to the Aware rows only.

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD annunciates a lost electrical zone and bleed status, but does not establish that every partial surface/inlet protection shortfall is detected in time, forcing a conservative crew-unaware reading.

assumptions.text: SF-027 partial loss stays within the served MAC when at least one of the two provided protection paths (bleed via cross-bleed manifold, or an independent electrical zone) remains available; total loss is breach of that minimum.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the true MAC line differs, conditions currently drafted as partial loss may be total loss (or vice versa), changing the SF-027 total/partial split.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-027 total loss vs partial loss split

citations.quote: Bleed protection is available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold.

assumptions.rationale: The MAC rule cited (SF-017: at least 1 of ITM-021/ITM-022) governs the served aircraft function, and SF-016 has no MAC rule yet, so the total/partial line is read conservatively against available protection paths.

assumptions.text: No MAC rule exists yet for SF-016; the SF-027 surface/inlet conditions are therefore read conservatively against the served protection minimum until that rule is defined.
assumptions.ifWrong: If SF-016's MAC rule, once defined, is more or less permissive, the SF-027 total-vs-partial boundary moves accordingly.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-027 total loss vs partial loss split
assumptions.rationale: The task states no MAC rule yet exists for SF-016, so the total/partial threshold for the surface/inlet protection served by that function cannot be stated precisely.

assumptions.text: The primary display and reference-unit chain (SF-029) can fail without an intrinsic sensory cue, and the standby instrument on the DC essential bus is the retained means when primaries are lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Total-vs-Partial boundary for SF-029 shifts: a loss the MAC rule tolerates would move from Total to Partial or vice versa.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-029 Total loss / Partial loss rows

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The function list and §5.11 describe redundancy but do not state which loss combinations breach the SF-018 MAC rule versus stay within it; the Total/Partial split leans on that.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/navigation data can develop below crew and cross-check detection thresholds (misleading data with no annunciation), justifying a distinct crew-Unaware malfunction row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If all erroneous data is intrinsically annunciated or cross-checked, the SF-029 Unaware malfunction row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: No detection-means or comparator-monitor coverage is described for out-of-tolerance data, so whether every erroneous case self-annunciates cannot be grounded.

assumptions.text: Loss or corruption of the crew-alerting function can itself be latent, since the alerting channel is the means by which the crew would otherwise be told a failure has occurred.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of alerting is always independently annunciated, the SF-030 Unaware rows collapse into the Aware rows.

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: Nothing in §5.11 states a means to annunciate loss of the alerting function itself; per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 loss of annunciation is a failure condition in its own right.

assumptions.text: The SF-019 MAC rule (at least one of ITM-032/ITM-033) governs the alerting-function Total-vs-Partial boundary, so degraded alerting with one channel retained stays within the MAC.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Total-vs-Partial boundary for SF-030 shifts depending on which items the MAC rule actually names.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-030 Total loss / Partial loss rows

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The MAC rule is given by item id only; mapping those items to the two independent alerting channels of §5.11.2 is not supplied and had to be assumed to split Total from Partial.

assumptions.text: Fire and overheat warnings are annunciated to the crew alerting system, so a total or partial loss of detection that is itself annunciated (loop fault) is crew-aware, while a latent detection failure that produces no fault flag is the crew-unaware variant.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of detection is fully self-annunciated in every case, the SF-031 Unaware rows collapse; if it is never annunciated, the Aware detection-loss rows are not credible.

citations.quote: AND logic between them for warning, degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop
Fire and overheat warnings to the crew alerting system

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection outputs warnings and degrades to single-loop logic, but does not confirm loss-of-detection (loop health) is annunciated in all cases, forcing the Aware/Unaware split.

assumptions.text: An inadvertent extinguishant discharge is evident to the crew via discharge status, whereas a failure to discharge on command may be latent until suppression is actually demanded, giving the SF-032 unaware malfunction variant.
assumptions.ifWrong: If failure to discharge is continuously annunciated, the SF-032 Unaware malfunction row is not credible and collapses to Aware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-032 Aware and Unaware malfunction rows

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists discharge status as an output but does not state whether a failed-to-discharge condition is annunciated before a discharge is commanded, forcing the malfunction awareness split.

assumptions.text: The MAC total/partial line for SF-031 detection is read against SF-020's rule (at least one detector element retained in each of five zone pairs), and for SF-032 extinguishing against SF-021's rule (at least one bottle path retained per engine pair plus the APU bottle); breaching the rule is total loss, remaining within it is partial loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the item groupings map differently, the boundary between total-loss and partial-loss conditions on both sub-functions shifts.
assumptions.usedFor: All SF-031 and SF-032 total-loss and partial-loss rows

citations.quote: Two bottles per engine pair with cross-plumbing; independent APU protection

assumptions.rationale: The provided MAC rules name only opaque item ids (ITM-034…ITM-048); mapping them to detection zones versus extinguisher bottles requires assuming SF-020 governs detection and SF-021 governs extinguishing.

assumptions.text: The aircraft can continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1, so partial forward-thrust loss holds the MAC rule.
assumptions.ifWrong: If one-engine-out continuation is not achievable, Partial loss of forward thrust generation would rise above Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-023-PL Partial loss of forward thrust generation

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.rationale: The provided SDD states the dispatch design case but the FHA must credit it to set the partial-loss class below Catastrophic.

assumptions.text: Rudder authority sized for the outboard-engine failure case is sufficient for the crew to arrest asymmetric or uncommanded thrust excursions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetric thrust exceeds controllable rudder authority, Asymmetric thrust generation would rise above Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-023-M Asymmetric thrust generation,Uncommanded thrust change

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the sizing case but does not quantify controllable asymmetry, forcing a judgement on whether the excursion is arrestable.

assumptions.text: Wheel braking with the ~1,080 m predicted rollout against the 1,800 m requirement retains adequate landing-distance margin without reverse thrust on the semi-prepared surface.
assumptions.ifWrong: If braking margin is inadequate on a contaminated strip, Total loss of ground reverse thrust would rise above Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024-TL Total loss of ground reverse thrust; SF-024-PL Partial loss of ground reverse thrust

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives dry predicted rollout and the requirement but no contaminated-surface case, forcing a margin judgement for reverse-loss classes.

assumptions.text: Inadvertent in-flight reverse deployment, despite the WOW/radio-altimeter inhibit and mechanical sleeve lock, is credited as a controllable single-engine asymmetry rather than loss of the aircraft.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the in-flight reverse asymmetry exceeds controllable authority, Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment would be Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024-M Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment,Asymmetric reverse thrust

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the inhibit architecture but does not quantify the resulting asymmetry, forcing a judgement on the credited outcome.

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and carries only flight crew, so no passenger conditioning or depressurisation exposure exists for any ECS failure condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold were occupied in flight, every effPax axis and the depressurisation-related classes (SF-026-TL, SF-026-M2) would rise toward Hazardous/Catastrophic on the occupant axis.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on all rows; SF-026-TL and SF-026-M2 severity

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.rationale: The occupant effect axis depends entirely on whether anyone is exposed in the hold; the description states the hold is not occupied.

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen (quick-donning masks) is available and, with the FL260 ceiling and emergency descent, keeps crew capability sufficient after total loss of pressure control so the outcome is Hazardous not Catastrophic.
assumptions.ifWrong: If crew oxygen were unavailable or time-to-incapacitation shorter than descent time, SF-026-TL and SF-026-M2 would move to Catastrophic on the crew axis.

citations.quote: feeding four quick-donning full-face masks with integral smoke goggles and demand regulators

assumptions.rationale: The pressure-loss classes turn on whether crew action with oxygen bounds the outcome below Catastrophic; the description gives crew oxygen and a maximum altitude of FL260.

assumptions.text: Single-pack operation with a reduced hold conditioning schedule is a permitted dispatchable degraded mode that retains flight-deck distribution.
assumptions.ifWrong: If single-pack operation did not retain adequate flight-deck conditioning, SF-025-PL would rise from Minor toward Major.

citations.quote: Single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule.

assumptions.rationale: The partial-loss class depends on whether one pack sustains acceptable operation; §5.9.3 states single-pack operation is permitted.

assumptions.text: Independent positive and negative mechanical pressure relief protects the fuselage structure regardless of control-system state, so erroneous pressure control does not produce structural over/under-pressure failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If mechanical relief did not bound the excursion, SF-026-M and SF-026-M2 could reach structural rupture and Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.rationale: The malfunction classes turn on whether an erroneous outflow-valve drive can over- or under-pressurise the structure; §5.9.2 states relief is independent of the control system.

assumptions.text: The flight crew are alerted to a detected total or partial loss of surface/inlet ice protection and can exit the icing envelope before accretion becomes unrecoverable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If timely escape cannot be shown, SF-027-TL and SF-027-TL2 could rise from Hazardous toward Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a lost electrical zone is annunciated and detection is advisory, but does not establish the time available to escape icing versus accretion rate.

assumptions.text: Bleed protection remains available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold so a partial loss still holds the SF-017 MAC (at least one of the credited protection means available).
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single partial failure can breach the SF-017 MAC, the partial-loss rows become total-loss cases and the class rises to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Bleed protection is available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold.

assumptions.rationale: The MAC rule for SF-017 requires at least one of ITM-021/ITM-022; the SDD confirms bleed availability from either side but does not map the MAC items to specific zones.

assumptions.text: The independent integrated standby instrument provides valid air data if probe icing corrupts the primary air-data sources.
assumptions.ifWrong: If probe icing can corrupt all air-data sources simultaneously, SF-028-TL and SF-028-TL2 could rise from Hazardous toward Catastrophic.

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, but does not confirm its sensing is immune to the same probe-icing event.

assumptions.text: A true total loss of all flight and navigation data presentation defeats the independent standby instrument at the same time as the primary displays.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby remains independently available, SF-029-TL is not a total loss of presentation and reduces toward partial loss (Major), not Catastrophic.

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, so a total loss of ALL presentation must be credited to a common cause reaching all three; the FCIM condition is written as total, forcing this reading.

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/navigation data is normally detectable through disagreement between the three reference units and the independent standby, giving the crew a valid comparison source.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the erroneous data can be presented commonly with no comparison flag, SF-029-M is not crew-detectable and merges with the Catastrophic SF-029-M2.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists three reference units and an independent standby but does not state comparison-monitor coverage; detectability of erroneous data is assumed from that redundancy.

assumptions.text: The loss of the crew alerting function is itself annunciated to the crew when at least one alerting channel remains or its health is monitored.
assumptions.ifWrong: If total loss of alerting is not self-annunciated in the SF-030-TL condition, that row is not the detected case and rises toward the Hazardous of SF-030-TL2.

assumptions.ifWrong: If ECS or AVI could interrupt the oxygen supply itself, the total-loss cases would become true as direct-loss contributors rather than detection-only.
assumptions.usedFor: all ECS/AVI total-loss and malfunction cases

citations.quote: the cabin altitude signal from the environmental control system; crew donning action.

assumptions.rationale: The FC concerns 'undetected' loss but the supplied systems are ECS and AVI, neither of which stores or delivers oxygen; their only OXY interfaces are signal and indication.

assumptions.text: An ECS or AVI malfunction can produce a false-normal or erroneous cabin-altitude/oxygen indication rather than an overtly annunciated failure, defeating detection.
assumptions.ifWrong: If malfunctions are always self-annunciated, the malfunction-bearing cases would be false because the loss would be detected.
assumptions.usedFor: malfunction cases for ECS, AVI and their combinations

citations.quote: cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting.

assumptions.rationale: The document describes indication and alerting functions but does not characterise malfunction (mis-indication) modes, forcing a conservative treatment of undetected coupling.

assumptions.text: The main-gear tyre burst debris field is bounded by AC 25.734-1 tread/debris geometry and the SDD's preliminary 20-tyre / six-bogie arrangement.
assumptions.ifWrong: The zones struck and whether both A and B brake lines in a bay are within the debris field could change, altering the tyre-burst CSFL and its mitigation adequacy.
assumptions.usedFor: Tire burst PRA row — zones 710/720/300 and the A/B brake-line common-bay CSFL

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the gear leg and bogie count is preliminary and not frozen, and gives no debris energy or trajectory data.

assumptions.text: The installed turbofan carries valid §33.76 bird-ingestion substantiation applicable at this installation.
assumptions.ifWrong: The bird-strike effect on SF-001 forward thrust could be more severe than 'shown acceptable', changing the propulsion failure-condition contribution and the required mitigation.
assumptions.usedFor: Bird strike PRA row — engine ingestion effect on SF-001 and the 'shown acceptable' effect claim

citations.quote: the model definition has not yet been released to the engineering organisation

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the engine model has not been released to engineering and downstream data are taken from a mature engine of the same class.

assumptions.text: The two forward-fuselage ice detectors, being the same type and same forward region, are a credible common-cause pair under a multi-bird forward-face encounter.
assumptions.ifWrong: If geometric separation is shown adequate, the ice-detector CSFL in the bird-strike row is removed and its mitigation requirement is discharged.
assumptions.usedFor: Bird strike PRA row — ice-detector CSFL and the dissimilar-detection requirement candidate

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records detector type commonality as an item for examination but provides no separation distance or strike-geometry analysis.

assumptions.text: The functions whose failure is Catastrophic/Hazardous and therefore drive lightning and HIRF protection are the fly-by-wire flight control (roll/pitch/yaw), flight/nav data presentation, cabin pressure control and nose-door pressure-boundary closure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a different function set is Catastrophic/Hazardous, the affected-function list and the requirement candidates for both PRA rows change to match.
assumptions.usedFor: Both PRA rows' functions[] and requirements[]

citations.quote: It does not enumerate failure conditions. It does not classify anything by severity

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the architecture but does not classify functions; the applicable HIRF/lightning protection scope depends on which functions are Catastrophic/Hazardous, which is set by the FHA not the SDD.

assumptions.text: The claimed physical/electrical independence of the three flight control channels, the two data networks and the HV/LV routes can be defeated in common by a single lightning transient or the HIRF environment unless protection is substantiated.
assumptions.ifWrong: If independence holds under these threats without additional protection, the common-mode scenarios and the separation/shielding requirement candidates in both rows are not required.
assumptions.usedFor: Both PRA rows' desc, mitigation and requirements

citations.quote: physical separation is replaced by shielding and a defined minimum distance

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the routes ARE the independence argument but marks bundle build/clamping as preliminary and explicitly flags the crossing points as items to be tested rather than assumed.

assumptions.text: Lightning attachment to the wing leading edges places an ignition-source threat on the flammable fluid present in zones 510/520 including the single spanwise cross-feed gallery.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the fuel installation is shown non-susceptible to lightning ignition, the §25.581 fuel-ignition requirement candidate in the Lightning row is unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: Lightning row requirement candidate on FUE zones 510/520

citations.quote: Fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route ... Flammable fluid present

assumptions.rationale: The zonal model lists flammable fluid present in 510/520 and the fuel gallery as a recorded particular-risk item, but the SDD does not assess ignition margins.

assumptions.text: Both same-type ice detectors on opposite sides of the forward fuselage can be struck/affected by a single hail encounter or icing condition, making the SF-017 dual-detector redundancy a common-cause candidate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detector siting genuinely prevents a single-encounter common-cause, the SF-017 CSFL claim and the detector-separation requirement in both rows drop.
assumptions.usedFor: Hail row CSFL + detector requirement; Ice row CSFL + SF-017-TL/M rows

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the same-type commonality as an item for examination but does not state whether siting defeats a single-encounter common-cause.

assumptions.text: The single cross-bleed manifold in Zone 300 is the shared feed for both wing and cowl bleed anti-ice, so a manifold-level fault is a common-mode against ice protection on both sides.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manifold isolation fully segregates the two sides, the Ice-row CSFL manifold common-mode and its first requirement weaken to a single-side effect.
assumptions.usedFor: Ice row CSFL + first ice-protection requirement; SF-016-TL

citations.quote: protected by hot bleed air, taken from the same manifold that supplies the environmental packs

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states wing and cowl protection is bled from the same manifold but does not quantify manifold-level fault isolation.

assumptions.text: Simultaneous hail ingestion or shed-ice ingestion into more than one inlet is credible given the four podded inlets and can exceed the one-engine-out dispatch case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If ingestion is credibly single-engine only, the multi-engine thrust scenario reduces to SF-001-PL/SF-001-M and the inlet requirements narrow.
assumptions.usedFor: Hail + Ice rows: SF-001 thrust functions and inlet requirements

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and is retained as a condition to be studied.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD frames single-engine-out as the dispatch case and retains second-engine loss as a condition to be studied; multi-inlet environmental ingestion is not bounded.

assumptions.text: The certification hail size/energy and the icing envelope limits are not fixed in the provided material, so the impact/accretion model is qualitative pending those inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the envelope/hail parameters differ materially, the affected-zone extent and the survivability claims in both rows may change.
assumptions.usedFor: Empty quantitative fields in both PRA rows; scope of both studies

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes the icing envelope only as 'the icing envelope of the certification basis' and gives no hail parameters; several PRA fields are left empty on this basis.

assumptions.text: The hold is not occupied in flight and carries only a single unitised blade with no combustible palletised load, so no hold fire suppression is fitted.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a combustible load or occupancy case is credible, the hold requires a §25.855 cargo-compartment fire suppression provision and the survivability outcome flips from open to not-acceptable-without-suppression.
assumptions.usedFor: add_pra Cabin/hold fire — mitigation and CSFL assessment

citations.quote: the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load, and hold suppression is deliberately not fitted

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the no-suppression decision but explicitly records it as an assumption to be substantiated, so the safety case cannot yet treat it as fixed.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop and the left-side low-voltage signal route are the only monitoring/signal paths that transit all three hold zones and share the hold environment.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a redundant or separately-zoned monitoring/signal path exists, the CSFL common-mode claim weakens and the second proposed separation requirement may be unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: add_pra Cabin/hold fire — csfl and second requirement

citations.quote: Single instrumented loop, full hold length, left side above the floor line

assumptions.rationale: The routing table names these as single spanwise/left-side runs through the hold zones; no independent second path through the hold is described, forcing the common-mode assumption.

assumptions.text: Project ITEMS carry an owning-system id but no zoneId, so equipment-to-zone placement was taken from the SDD §3 zone-contents table rather than a machine join.
assumptions.ifWrong: If actual item placement differs from the SDD contents table, the housed-equipment and functional-impact fields of the affected zones change, and some inherent-hazard findings may move zones.

citations.quote: Zone Description Principal contents Environment 110 Nose visor structure Visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, sensing harness

assumptions.rationale: The items[] array in project state has no zone field, so the zone→item→function join required by App K cannot be computed from the model and had to be sourced from the document.

assumptions.text: Zones 510/520, 530/540, 610–640 and 710/720 are left/right symmetric pairs with substantially uniform environment, so one representative zone was authored per pair with mirror noted.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a mirror zone differs (e.g. only inboard nacelles carry reversers, or one wing root carries the refuel point), that zone needs its own ZSA row with distinct equipment and findings.

citations.quote: 510 / 520 Left / right wing box and leading edge Fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists these zones as mirrored pairs and Figure 6-1 was not machine-readable, so I could not confirm any asymmetry that would warrant separate authoring.

assumptions.text: Each ZSA severity is an inherent-hazard consequence judgement for engineer confirmation, not a §25.1309 failure-condition classification; where I cited Catastrophic/Hazardous I anchored to an existing AFHA FC for the function housed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the engineer intends ZSA severity to reflect only the local physical event rather than the governing aircraft-level FC, several Catastrophic ratings drop to the local-damage level.
assumptions.usedFor: severity field on all add_zsa rows

citations.quote: It does not classify anything and it does not assess anything.

assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A App K assesses failure-consequence within/beyond the zone qualitatively; the provided state gives AFHA severities but the ZSA schema demands a single severity field, so I mapped to the governing FC.

assumptions.text: The engine nacelles and the APU compartment are treated as designated fire zones with drainage/ventilation obligations, per §25.1181 and §29.1187, consistent with the SDD calling them fire zones.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a compartment is not ultimately a designated fire zone or drainage/ventilation is shown compliant by other means, the nacelle (610–640) and 800/APU mitigations change.

citations.quote: 800 Aft fuselage and empennage Rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment Mixed; APU is a fire zone

assumptions.rationale: The regulation list supplied designates these compartments and the SDD labels nacelles and APU as fire zones; drainage/ventilation adequacy is not stated in the document and must be substantiated.

assumptions.text: All four turbofans are the same certified engine type/model, making a type-level design/software/material defect a credible common cause across the four-engine set.
assumptions.ifWrong: If positions were dissimilar or the type-level coupling is not credible, the SF-001-TL common-cause contributor would be removed and the four-engine AND could stand closer to independent.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-TL CMA rows (both branches) — shared engine type finding and the requirement for an explicit common-cause contributor

citations.quote: The generators are of a single part number across all four positions

assumptions.rationale: The SDD selects one engine class for all positions but the model is not yet released to engineering, so no dissimilarity between positions is available to break the coupling.

assumptions.text: The single spanwise fuel cross-feed gallery and the zone-300 mid-hold commonality couple otherwise-separated engine feed paths, so both are credible common-cause contributors to SF-001-TL.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the gallery and zone-300 co-transit are shown not to couple both engine pairs, those findings drop and the SF-001-TL contributors reduce to the engine-type commonality only.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-TL CMA rows — fuel-gallery and zone-300 common-environment findings

citations.quote: Single spanwise run through the wing box; the only path from one wing to the opposite engines

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the gallery is the only cross-side fuel path and zone 300 is the principal commonality zone, but no quantitative separation/segregation substantiation is provided.

assumptions.text: The two inboard reversers share a common weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter deploy/inhibit design, making that logic a credible common-cause contributor to total loss of ground reverse thrust.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the deploy-permit signals are independent per reverser, the SF-002-TL common-cause contributor is removed and the two-reverser AND stands closer to independent.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL CMA row — shared deploy/inhibit design finding and the associated independence requirement

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a single inhibit scheme for reverser deployment but does not state whether the WoW/radio-altimeter signals are independent per reverser.

assumptions.text: Reverse-thrust total loss is driven by the two inboard reversers (ITM-005, ITM-006) and their engines being the sole redundant set.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust has additional redundancy or a single-point manifold, the independence claim and the requirements change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL · PRP ∧ AVI independence; SF-002-TL · PRP inboard-reverser redundancy independence

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.rationale: The seeded SF-002-TL tree is an OR of PRP and AVI contributions with no explicit redundant basic events, so the actual redundancy relied upon had to be read from the SDD.

assumptions.text: The weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement that permits reverser deployment is shared across both inboard reversers rather than dedicated per side.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the permission sources are dedicated and dissimilar per side, the AVI-side coupling concern and its requirement are removed.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the deploy-permission logic but does not state whether the WOW/radio-altimeter sources are independent per reverser.

assumptions.text: The two air cycle packs share a single cross-bleed manifold as their common bleed supply path.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each pack has an independent bleed path immune to a single manifold failure, the shared-manifold common-cause contributor is removed from SF-014-TL.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-014-TL · Air cycle pack 1 ∧ pack 2 independence

citations.quote: Two air cycle packs are supplied with bleed air from the four engines through a cross-bleed manifold

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes one cross-bleed manifold supplying both packs; whether a manifold failure can defeat both is not resolved.

assumptions.text: The two pressurisation controllers (ITM-017/018) and two outflow valves (ITM-019/020) are not confirmed to be fed from independent electrical sources.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they are in fact segregated, the EPS common-resource concern (finding 1) downgrades and the corresponding independence requirement closes.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA rows SF-015 dual pressurisation controllers and SF-015 dual outflow valves

citations.quote: electrical power to the controllers, valves and fans

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists electrical power as an ECS input but does not allocate the controller/valve pairs to distinct EPS buses.

assumptions.text: The two same-type ice detectors share no dissimilarity argument, so a common-design or common-icing-envelope deficiency can fail both.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a dissimilarity or independent crew procedure is credited, the SF-017-TL common-design concern downgrades and the independence requirement closes.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA row SF-017 dual ice detectors

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly records the detector commonality as an unresolved item and states no dissimilar detection principle.

assumptions.text: Both fire detection loops (A and B) in a monitored zone are powered from the single DC essential bus, with no independent second supply to loop B.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loop B is independently supplied, the DC-essential common-resource contributor is removed from the SF-020-TL evaluation and one independence requirement is unnecessary.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA subject SF-020-TL — Common Resource (power) finding and requirement 3

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is supplied from the DC essential bus but does not distinguish supplies between loop A and loop B, so a shared-supply common cause cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: Loops A and B use the same continuous-detection element type with no dissimilarity between them.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loops A and B are dissimilar by design, the Common Design contributor drops out of the SF-020-TL CMA.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA subject SF-020-TL — Common Design finding

citations.quote: dual-loop continuous fire detection, with the two loops routed separately

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes 'dual-loop continuous fire detection' without asserting dissimilarity, so a common design/material deficiency contributor cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: Both fire-detection loops A and B of each nacelle (and of the APU compartment) draw their sensing supply from the DC essential bus, making it a shared resource across the redundant pair.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loops A and B are on genuinely independent supplies, the DC-essential common-cause contributor is removed from the SF-020-TL finding and the AND independence strengthens.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-TL engine and APU fire-detection CMA findings

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is DC-powered from the essential bus but does not split the two loops onto separate supplies, forcing the assumption that both loops share it.

assumptions.text: The two extinguisher bottles of each engine pair share the hot battery bus for their discharge circuits, making it a common resource across the pair.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each bottle's discharge circuit is on an independent supply, the hot-battery-bus common-cause contributor drops out of the SF-021-TL finding.

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD assigns discharge circuits to the hot battery bus without stating per-bottle supply separation, forcing the shared-supply assumption.

assumptions.text: The nacelle fire-detection loops A/B and the APU loops A/B are of a single common detection part type, exposing them to systematic common-mode.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loops A and B are dissimilar in technology, the common-design contributor is removed and the systematic common-mode concern is discharged.
assumptions.usedFor: Common design/part-type rows of the SF-020-TL findings

citations.quote: dual-loop continuous fire detection, with the two loops routed separately and an AND logic between them

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual-loop continuous detection without asserting dissimilarity between the two loops, so a common part type is assumed.

assumptions.text: The two extinguisher bottles within an engine pair are of the same type / part number, creating a common design and manufacturing-lot common-cause exposure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the bottles are dissimilar/independent-lot, common-design and common-lot contributor (finding 3) drops and requirement 2 is discharged by design.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA finding (3) and independence requirement 2 for SF-021-TL

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two bottles per pair and cross-plumbing but does not state whether the bottles are dissimilar or a single part number, forcing an assumption to test the design common cause.

assumptions.text: Both bottles of an engine pair share the hot battery bus as their discharge electrical source, making that bus a common resource across the redundant pair.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two bottles of a pair are fed from segregated discharge supplies, common-bus contributor (finding 1) is removed and requirement 1's electrical clause is satisfied by architecture.
assumptions.usedFor: CMA finding (1) and independence requirement 1 for SF-021-TL

citations.quote: Discharge circuits are supplied from the hot battery bus so that they remain available with all generation lost.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD places discharge circuits on the hot battery bus but does not confirm per-bottle bus segregation, forcing the shared-resource assumption.

assumptions.text: No SF-021-TL (or system-level SF-032-TL) fault-tree page exists in the model, so the CMA cannot yet be linked to an AND gate and is filed as a development-phase independence requirement only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an SF-021-TL fault tree is later built, a link (fromTable 'cma' → the AND gate) should be added and the finding re-run as a verification-phase check.
assumptions.usedFor: Absence of a link action for the SF-021-TL CMA row
assumptions.rationale: The ftaPages list in project state contains only SF-001 through SF-008 MF&MS pages; there is no SF-021/SF-032 tree to which a CMA gate link could attach.

assumptions.text: The high-lift (flaps/slats) function is commanded by the crew through a selector, since the document describes the drive architecture but not the control interface.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-008 allocation row changes from crew to shared or automation if the design schedules high-lift automatically.

citations.quote: High-lift comprises double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats, driven by two independent power drive units through a common torque shaft

assumptions.rationale: §5.3 describes the high-lift power drive units and asymmetry brakes but §5.3.6 does not state who commands high-lift, so the allocation for SF-008 was assumed from conventional crew selection.

assumptions.text: Isolating a failed engine by the wrong fuel shut-off / fire handle produces an asymmetric thrust condition rather than a symmetric one.
assumptions.ifWrong: The fcIds mapping on the engine-isolation selection row changes from SF-001-M to a partial-loss condition.

citations.quote: There is no crew action required to isolate a failed engine other than to close the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the crew action to isolate an engine but does not enumerate the failure condition a selection error feeds; the failure-condition list separates asymmetric from partial loss.

assumptions.text: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation are the crew actions through which an erroneous fuel distribution can be commanded.
assumptions.ifWrong: The commission row for erroneous fuel distribution loses its grounded crew task and should be dropped.

citations.quote: The crew can select manual cross-feed and can isolate any tank.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD says distribution is normally automatic and lists only manual cross-feed and tank isolation as crew-selectable; no other in-flight fuel action is described.

assumptions.text: The consolidated crew alert list presents fuel-feed, restraint, fire, and control-law conditions in a manner detectable and intelligible under multiple-alert conditions per §25.1322(a)(2).
assumptions.ifWrong: The 'information to perform the task' findings for the alerting rows would need requalification against detectability and multiple-alert legibility.
assumptions.usedFor: Prioritised crew alert list; Fuel low-pressure and imbalance discretes; Strap tension / restraint status indication; Fire and overheat warnings

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the alerting list consolidates every system's status but does not describe detectability or intelligibility under concurrent alerts.

assumptions.text: The consolidated crew alert list is the primary situation-awareness cue for non-normal engine and flight-control conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: Rows that rely on the alert list as the perception/comprehension cue would need a different cue or would become open findings.
assumptions.usedFor: Which engine has failed and needs isolation; Asymmetric thrust condition following an engine failure

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: The document describes a single prioritised crew alert list but does not enumerate which specific failure conditions raise an alert, forcing an assumption about coverage.

assumptions.text: The document does not describe a dedicated flight-deck indication of thrust-reverser deployed/stowed state.
assumptions.ifWrong: The reverser-state and inadvertent-deployment rows would carry a real cue rather than a finding of an absent cue.
assumptions.usedFor: Reverser deployment state on landing rollout; Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.rationale: Only the in-flight deployment inhibit and mechanical lock are described; no reverser position display is mentioned, forcing the finding that the perception cue is unstated.

assumptions.text: On a ground-phase loss before V1 the take-off can be rejected and the aircraft stopped within the runway/strip available.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives V1 continuation for one-engine failure but does not state the reject stopping performance for a total thrust loss on the ground.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-001-TL Standing/Taxi/RTO row would no longer be No Safety Effect and would rise toward the in-flight class if a stop cannot be achieved.

citations.quote: continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: The representative partial loss of forward thrust is a single-engine loss, with same-side dual-engine loss excluded as outside the dispatch case.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states one-engine-out is the design dispatch case and a second same-side engine loss is retained for study, so the partial-loss depth is not bounded for the FHA.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-PL would rise above Major if the credited partial loss extends to two engines on one side.

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and is retained as a condition to be studied

assumptions.text: Asymmetric thrust in flight is bounded by a single outboard-engine failure and countered within the rudder authority sized for that case.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard-engine asymmetry as the directional-control sizing case but does not bound the concurrent loss of the countering rudder supply.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-M in-flight would rise above Major if the asymmetry exceeds sized rudder authority or the countering supply is concurrently lost.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: Wheel braking alone stops the aircraft within the 1,800 m landing requirement without credit for reverse thrust, on the semi-prepared surface.
assumptions.rationale: The margin is stated for nominal predicted rollout; braking degradation and low-friction strip conditions concurrent with reverse loss are not bounded.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-TL Landing/RTO would rise above Minor if braking is also degraded or friction is low enough to exceed the available margin.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis on which braking degradation is assessed

assumptions.text: Undetected partial thrust loss is classified by the §5.4.2 loss-of-annunciation default pending assessment of engine-parameter monitoring coverage.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms engine parameter data reaches the displays but does not state the integrity/coverage of monitoring that would detect a partial thrust shortfall.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-M2 would rise above Major if the undetected shortfall could contribute to a hazardous outcome, or fall if full monitoring coverage is shown.

citations.quote: engine parameter data to the avionics display system

assumptions.text: Wheel braking is the primary ground deceleration means and reverse thrust is supplementary, not credited against the landing-distance requirement.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the landing-distance requirement and predicted rollout but does not state whether reverse thrust is credited in that rollout figure.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-PL on landing/RTO rises from Minor to Major or higher if braking credit depends on reverse thrust for the semi-prepared/wet case.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.text: The weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter inhibit and the mechanical sleeve lock together defeat any in-flight reverser deployment as a credited barrier set with no defeating common cause.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the inhibit and lock exist but does not establish their independence or freedom from common cause (e.g. a shared WoW signal source).
assumptions.ifWrong: The in-flight SF-002-M No Safety Effect row becomes a realised in-flight asymmetric reverse deployment near the 28 m outboard-equivalent moment, potentially Hazardous or Catastrophic, and the row splits.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-M in-flight NSE row; SF-002-M2 in-flight NSE row

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock

assumptions.text: On the ground the crew arrests the directional excursion from an inboard asymmetric reverse-thrust event within the available 1,800 m on the semi-prepared surface.

assumptions.rationale: The unaware case by definition credits no alerting; the model does not confirm an independent cabin-altitude warning exists and is effective.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an effective independent cabin-altitude warning is credited, SF-015-M4 high-altitude rows revert to the aware Hazardous case.

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: Loss of ice protection is annunciated and escapable — the crew detect it (via ice detectors / lost-zone annunciation) and can exit the icing envelope in time.
assumptions.rationale: The cert-basis icing envelope is not quantified in the SDD, so escapability had to be assumed to classify below hull loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If protection must be continuously available in the design icing envelope with no escape, SF-016-TL in-icing rows could rise toward Catastrophic.

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 is certified to dispatch into and operate within an icing envelope where ice accretion on unprotected surfaces/inlets or iced probes materially affects safety.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states ice protection is for 'flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis' but does not define that envelope, and the class of every erroneous/loss condition turns on how much icing exposure is credited.
assumptions.ifWrong: If icing exposure is negligible, SF-016-M2, SF-017-TL, SF-017-PL and SF-017-M would drop one class (Major→Minor, Hazardous→Major).

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis.

assumptions.text: Ice protection can be selected and run manually at any time and this manual means remains available after loss of detection.
assumptions.rationale: Detection-loss severity depends on whether protection itself remains commandable; the SDD states manual selection is always available but does not tie its power/availability to the detection failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manual protection is unavailable after detection loss, SF-017-TL would rise from Major toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: the system may also be selected on manually at any time.

assumptions.text: Probes and heated elements are individually monitored and sufficiently redundant that a partial loss of probe protection degrades but does not eliminate valid air data.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD says probes are monitored individually but does not map probe-to-air-data-source redundancy, on which the partial-loss class depends.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a partial probe-protection loss can silently corrupt multiple air-data sources in icing, SF-017-PL would rise from Major to Hazardous.

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.text: Erroneous detection reporting a false 'no icing' is the credited (worst) sub-case and no independent, timely icing cue reliably prompts the crew before hazardous accretion.
assumptions.rationale: SF-017-M is a malfunction with both misleading-safe and false-alarm sub-cases; the class is driven by the misleading-safe case, whose severity depends on whether other cues alert the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reliable independent icing cues alert the crew promptly, SF-017-M would drop from Hazardous to Major.

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.text: Undetected loss of icing detection leaves manual anti-ice selection available and the crew can infer icing from other cues before accretion becomes hazardous.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is advisory with automatic activation and manual selection at any time, but gives no accretion-rate or icing-envelope data to bound the delay to recognition.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-017-TL2 in-flight row moves from Major to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of icing detection (in-flight row)

citations.quote: Detection is advisory and automatic activation is available; the system may also be selected on manually at any time

assumptions.text: Undetected loss of probe protection allows iced probes to feed misleading air data to the primary displays without a probe-heat annunciation to prompt reversion.
assumptions.rationale: Probe heat is 'monitored individually' per the SDD, so whether a loss is truly undetected turns on monitoring coverage the document does not fully resolve.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-017-M2 in-flight row moves from Hazardous to Major if the loss is in fact annunciated.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of probe protection (in-flight row)

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually

assumptions.text: 'Total loss of flight and navigation data' means loss of the primary three-processor presentation while the independent standby instrument remains available and sufficient for continued flight and landing.

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-018-TL in-flight row moves from Hazardous to Catastrophic if the standby is included in the loss.

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight and navigation data can be presented as valid (misleading) in a way not caught by three-source voting or standby cross-check before it drives an unrecoverable trajectory.
