assumptions.ifWrong: SF-018-M in-flight row moves from Catastrophic to Hazardous if any single-source error is voted out and annunciated.
assumptions.usedFor: Erroneous flight and navigation data (in-flight row)

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data. Two are supplied from the main buses and one from the DC essential bus

assumptions.text: A subset of erroneous flight/navigation data errors can be subtle enough to defeat the independent standby-instrument cross-check before an unrecoverable flight state is reached.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD credits an independent standby instrument but does not characterise the error modes or detectability of erroneous primary data, which the Catastrophic classification of SF-018-M2 turns on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every erroneous-data mode is reliably caught by the standby cross-check in time, SF-018-M2 in flight drops from Catastrophic toward Hazardous/Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M2 in-flight row (Undetected erroneous flight and navigation data, Catastrophic)

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus

assumptions.text: In a partial loss of alerting no single high-priority alert class (e.g. fire, takeoff configuration) is wholly lost, given the two independent alerting processing channels.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual independent alerting channels but does not enumerate the partial-loss mode set that SF-019-PL severity depends on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a critical alert class can be wholly lost in the partial case, SF-019-PL rises from Minor to Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-PL row (Partial loss of crew alerting, Minor)

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: The crew can generally disambiguate an erroneous alert against raw parameters before committing to an irreversible unsafe action.
assumptions.rationale: No human-factors record or alerting-integrity argument is provided to bound crew response to misleading alerts, which SF-019-M severity turns on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a misleading alert can drive an irreversible unsafe action (e.g. wrong-engine shutdown) in a critical phase, SF-019-M could rise above Major.

citations.quote: the alerting that tells the crew what has failed and what to do about it

assumptions.text: An ill-timed inadvertent/nuisance alert in a critical phase produces a significant, not merely slight, increase in crew workload.
assumptions.rationale: No nuisance-warning assessment or human-factors data is provided to bound the workload impact of false alerts, which SF-019-M2 severity turns on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If nuisance alerts are demonstrably low-consequence and readily dismissed, SF-019-M2 drops from Major to Minor.

assumptions.text: The worst credible un-annunciated downstream failure that coincides with an undetected loss of crew alerting is at least hazardous in effect.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual independent alerting channels but gives no combined-condition probability or list of the specific downstream conditions that rely on alerting for detection.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the credited combination is only major, SF-019-TL2 drops to Major and its allocation eases.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-TL2 — Undetected loss of crew alerting

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: A total or undetected loss of fire/overheat detection is credited as coinciding with a fire in a monitored fire zone often enough to drive a hazardous outcome.
assumptions.rationale: The provided material names the fire zones and dual-loop architecture but gives no fire probability or combined fire-plus-detection-loss rate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the credited joint condition is less severe, SF-020-TL and SF-020-TL2 could reduce toward Major.

citations.quote: Each engine nacelle and the APU compartment carry dual-loop continuous fire detection

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states extinguishing is a crew action via fire handles but does not state crew procedure resistance to a false single warning.
assumptions.ifWrong: If false warnings cannot drive an unnecessary shutdown/discharge, SF-020-M reduces toward Minor.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-M — Erroneous fire and overheat detection

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.text: Total loss of extinguishing coincident with an engine or APU fire remains Hazardous (large margin reduction) rather than progressing to hull loss, based on nacelle/APU fire containment.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes detection, agent quantity and cross-plumbing but states no nacelle/APU fire containment or burn-through time, which is what decides whether an unextinguishable fire reaches hull loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-021-TL and SF-021-TL2 rise from Hazardous to Catastrophic (CAT-1), and the crew/occupant axes go to their top step.

citations.quote: hold suppression is deliberately not fitted. That decision is recorded and carried forward as an assumption to be substantiated

assumptions.text: A single partial or inadvertent discharge still leaves a usable extinguishing means into any given engine fire zone via the cross-plumbed bottle pair.

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-021-PL and the in-flight SF-021-M rows rise toward the SF-021-TL zone effect (Hazardous) instead of Major.

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair

assumptions.text: An inadvertent discharge on the ground is annunciated and the agent can be recharged before dispatch, so the ground case is recoverable.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists discharge status output and origin dispatch decisions but does not confirm ground recharge capability at the origin.
assumptions.ifWrong: The ground SF-021-M row rises from Minor if the depleted zone cannot be restored before the outbound/return sectors.

citations.quote: Dispatch decisions are therefore taken at the origin with the outbound and return sectors considered together

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-022-TL rises from Hazardous to Catastrophic if the descent cannot be completed before crew incapacitation; oxygen loss alone with the cabin intact would fall well below Hazardous.

citations.quote: supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and for the descent and diversion that follow

assumptions.text: A partial loss of crew oxygen still leaves usable breathing oxygen at reduced reserve, not zero supply.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a partial loss can leave effectively no usable reserve for the diversion, SF-022-PL rises toward Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

citations.quote: The system is sized for four occupants for the diversion time associated with the maximum operating altitude, with reserve.

assumptions.text: Maximum operating altitude is FL260, bounding the time-of-useful-consciousness exposure for an oxygen loss coincident with depressurisation.
assumptions.rationale: The severity of an undetected oxygen loss depends on the altitude exposure the crew must survive without breathing protection; the SDD states the ceiling.
assumptions.ifWrong: If sustained operation at a higher altitude were possible, SF-022-TL2 could escalate toward Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in flight, the occupant axis and possibly the class would change on both rows.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply; Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

assumptions.text: An undetected total oxygen loss requires a further coincident event (depressurisation or smoke/fume) to threaten the aircraft, so it is Hazardous rather than Catastrophic on its own.
assumptions.rationale: Whether the condition is credited alone or only in combination sets Hazardous vs Catastrophic; the SDD states oxygen is provided for loss-of-pressurisation and smoke/fume events.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected loss alone (with an expected depressurisation exposure) is credited as preventing continued safe flight and landing, SF-022-TL2 rises to Catastrophic (CAT-1).
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

assumptions.ifWrong: The ground/RTO rows for SF-001-TL, SF-001-PL and SF-001-M2 would carry the committed airborne end state (Catastrophic / Major / Hazardous) rather than No Safety Effect / Minor.

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-PL airborne Major would rise toward Hazardous/Catastrophic for the multi-engine same-side case.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-PL airborne row, SF-001-M airborne row

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case

assumptions.text: Rudder authority sized to the outboard-engine-out case at the 28 m moment arm maintains directional control for asymmetric thrust within that sizing case.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the outboard asymmetric case as the directional-control sizing case but the classification depends on the resulting authority actually maintaining control, which is a flight-control sizing result not stated numerically here.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-M airborne Major would rise if the retained directional-control authority is insufficient for the credited asymmetry.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: An undetected partial thrust loss is not annunciated to the crew, so the crew take no action per the unaware rule.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states engine parameter data goes to the display system but does not state that a partial thrust shortfall is annunciated or monitored such that the crew would detect it; the unaware condition assumes no crew action.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-001-M2 airborne Hazardous would revert toward the aware Major case if thrust/parameter monitoring is credited to alert the crew.

citations.quote: engine parameter data to the avionics display system

assumptions.text: Wheel braking alone (carbon multi-disc, dual hydraulic supply, accumulator reserve) stops the aircraft within the available distance on the semi-prepared surface without reverse thrust.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the 1,080 m predicted rollout and 1,800 m requirement but does not state how much of the deceleration is attributed to reverse versus braking, nor the semi-prepared surface friction assumption.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-TL landing/RTO Major would rise to Hazardous if wheel braking alone cannot stop within the available distance on a semi-prepared surface.

citations.quote: Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust on the Aeolus HL-1 is used only in the ground deceleration phases (Landing, Rejected Takeoff) and is inhibited/stowed in all airborne phases.

assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust were credited in any airborne phase, the No Safety Effect airborne rows for SF-002-PL and SF-002-M2 would move up in class.

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.text: The 1,800 m landing requirement against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout leaves enough braking margin to absorb loss of one inboard reverser without a significant reduction in stopping capability.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the two distances but not a braking-degradation analysis on the semi-prepared surface; SF-002-PL Minor vs Major turns on that margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the residual margin is insufficient, SF-002-PL becomes Major (MAJ-1) rather than Minor on the ground rows.

citations.quote: The landing distance requirement of 1,800 m on a semi-prepared surface is the sizing case; predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m

assumptions.text: Undetected asymmetric inboard reverse thrust during ground deceleration on a semi-prepared strip produces a directional excursion the crew cannot arrest before departure from the surface.
assumptions.rationale: No ground-controllability or reverser-asymmetry annunciation analysis is provided; SF-002-M2 Hazardous vs Major depends on whether steering/braking recover the excursion.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection and ground steering recover the asymmetry, SF-002-M2 reduces from Hazardous to Major.

assumptions.rationale: The differential and ceiling are marked preliminary in the SDD and no time-of-useful-consciousness analysis is provided, yet the SF-015 malfunction classes turn on how fast an excursion becomes life-threatening.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-015-M4 could move from Hazardous toward Catastrophic and SF-015-M2/M3 toward Hazardous if the frozen differential/ceiling shorten TUC below any credited crew recovery.

assumptions.text: The aircraft is flight-crew only with an unoccupied hold in flight, so the occupant axis reduces to the flight crew and there are no passengers to injure.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant axis needs to know who is aboard; the SDD states crew-only operation but this is an operating-concept assumption the safety case rests on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants can be carried in the hold, the occupant axis on every SF-015 and SF-016 row would need re-evaluation and several classes could rise.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: For SF-015-M4 the pressure change is genuinely unannunciated (loss of the cabin-altitude cue), so no crew detection or descent is credited per §5.4.2.
assumptions.rationale: The unaware condition only holds if the alerting/indication that would normally cue the crew is itself lost; the SDD does not enumerate the annunciation failure path.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a residual independent cue always remains, SF-015-M4 collapses toward the aware Major case and the Hazardous class no longer holds.

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: The SF-016 total- and partial-loss classes assume the crew can, in a material fraction of encounters, avoid or exit the certification icing envelope, and that partial loss retains protection of the flight-critical surfaces.
assumptions.rationale: No MAC rule and no HF task analysis exist for SF-016, and the SDD does not state which surfaces a partial loss can uncover or whether icing is always avoidable.
assumptions.ifWrong: If unavoidable basis-envelope icing leads to loss of control, SF-016-TL rises to Catastrophic; if a single partial mode uncovers a critical surface, SF-016-PL rises to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: Total loss of ice protection; Partial loss of ice protection

citations.quote: for flight in the icing envelope of the certification basis

assumptions.text: The aircraft operates within the icing envelope of the certification basis, so a loss/error of ice detection or protection has a realised in-flight safety effect.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD defines IPS for the icing envelope but the mission/operating concept does not state icing exposure per sector, so the safety-relevance of every SF-017 in-flight row rests on this premise.
assumptions.ifWrong: If icing exposure is not credible in operation, the in-flight SF-017-TL/PL/M rows drop from Hazardous/Major toward Minor or No Safety Effect.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-017-TL (in-flight row), SF-017-PL (in-flight row), SF-017-M (in-flight row), SF-016-M2 (in-flight row)

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The crew can select ice protection manually on independent cues (visual, TAT/conditions) after loss or error of detection, providing a partial alleviation credited in the in-flight SF-017 rows.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states manual selection is available at any time but does not establish it as a timed, credited means; the class turns on how much alleviation it provides.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manual selection is not a credible alleviating means, SF-017-TL/PL could be more severe and SF-017-M's misleading case could rise above Major.

citations.quote: the system may also be selected on manually at any time

assumptions.text: The two ice detectors are of the same type and share a common-mode vulnerability, so a common error can defeat both detection and a misleading agreed indication is credible.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the common type as an item for examination but no CMA disposition exists; the SF-017-TL and SF-017-M classes assume the commonality is not yet dispositioned.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a CMA shows the detectors are effectively independent, SF-017-TL likelihood/architecture changes and the misleading-agreement case in SF-017-M weakens.

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination

assumptions.text: Crew-workload levels on these ice-protection conditions are placeholder judgements pending the human-factors workload/task analysis.
assumptions.rationale: No timed crew task or HF workload record is provided for these conditions, and this was directed to be recorded as assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the HF analysis shows higher workload (e.g. excessive workload such that the crew cannot be relied upon), the crew axis could raise SF-017-TL or SF-016-M2/SF-017-M above their proposed classes.

assumptions.ifWrong: The crew axis on those rows changes; if workload is excessive the class is unaffected (already Hazardous on the aircraft axis), if slight the crew axis is not driving the class.

assumptions.ifWrong: If independent annunciation or handling cues reliably prompt crew action, the aircraft axis drops below 'large' and SF-017-TL2/M2 fall to Major.

assumptions.text: Total loss of flight and navigation data in flight is outside the MAC (no processor, no reference unit and no standby remaining), leaving no valid flight picture.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a residual valid source remains, SF-018-TL is not hull loss and the class lowers to Major/Hazardous.

assumptions.ifWrong: If cross-comparison and alerting reliably flag misleading data in time, SF-018-M drops below hull loss and the class lowers to Hazardous or Major.

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data

assumptions.ifWrong: If the ground escape is not credited, those phases carry the in-flight end effect and their class rises.

assumptions.text: Fire/overheat detection failures produce no realised effect unless a fire or overheat also occurs, so the SF-020 loss rows are classified on the assumption that an undetected/unmanaged fire is credited as the end effect.
assumptions.rationale: Detection is a protective function; the SDD describes detection and extinguishing but the FHA must credit the fire scenario the detection loss exposes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an independent detection means or reliably timely secondary-cue detection is credited, the SF-020-TL and SF-020-TL2 classes reduce below Hazardous.

assumptions.text: Total loss of detection and undetected loss of detection are treated as latent to the extent that no reliable annunciation of total detection loss is credited beyond the annunciated single-loop degradation.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD annunciates loop loss and describes degraded single-loop logic but does not state whether complete loss of detection in a zone is annunciated as such.
assumptions.ifWrong: If total detection loss is reliably annunciated, SF-020-TL2 collapses into SF-020-TL and the latent-failure basis for its Hazardous class is removed.

citations.quote: degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.text: Total or undetected loss of fire extinguishing reaches a catastrophic outcome only in combination with a subsequent engine/APU fire the crew cannot otherwise control.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes extinguishing as a protective function; the provided inputs give no single-failure path that both defeats extinguishing and ignites a fire, so the combination must be assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single event can defeat extinguishing and cause a fire concurrently, SF-021-TL and SF-021-TL2 move from Hazardous to Catastrophic.

citations.quote: detects fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected, and provides the means to extinguish or suppress them

assumptions.ifWrong: If a single bottle loss breaks the MAC (e.g. cross-plumbing does not cover the pair), SF-021-PL escalates toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so that either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair

assumptions.text: A single inadvertent extinguisher discharge does not disable an engine or otherwise endanger the aircraft, and leaves the extinguishing MAC satisfied for the remaining coverage.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a discharge could disable an engine or break the MAC, SF-021-M moves from Major toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair

assumptions.text: Loss of crew oxygen becomes catastrophic only in combination with a subsequent depressurisation or smoke/fume event, and no single ECS/pressurisation failure makes cabin altitude untenable concurrently with the oxygen loss.

assumptions.text: No timed crew task or HF workload analysis exists for SF-022, so the crew-workload level on both rows is assumed pending that analysis.
assumptions.rationale: The turn instruction records the crew level as assumed pending HF workload, and no task-analysis data is present in the provided inputs.
assumptions.ifWrong: If HF data shows the reduced reserve or the undetected loss drives crew workload higher or lower than assumed, the crew axis and hence the derived class on the affected row changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply; Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

assumptions.text: An undetected total loss of crew oxygen co-occurs with a credible loss-of-pressurisation or smoke/fume demand during its latent exposure period, which is what makes it consequential.
assumptions.rationale: Crew oxygen is a reserve used only at a depressurisation/smoke event; the provided inputs give no latent exposure time or event co-probability, so the co-occurrence had to be assumed to classify the undetected condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the latent exposure and event co-probability are shown negligible, SF-022-TL2 would classify below Hazardous; conversely a long unchecked latency reinforces Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

citations.quote: The crew oxygen system supplies breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

assumptions.text: An UNDETECTED total loss of crew oxygen implies the continuous cylinder-pressure indication and low-pressure alerting have also failed or been defeated.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and low-pressure alerting is provided, so a genuinely undetected total loss requires the indication path to be lost as well; the inputs do not describe that combined failure explicitly.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the indication cannot fail such that a total loss is undetected, SF-022-TL2 collapses into the detected total-loss case and its class is set by that (aware) condition instead.
assumptions.usedFor: Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

citations.quote: cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting.

assumptions.text: The occupant axis is none for both rows because the aircraft carries flight crew only, provides no passenger oxygen and the hold is unoccupied in flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the hold is not occupied and there is no passenger oxygen, forcing the occupant axis to none rather than any injury level.
assumptions.ifWrong: If supernumerary occupants are ever carried, the occupant axis and the derived class would need reassessment.
assumptions.usedFor: Partial loss of crew breathing oxygen supply; Undetected loss of crew breathing oxygen supply

citations.quote: There is no passenger oxygen: the hold is not occupied in flight.

praData.csfl: Brake lines A and B share each main gear bay in adjacent bundles (recorded zonal item, SDD §5.4.5/§5.6.5); a single burst event could defeat the A/B brake-supply independence claim within that bay, and the A/B brake-line transit through zone 300 is a further common-zone point.
praData.desc: Burst of one of the 20 tyres on the six three-wheel main bogies (three per side) releases debris and flailing tread within the main gear bays (710 left / 720 right). Each bay carries brake hydraulic lines A and B in adjacent, separately clipped bundles, and the steering and brake harnesses. The A/B brake lines route out of the bays through zone 300, so a burst can propagate to the opposite-side bundle transit. Bogie/tyre count is preliminary per the SDD and debris energy is not yet substantiated.
praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread — main gear bogie (§25.734 / AC 25.734-1)
praData.systems: LDG (braking, steering); HYD A and B (brake supply); AVI (wheel speed / brake temp / WoW sensing). WoW is a fan-out signal to reversers, pressurisation and cargo restraint monitor.
praData.mitigation:
Separately clipped and shielded A/B brake bundles within each bay; free-fall alternate gear extension independent of hydraulic pressure; accumulator-supported emergency braking sized to six full applications with all three systems lost; steering and brake harnesses routed on opposite sides of each bay. Effect claim: MINIMISED (loss of one bay's A+B brake supply is degraded not total deceleration, given accumulator reserve and the 1,080 m rollout vs 1,800 m requirement margin) — to be confirmed.
Proposed requirements: • Substantiate that a main-gear tyre burst debris field cannot sever both brake hydraulic lines A and B within a single gear bay (separation / shielding of the adjacent bundles).
• Substantiate that the A/B brake-line transit through zone 300 tolerates a burst-originated debris/overheat event without common loss.
• Confirm accumulator-supported braking plus the rollout margin bounds the worst-case single-bay A+B brake loss on a semi-prepared surface.

praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are identical in type and mounted on the forward fuselage (recorded commonality item, SDD §5.10.3); a multi-bird encounter across the forward face could challenge both simultaneously. Nose visor is a single load path treated as structure with no redundancy.
praData.desc: Bird impact on forward-facing surfaces: the four engine inlets (nacelles 610–640), the upward-hinging nose visor structure (110) which forms the forward pressure boundary and structural load path when closed, and the flight deck (130). Also strikes the externally mounted probes/static ports/windshields and the two ice detectors (mounted on opposite sides of the forward fuselage). Engine ingestion energy per §33.76 is not substantiable here — the turbofan model is not yet released to engineering.
praData.threat: Bird strike — forward-facing structure, inlets and probes (§25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76)
praData.systems: PRP (inlet ingestion, thrust); IPS (two ice detectors, probe heat); AVI (pitot/static/AoA sensing, windshields); NZD/structure (nose visor pressure boundary and load path); ECS (pressure boundary integrity via visor).
praData.mitigation:
Engines are an existing certified type carrying their own §33.76 ingestion substantiation (to be confirmed once the model is released); ice detectors and probes on opposite sides of the forward fuselage give geometric separation; the integrated standby instrument shares no sensor with the primary displays. Nose visor bird-impact resistance is a structural / special-condition item (nose door as primary structure and pressure boundary). Effect claim per struck function to be confirmed — SHOWN ACCEPTABLE pending the engine ingestion evidence and visor structural substantiation.
Proposed requirements: • Substantiate engine inlet bird-ingestion tolerance per §33.76 once the turbofan model is released, and carry the result into the propulsion failure conditions.
• Substantiate the nose visor structure and pressure boundary against the §25.631 bird-strike threat as a special-condition item.
• Confirm the two same-type forward-fuselage ice detectors are not defeated by a single multi-bird forward-face encounter, or provide dissimilar detection.
• Confirm pitot/static/AoA/windshield strike does not produce common loss of primary flight and navigation data below the level protected by the independent standby instrument.

SF-017 Protect probes and detect icing
SF-018 Acquire and present flight and navigation data
SF-012 Provide nose loading access and pressure boundary closure

praData.desc: Direct attachment and swept-stroke to extremities (nose visor, wing leading edges, nacelles, empennage) with conducted/coupled transients entering the six EWS routes. Attachment at zone 110 (visor latches, lock pins, sensing harness) and 510/520 (wing box, cross-feed gallery, flammable fluid present) are the structural/ignition concerns; conducted transients propagate along the HV feeder (610,620,530,300,200), the LV signal route and the two data network channels to the fly-by-wire FCS computers, EPS bus control units, AVI reference units and the pressurisation and nose-door lock controllers.
praData.systems: FCS, EPS, AVI, ECS, NZD, IPS, FUE
praData.mitigation:
Bonding and lightning-strike protection of metallic and nonmetallic structure and extremities; transient protection at every EWS route penetration; HV/LV route separation with shielding at the two mid-equipment-bay crossing points; three FCS computers on three separate electrical sources in three bays; three data-network/reference-unit channels and an integrated standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing; fuel tank/vent bonding and ignition-source control per §25.581/§25.1316; nose-door lock sensing on two dissimilar independently routed circuits. Survivability claim: effects MINIMISED / SHOWN ACCEPTABLE pending CMA confirmation of the claimed channel independence under a common transient.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft structure and extremities shall be protected against catastrophic direct and swept-stroke lightning effects per 14CFR-25.1316 / AC 20-136B, substantiated by bonding and strike-protection analysis and test.
• The EWS shall provide transient protection at each route penetration such that a lightning-induced transient does not defeat the independence of the three fly-by-wire flight control channels.
• The fuel system tanks, vents and cross-feed gallery in zones 510/520 shall be protected against lightning ignition sources per 14CFR-25.581.
aiRequirements: The aircraft structure and extremities shall be protected against catastrophic direct and swept-stroke lightning effects per 14CFR-25.1316 / AC 20-136B, substantiated by bonding and strike-protection analysis and test.
The EWS shall provide transient protection at each route penetration such that a lightning-induced transient does not defeat the independence of the three fly-by-wire flight control channels.
The fuel system tanks, vents and cross-feed gallery in zones 510/520 shall be protected against lightning ignition sources per 14CFR-25.581.

praData.desc: External radiated electromagnetic energy coupling into the fly-by-wire and avionics backbone through apertures, wiring and equipment enclosures. The HV/LV signal routes and the two data network channels transit zones 120,200,300,400,800; the three flight control computers sit in the forward, mid and aft equipment bays (120,300,400) and the three display processing units and reference units are on the dual deterministic data network — a HIRF environment is a candidate common-mode across these nominally independent channels because it can couple to all of them simultaneously.
praData.mitigation:
HIRF protection of electrical/electronic systems performing functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous per §25.1317 / AC 20-158A: enclosure shielding, harness shielding and grounding, filtering at equipment interfaces; physical separation of the two network channels (no shared connector or penetration) and of HV/LV routes; three dissimilar FCS computers on different sources hosting dissimilar software; standby instrument on an independent route and supply. Survivability claim: effects MINIMISED / SHOWN ACCEPTABLE pending CMA confirmation that HIRF does not defeat the dissimilarity/independence argument.
Proposed requirements: • Electrical and electronic systems that perform functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the HIRF environment per 14CFR-25.1317 / AC 20-158A, verified by test and analysis.
• The two data network channels and the HV/LV signal routes shall retain adequate separation and shielding such that the HIRF environment does not defeat the independence of the three flight control channels or the standby instrument.
aiRequirements: Electrical and electronic systems that perform functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the HIRF environment per 14CFR-25.1317 / AC 20-158A, verified by test and analysis.

The two data network channels and the HV/LV signal routes shall retain adequate separation and shielding such that the HIRF environment does not defeat the independence of the three flight control channels or the standby instrument.

praData.csfl: Both same-type ice detectors (ITM-021/ITM-022) struck by a single broadside hail encounter defeats the SF-017 dual-detector independence claim; simultaneous multi-inlet hail ingestion challenges the one-engine-out dispatch case toward multi-engine effect. Forward air-data probes on the same forward fuselage are a common-cause candidate against SF-018.
praData.desc: Hail impact on forward-facing structure and inlets. Model: hail/ice mass striking the upward-hinging nose visor (Zone 110) which is both pressure boundary and forward structural load path, the four engine inlet cowls (Zones 610–640), and the wing/stabiliser leading edges (510/520/800). The two ice detectors are of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage — a broadside hail encounter is a credible common-cause on both. Debris/impact energy and stone size are preliminary/unstated and left for the analyst.
praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure and inlets
praData.systems: NZD (nose visor, Zone 110); PRP (four inlets, Zones 610–640); FCS/IPS leading-edge surfaces (510/520/800); IPS ice detectors (ITM-021 Zone 110-area left, ITM-022 right forward fuselage); AVI air-data/probes on the forward fuselage.
praData.mitigation:
Impact-resistant nose-visor skin and windshield; engine inlet/ingestion substantiation for hail; leading-edge impact tolerance; verify ice-detector siting and same-type commonality (recorded item) survives a single hail encounter; confirm forward air-data probe separation.
Proposed requirements: • The nose cargo door visor structure and pressure boundary shall withstand the certification hail impact without loss of structural load path or pressure boundary integrity.
• The engine inlets shall tolerate hail ingestion without loss of forward thrust from more than one engine.
• The two ice detectors shall be sited and/or dissimilar such that a single hail encounter does not defeat both.
• The forward air-data probes shall be separated such that a single hail encounter does not produce erroneous flight and navigation data.

The engine inlets shall tolerate hail ingestion without loss of forward thrust from more than one engine.

praData.csfl: Bleed anti-ice for both wings and all four cowls is fed from the single cross-bleed manifold in Zone 300 — a manifold-level common-mode defeats wing/cowl protection across both sides simultaneously. Two same-type ice detectors are a common-cause candidate against SF-017 detection. Shed ice into multiple inlets challenges the single-engine-out dispatch case.
praData.desc: Ice accretion/shedding. Model: accretion on unprotected or under-protected surfaces, inlets and probes within the certification icing envelope, and shed ice from the wing/nacelle re-ingested by the inboard/downstream engines. Bleed-fed wing and cowl anti-ice, six electrically-heated stabiliser zones (Zone 800), and electrically-heated probes/detectors are the functional counterpart. The certification ice envelope limits are unstated in the SDD and are left for the analyst.
praData.systems: IPS (bleed anti-ice to wings/cowls via cross-bleed manifold in Zone 300; six electrical stabiliser zones in Zone 800; heated probes and two ice detectors); PRP inlets (Zones 610–640) for shed-ice ingestion; ECS/IPS shared cross-bleed manifold; AVI probes/air-data.
praData.mitigation:
Ensure either bleed side supplies protection through the cross-bleed manifold; independently supplied and annunciated electrical stabiliser zones; individually monitored heated probes; confirm ice-detector same-type commonality (recorded item) does not create a single detection common-cause; substantiate shed-ice ingestion tolerance.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall protect the wings and engine inlets across the certification icing envelope with either bleed source available through the cross-bleed manifold.
• The two ice detectors shall not share a single failure mode that defeats icing detection in the certification envelope.
• The engine inlets shall tolerate shed-ice ingestion without loss of forward thrust from more than one engine.
• The heated probes and static ports shall be individually monitored so that loss of probe heat is detected before erroneous flight and navigation data is presented.

SF-001 Generate forward thrust — SF-001-PL partial loss (shed-ice ingestion)
SF-018 Flight and navigation data — SF-018-M erroneous flight and navigation data (blocked/iced probes)

The two ice detectors shall not share a single failure mode that defeats icing detection in the certification envelope.
The engine inlets shall tolerate shed-ice ingestion without loss of forward thrust from more than one engine.
The heated probes and static ports shall be individually monitored so that loss of probe heat is detected before erroneous flight and navigation data is presented.

praData.csfl: A hold fire in zone 300 is a common-mode threat to the mid equipment bay (FCC 2) and to the HV/LV crossing points, and to the single restraint tension loop and left-side LV signal route that transit all hold zones — defeating the independence otherwise claimed between restraint monitoring, fire detection and the affected avionics functions co-located in or routed through the hold.
praData.desc: In-flight fire or smoke in the low-differential unoccupied hold (stations 1–9). Hold has smoke detection at nine stations and NO suppression fitted; that no-suppression decision is recorded as an assumption to be substantiated (SDD §5.12.2). Fire in the mid hold (zone 300) co-locates with FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points; forward (200) and aft (400) holds house FCC 1-adjacent and FCC 3 respectively. Cross-zone propagation: the restraint tension monitoring loop (single instrumented loop, full hold length, left side) and the left-side low-voltage signal route (120,200,300,400,800) both transit all three hold zones, so a fire in any hold zone can reach restraint monitoring and LV-signal-fed functions in the others; the fuel gallery vent shares the hold zone per SDD §5.8.5.
praData.threat: Cabin/hold fire — in-flight fire or smoke originating in the unoccupied cargo hold
praData.systems: Fire Protection (FPR) — hold smoke detection; Cargo Handling & Restraint (CRG) — restraint tension loop; Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI) — FCC 2/3 and left-side LV data reached via shared hold zone
praData.mitigation:
Nine-station smoke detection along the hold length provides crew awareness (SF-020). No fire suppression is fitted in the hold — the decision rests on the hold carrying a single blade and no combustible palletised load, and is recorded as an assumption requiring substantiation (SDD §5.12.2). Survivability outcome to be established: this study cannot yet claim the effect is ELIMINATED, MINIMISED or SHOWN ACCEPTABLE for the hold — the no-suppression decision is the open item. Flammable-fluid-carrying components in fire-exposed areas are governed by 14CFR-25.1183; §25.855 governs cargo compartment fire protection. Candidate mitigations: substantiate the no-suppression case against §25.855 cargo-compartment classification; assess separation/shielding of the restraint tension loop and left-side LV route from a hold fire source; assess FCC 2 installation in zone 300 against a hold fire.
Proposed requirements: • The cargo hold fire protection provision shall be substantiated against the applicable cargo compartment classification of §25.855, including the decision not to fit hold suppression.
• The restraint tension monitoring loop and the left-side low-voltage signal route shall be separated, segregated or shielded from a hold fire source such that a single hold fire does not defeat restraint monitoring and the affected avionics functions simultaneously.
aiRequirements: The cargo hold fire protection provision shall be substantiated against the applicable cargo compartment classification of §25.855, including the decision not to fit hold suppression.

The restraint tension monitoring loop and the left-side low-voltage signal route shall be separated, segregated or shielded from a hold fire source such that a single hold fire does not defeat restraint monitoring and the affected avionics functions simultaneously.

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — unpressurised when open, pressure boundary when closed. Houses the 12 rotary latches on a common torque shaft, 8 lock pins on a separate actuator/supply, the lock actuator and the pin-position sensing harness. Nose door lock sensing harness transits 110→120→130.
zsaData.equip: Visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, lock sensing harness (SF-012 nose loading access / pressure boundary closure)
zsaData.mitigation: Pins on a separate actuator and separate hydraulic supply so latches cannot back-drive while pins engaged; dual dissimilar independently-routed lock sensing (proximity harness + mechanical indicator linkage) crossing at two separated bulkhead penetrations; pressure interlock in series with unlock command confirming <0.1 psi residual differential; verify latch/pin rig and sensing independence at installation.
zsaData.interference: Common torque shaft driving all 12 latches is a single mechanical path; sensing harness and door actuation power co-transit toward zone 120/130; inadvertent loss of pressure boundary closure in flight is classified Catastrophic at aircraft level (SF-012-M).

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned. Houses FCC 1 (flight control computer, forward bay), oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks. Low-voltage signal route and data network channels originate/transit here; nose door lock sensing harness transits.
zsaData.equip: FCC 1, crew oxygen HP cylinders, forward avionics racks; ADIRU/DPU racks (SF-005/006/007 FCS via FCC, SF-018 flight & nav data, SF-022 crew oxygen)
zsaData.mitigation: Cylinders installed outside any zone containing a high-energy electrical source per SDD 5.13.5 — CONFIRM against final rack layout; O2 supply line routed clear of HV feeder route; three FCCs in three separate bays preserve FCS independence; thermal discharge indicator on skin for cylinder overpressure; materials-compatibility and cleanliness controls for the O2 installation.
zsaData.interference: Co-location of a high-pressure oxygen cylinder with avionics/electrical racks — oxygen-enriched environment adjacent to potential ignition source; FCC 1 is one of three dissimilar computers in three separate bays, so bay-local damage must not defeat the other two.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied. Houses displays, inceptors, the independent integrated standby instrument, the fire handles and the crew oxygen masks. Nose door lock sensing terminates here at the flight-deck bulkhead penetrations.
zsaData.equip: Displays, inceptors, standby instrument (DC essential), fire handles, crew O2 masks (SF-018 indication, SF-019 alerting, SF-021 fire extinguish command, SF-022 oxygen)
zsaData.mitigation: Standby instrument wired directly to DC essential on a route independent of primary display feeders (SDD 5.11.5); quick-donning full-face masks with smoke goggles at four stations; fire handles hardwired; lock status permanently displayed; verify display-feeder vs standby-feeder separation at the bulkhead.
zsaData.interference: Concentration of crew-interface controls in one occupied zone; standby instrument must share no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays; smoke/fume ingress affects the only occupied station.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold, stations 1–3 — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 1–3, restraint straps, the restraint tension monitoring loop and smoke detectors. HV feeder left/right, LV signal, data channels, HYD C run and the restraint loop transit this zone.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension monitoring loop, hold smoke detectors (SF-013 payload restraint, SF-020 fire/overheat detection)
zsaData.mitigation: Two tension straps per saddle with load paths sized so loss of one strap is carried by neighbours; loss on two adjacent stations annunciated as restraint condition; loop routed above floor line, left side; smoke detection at nine stations; substantiate the no-hold-suppression decision (SDD 5.12.2) as a Cabin Fire particular-risk item; separation of restraint loop from fuel vent and electrical route to be verified.
zsaData.interference: Single instrumented restraint tension loop shares the hold zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (SDD 5.8.5); loss of payload restraint of a 72.6 t single blade is Catastrophic (SF-013-TL); hold has smoke detection but NO suppression (recorded assumption to be substantiated).

zsaData.desc: Mid hold, stations 4–6 — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 4–6, the mid equipment bay, FCC 2, and the HV/LV crossing points. This is the aircraft's principal commonality zone: fuel feed gallery, HYD A+B wing-root run, HYD C run, brake lines A/B, both HV feeders, LV routes, data channels, bleed cross-bleed manifold and the two HV↔LV crossings all transit here.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points; transiting fuel gallery, HYD A/B/C, bleed cross-bleed manifold (SF-013 restraint; FCS, HYD, FUE, ECS, IPS routing)
zsaData.mitigation: HV/LV separation maintained with only two identified crossing points replaced by shielding + defined minimum distance; HYD C routed separately from A/B; data channels on opposite sides with no shared connector; FCC 2 one of three separated bays; flag HYD A/B shared wing-root run + fuel gallery + cross-bleed as CMA candidates feeding the affected fault trees; verify minimum separations at the two HV↔LV crossings.
zsaData.interference: Highest co-location density on the aircraft: the single spanwise fuel cross-feed gallery, the HYD A+B shared wing-root run, both HV feeders, and the cross-bleed manifold all pass through one zone — a single zonal event here could defeat multiple nominally independent redundancies (candidate common-cause contributor to affected fault trees per ARP4761A).

zsaData.desc: Aft hold, stations 7–9 — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 7–9, the aft equipment bay and FCC 3. HYD C run, LV signal, data channels and the restraint tension loop transit.
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3 (SF-013 restraint; FCS via FCC 3, flight/nav data routing)
zsaData.mitigation: Two straps per saddle with redundant load paths; FCC 3 in a bay separate from FCC 1 (120) and FCC 2 (300); HYD C routed separately from A/B along the opposite side; verify tension-loop and FCC 3 feeder independence.
zsaData.interference: Loss of restraint at aft stations of a full-length blade; FCC 3 completes the three-bay separation of the flight control computers, so aft-bay damage must not coincide with a mid/forward bay loss.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present (representative; 520 right is mirrored). Houses fuel tanks, the cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route. Fuel feed gallery and wing anti-ice ducting transit.
zsaData.equip: Wing fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice bleed ducting, outboard electrical route (SF-003 fuel feed, SF-016 ice protection)
zsaData.mitigation: Wing anti-ice ducting separated from the outboard electrical route by a shielded partition along the full run (SDD 5.10.5); tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses; bonding and lightning/HIRF protection per §25.581/§25.1316/§25.1317; verify shielded-partition integrity and electrical-to-fuel separation. Mirror findings apply to zone 520.
zsaData.interference: Flammable fluid co-located with hot bleed anti-ice ducting and an electrical route in the leading edge; ignition-source proximity to fuel/vapour; a fuel-tank ignition is a well-known hazard extending beyond the zone (Lightning, HIRF, Engine/Rotor Burst bearing).

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit (representative; 540 right is mirrored). Houses the HYD A and B wing-root run, a bleed duct penetration and HV feeder transit. HYD A+B run, HV feeders left, bleed ducts and wing anti-ice ducting transit.
zsaData.equip: HYD A + HYD B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit (HYD supply to FCS/LDG/NZD, ECS/IPS bleed)
zsaData.mitigation: No two hydraulic systems share a wing-root PENETRATION even though A/B share the run; bleed ducts cross at separated penetrations; ECS duct kept clear of HV feeder with minimum separation maintained (SDD 5.9.5); record HYD A/B shared run as a dedicated CMA item feeding the FCS/LDG fault trees; verify separation at the penetrations. Mirror findings apply to zone 540.
zsaData.interference: HYD A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (SDD 5.3.5 / 5.4.5) — a co-location that is a claim about independence to be TESTED, not assumed; hot bleed duct and HV feeder pass the same pressure-boundary region.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 — designated fire zone; high energy, flammable fluid (representative; 620/630/640 mirrored, inboard nacelles 620/630 also house thrust reversers). Houses the engine, FADEC, generator, engine-driven pump, dual fire detection loops and extinguisher plumbing. HV feeder and bleed ducts originate here.
zsaData.equip: Engine, FADEC (dual channel), 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump, dual fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SF-001 forward thrust, SF-002 reverse thrust on inboard nacelles)
zsaData.mitigation: Complete drainage of each part of the fire zone and ventilation to prevent flammable-vapour accumulation per §25.1181/§29.1187; dual-loop continuous detection routed separately with AND logic degrading to single-loop; two bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed; fire handle isolation; FADEC channels on four different power sources so no single bus loss affects >1 engine; burst-debris trajectories handed to the Rotor/Engine Burst PRA. Mirror findings apply to nacelles 620/630/640.
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181(a)(1)/(2)/(6) with flammable fluid and ignition sources; uncontained rotor/engine burst can release high-energy debris beyond the nacelle affecting adjacent structure, fuel and other systems (Rotor Burst / Engine Burst bearing, PRA-owned as it extends beyond the zone).

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted (representative; 720 right is mirrored). Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, and steering/brake harnesses. Brake hydraulic lines A/B transit 710→720→300.
zsaData.equip: Three main bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, steering and brake electrical harnesses (SF-009 ground load support, SF-010 ground deceleration, SF-011 ground directional control)
zsaData.mitigation: A/B brake lines separately clipped and shielded though sharing the bay; steering and braking electrical harnesses routed on opposite sides of each bay; overheat detection fitted to the bays; free-fall alternate extension independent of hydraulic pressure; accumulator-supported emergency braking (six applications); tyre-burst debris trajectories handed to the Tire Burst PRA; verify A/B bundle clipping and shielding. Mirror findings apply to zone 720.
zsaData.interference: Brake lines A and B run through the same gear bay in adjacent bundles (SDD 5.6.5) — co-location of the normal and alternate brake supplies; tyre burst / flailing tread can damage co-located lines and harnesses within the bay (Tire Burst bearing); overheat/brake-fire potential.

zsaData.desc: Nose gear bay — unpressurised. Houses the nose unit, the steering actuator and the tow disconnect.
zsaData.equip: Nose gear unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect (SF-009 ground load support, SF-011 ground directional control)
zsaData.mitigation: Mechanical disconnect for towing with defined re-connect procedure; independent dual downlock sensing per unit; tyre-burst debris handed to the Tire Burst PRA; inspect tow-disconnect state and steering rig at turnaround.
zsaData.interference: Steering actuator and tow disconnect co-located; tyre burst from the twin-wheel nose unit can damage steering/sensing in the bay (Tire Burst bearing); tow-disconnect mis-set is a maintenance/servicing error.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed environment; APU compartment is a designated fire zone. Houses the rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders and the APU compartment. Rudder control runs, LV signal and data channels transit.
zsaData.equip: Rudder upper/lower control runs, stabiliser heater feeders (six IPS zones), APU and its fire detection/extinguishing (SF-007 yaw control, SF-016 ice protection)
zsaData.mitigation: Upper and lower rudder segment runs routed on opposite sides of the aft fuselage (SDD 5.3.5) on independent hydraulic supplies (A and B); stabiliser heater feeders routed opposite the rudder runs; APU dual-loop detection with single dedicated bottle discharged automatically when unattended; APU compartment drainage and ventilation per §25.1181/§29.1187; automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation on APU fire; verify rudder-run and heater-feeder separation.
zsaData.interference: APU compartment is a designated fire zone per §25.1181(a)(4) with flammable fluid; rudder control runs and stabiliser heater feeders share the aft fuselage — split-rudder segment independence must survive a local aft-fuselage event; total loss of yaw control is Catastrophic (SF-007-TL).

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent failure of the four podded turbofans and their per-engine generator/EDP/FADEC feeds underpins the AND-gate independence for SF-001-TL.. At least one engine of the left pair (ITM-001/ITM-002) remains available, failing independently of the right pair, so complete loss of forward thrust generation requires independent loss of both branches.
cmaData.subject: MAC-BRCH SF-001-TL — {Eng 1 (ITM-001) left-outboard branch} of the forward-thrust survival claim
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common engine type — single certified turbofan of the 330 kN class across all four positions (design/software/material commonality) | A latent type-level design or in-service defect could affect all four engines within a short interval, defeating the AND | Mitigating: staggered in-service exposure; NO dissimilarity between positions — design-level common cause remains; belongs in the tree as a common-cause contributor across the four-engine set.
(2) Single spanwise fuel cross-feed gallery through wing box (zones 510/530/300/540/520) — the only path from one wing to opposite engines | A gallery/manifold fault or a zone-300 event can starve engines on both sides, coupling left and right branches | Mitigating: dedicated collector cells, paired boost pumps and gravity feed below FL150; the gallery is a recorded single-run particular-risk/zonal item — residual coupling in zone 300.
(3) Common environment — zone 300 mid-hold commonality zone transited by fuel gallery, HV feeders, LV, data | A single zonal event in 300 can reach multiple engine-feed/control paths | Mitigating: left/right feeders on opposite sides, HV/LV separated except two shielded crossings; residual co-transit in 300.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the four-engine set with an explicit common-cause contributor for shared engine type/design; retain the fuel cross-feed gallery and zone-300 commonality as particular-risk/zonal items feeding the SF-001-TL tree rather than a bare AND of independent engines.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The four FADEC power feeds shall be arranged so that no single bus loss affects more than one engine (per SDD §5.1.5 — verify).
• Left and right engine fuel/hydraulic/electrical services shall not be commingled outboard of the wing root.
• A common-cause contributor representing shared engine type/design shall be included explicitly in the SF-001-TL fault tree.

aiRequirements: The four FADEC power feeds shall be arranged so that no single bus loss affects more than one engine (per SDD §5.1.5 — verify).
Left and right engine fuel/hydraulic/electrical services shall not be commingled outboard of the wing root.
A common-cause contributor representing shared engine type/design shall be included explicitly in the SF-001-TL fault tree.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent failure of the right-pair turbofans and their per-engine generator/EDP/FADEC feeds underpins the AND-gate independence for SF-001-TL.. At least one engine of the right pair (ITM-003/ITM-004) remains available, failing independently of the left pair, so complete loss of forward thrust generation requires independent loss of both branches.
cmaData.subject: MAC-BRCH SF-001-TL — {Eng 3 (ITM-003) right-inboard branch} of the forward-thrust survival claim
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common engine type across all four positions (single certified turbofan, model not yet released) | A type-level defect couples right-pair engines to the left pair, defeating the four-engine AND | Mitigating: no dissimilarity; design-level common cause must be modelled explicitly.
(2) Single spanwise fuel cross-feed gallery through the wing box | A gallery or zone-300 fault feeds fuel starvation to right-inboard as well as left engines | Mitigating: dedicated collectors, paired boost pumps, gravity feed <FL150; single-run gallery retained as PRA/ZSA item.
(3) Zone 300 (mid hold, FCC 2, HV/LV crossings) shared transit | A single zonal event reaches multiple engine feed/control routes | Mitigating: opposite-side left/right routing, HV/LV separated except two shielded crossings; residual co-transit in 300.
cmaData.mitigation:
Include an explicit common-cause contributor for shared engine type/design across the four-engine set; carry the fuel cross-feed gallery and zone-300 commonality as particular-risk/zonal items in the SF-001-TL tree.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Right-pair engine fuel/hydraulic/electrical services shall not be commingled with the left side outboard of the wing root.
• A common-cause contributor for shared engine type/design shall appear explicitly in the SF-001-TL fault tree.

aiRequirements: Right-pair engine fuel/hydraulic/electrical services shall not be commingled with the left side outboard of the wing root.
A common-cause contributor for shared engine type/design shall appear explicitly in the SF-001-TL fault tree.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent failure of the two inboard-engine thrust reversers and their deploy/inhibit control underpins the AND-gate independence for SF-002-TL.. At least one inboard-engine reverser (ITM-005/ITM-006) remains available, failing independently of the other, so total loss of ground reverse thrust requires independent loss of both reversers.
cmaData.subject: MAC-BRCH SF-002-TL — {Thrust reverser — engine 2 (ITM-005)} branch of the ground reverse-thrust survival claim
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common deploy/inhibit design — both reversers inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical translating-sleeve lock | A common design fault or common WoW/radio-altimeter signal loss could inhibit or fail both reversers together | Mitigating: mechanical lock at the sleeve is independent of the electrical inhibit; commonality of the WoW/radio-altimeter agreement logic remains to be examined.
(2) Common engine type for the two host inboard engines (ITM-002/ITM-003) | A host-engine type defect that shuts down both inboard engines removes both reversers | Mitigating: reverse thrust is a ground deceleration supplement; braking/deceleration functions provide alternate means (SF-010).
(3) WoW discrete source shared with many consumers (per SDD §5.6.4) | A common weight-on-wheels fault denies the deploy permit to both reversers | Mitigating: reverser deployment requires WoW AND radio-altimeter agreement — dual discrete path; residual commonality in shared WoW.
cmaData.mitigation:
Examine commonality of the weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter deploy/inhibit logic across the two reversers and, where shared, model it as a common-cause contributor in the SF-002-TL tree rather than a bare AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverser deploy-permit logic shall be evaluated for common-cause coupling of the weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement signals between the two inboard reversers.
• A common-cause contributor for the shared deploy/inhibit design shall be represented in the SF-002-TL fault tree where commonality is confirmed.

aiRequirements: The reverser deploy-permit logic shall be evaluated for common-cause coupling of the weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement signals between the two inboard reversers.
A common-cause contributor for the shared deploy/inhibit design shall be represented in the SF-002-TL fault tree where commonality is confirmed.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Reverse thrust is provided only by the two inboard engines (ITM-005, ITM-006); their reverser deployment logic and the AVI deploy-permission (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement) are asserted to be independent between sides.. The Propulsion contribution and the Avionics & Flight Deck contribution to total loss of ground reverse thrust fail independently.
cmaData.subject: SF-002-TL · PRP ∧ AVI independence for total loss of ground reverse thrust
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — EPS: both inboard FADEC channels and the reverser control draw AC/DC from the shared electrical system; both AVI processing channels are EPS-supplied. Common Resources — data/AVI: reverser deployment is inhibited/permitted by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement supplied through the avionics network; a common erroneous WOW or radio-altimeter source could couple both reversers. Installation — zone 300: both HV feeders, LV signal and both data network channels transit the mid-hold commonality zone, where a single zonal event could affect the deploy-permission path to both reversers. Common design: the two inboard reversers and their translating-sleeve locks are of common part number.
cmaData.mitigation:
FADEC channels take power from four different sources so no single bus loss affects more than one engine (per SDD §5.1.5); reverser deployment requires WOW and radio-altimeter agreement plus a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve; data network channels 1 and 2 are on opposite sides with no shared connector or penetration. Residual: shared WOW/radio-altimeter data and EPS remain to be shown non-coupling.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The reverse-thrust deploy-permission (weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement) shall be derived from independent, dissimilar sources such that no single erroneous source can enable or inhibit both inboard reversers.
• The electrical supplies to the two inboard reverser control paths shall be segregated such that no single bus loss affects both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): OPEN — confirm in SSA: (a) independence of the WOW and radio-altimeter data feeding both reversers; (b) EPS bus segregation across the two inboard reverser control paths; (c) zone 300 zonal analysis for the deploy-permission routing.

aiRequirements: The reverse-thrust deploy-permission (weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement) shall be derived from independent, dissimilar sources such that no single erroneous source can enable or inhibit both inboard reversers.
The electrical supplies to the two inboard reverser control paths shall be segregated such that no single bus loss affects both.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Reverse thrust redundancy is the two inboard reversers ITM-005 (engine 2) and ITM-006 (engine 3), each with its own engine, FADEC and hydraulic drive.. The two inboard reverser/engine channels (engine 2 / engine 3) fail independently for total loss of ground reverse thrust.
cmaData.subject: SF-002-TL · PRP inboard-reverser redundancy independence
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — hydraulic/pneumatic: reverser actuation motive power source is not stated per side and requires confirmation. Common design/manufacturing: both inboard reversers are of a common part number and translating-sleeve lock design; a common design or manufacturing-lot defect could disable both. Common Resources — EPS: reverser control electronics are EPS-supplied. Installation — left/right engine pairs sit in separate zones (610/620 vs 630/640) and services are not commingled outboard of the wing root, which supports side-to-side physical independence.
cmaData.mitigation:
Left and right engine pairs sit in separate zones; fuel, hydraulic and electrical services to each engine routed through the corresponding pylon and not commingled with the opposite side outboard of the wing root (SDD §5.1.5). Residual: common part number / common design of the two inboard reversers.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Common-cause exposure of the two inboard thrust reversers (common part number, translating-sleeve lock design) shall be assessed and, where a DAL reduction rests on their independence, an explicit common-cause contributor shall be carried in the fault tree.
Verification (SSA/ASA): OPEN — confirm in SSA: reverser motive-power source per side; manufacturing-lot / overhaul-interval staggering for the two inboard reversers.

aiRequirements: Common-cause exposure of the two inboard thrust reversers (common part number, translating-sleeve lock design) shall be assessed and, where a DAL reduction rests on their independence, an explicit common-cause contributor shall be carried in the fault tree.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The MAC rule for SF-014 requires at least 1 of { ITM-015, ITM-016 }; the two packs are asserted redundant for flight-deck conditioning and hold air supply.. Air cycle pack 1 (ITM-015) and pack 2 (ITM-016) fail independently, so that loss of the pair (the SF-014 Minimum Acceptable Configuration breach) requires two independent failures.
cmaData.subject: SF-014-TL · Air cycle pack 1 ∧ pack 2 independence (MAC breach)
cmaData.findings: Common Resources — bleed/pneumatic: both packs are supplied through a single cross-bleed manifold with isolation valves in zone 300; a manifold or cross-bleed common-cause defeats the pair. Common Resources — EPS: both packs and their fans/controllers are EPS-supplied. Installation — zone 300: the mid-hold is the principal commonality zone through which the bleed cross-bleed manifold transits; a single zonal event there could affect both pack supplies. Common design/manufacturing: the two packs are of common part number.
cmaData.mitigation:
Cross-bleed manifold permits either pack to be supplied from either side (SDD §5.9.2), which mitigates loss of one bleed source but is itself the shared element for a manifold-level failure. Single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule. Residual: the shared cross-bleed manifold and shared EPS are common resources to both packs.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The bleed supply to the two air cycle packs shall be arranged such that no single cross-bleed manifold failure defeats both packs, or the common-cause contribution of the shared manifold shall be carried explicitly in the SF-014-TL fault tree.
• The electrical supplies to the two air cycle packs shall be segregated such that no single bus loss defeats both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): OPEN — confirm in SSA: (a) cross-bleed manifold single-failure exposure to both packs; (b) EPS bus segregation across pack 1 and pack 2; (c) zone 300 zonal analysis covering the cross-bleed manifold.

aiRequirements: The bleed supply to the two air cycle packs shall be arranged such that no single cross-bleed manifold failure defeats both packs, or the common-cause contribution of the shared manifold shall be carried explicitly in the SF-014-TL fault tree.
The electrical supplies to the two air cycle packs shall be segregated such that no single bus loss defeats both.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the redundant pressurisation controllers underpinning MAC clause {min 1 of ITM-017, ITM-018}.. The two pressurisation controllers fail independently, so total loss of cabin pressure control (SF-015-TL) requires both to fail.
cmaData.subject: SF-015 cabin pressure control — dual pressurisation controllers (ITM-017 ∧ ITM-018)
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common resource — Electrical Power (EPS): both controllers consume EPS, which the SDD states "Supplies all systems"; the SDD does not state the two controllers are fed from distinct/segregated buses | A common bus loss could disable both controllers, defeating the AND | Not grounded — bus allocation of ITM-017/018 not stated; open independence requirement.
(2) Common design/software: SDD describes "two digital controllers" of apparently the same type, with no dissimilarity argument stated | A common specification/software/hardware error could fail both | No dissimilarity claim in the SDD; unmitigated as documented — mechanical relief and pneumatic backup mode mitigate the outcome, not the controller commonality.
(3) Common environment (Installation): both controllers likely co-located; installation not detailed | Shared thermal/EMI/HIRF exposure | Not grounded.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independent pneumatic backup mode drives one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure, and positive/negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system (per SDD §5.9.2). These mitigate the SF-015-TL OUTCOME but do NOT restore controller independence.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two pressurisation controllers shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both (independence requirement, development/PSSA).
• A dissimilarity or common-mode error argument shall be established for the two digital pressurisation controllers, or the SF-015-TL AND-gate credit shall not rest on their independence.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the redundant outflow valves underpinning MAC clause {min 1 of ITM-019, ITM-020}.. The two outflow valves fail independently, so total loss of cabin pressure control (SF-015-TL) requires both to fail.
cmaData.subject: SF-015 cabin pressure control — dual outflow valves (ITM-019 ∧ ITM-020)
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common resource — Electrical Power (EPS) to the valves: SDD lists "electrical power to the controllers, valves and fans" as an ECS input; distinct-source allocation of the two valves not stated | A common bus loss could freeze both valves | Not grounded — open independence requirement.
(2) Common design: "two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient" — apparently identical valves | A common specification/manufacturing/lot deficiency could fail both | No dissimilarity or lot-segregation claim stated.
(3) Common environment/installation: both valves in the pressure shell, likely co-located aft; installation not detailed | Shared environment could strike both | Not grounded.
cmaData.mitigation:
Pneumatic backup mode drives one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure, and independent mechanical positive/negative relief protects the structure (per SDD §5.9.2) — outcome mitigations, not valve-independence restorers.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two outflow valves shall be electrically supplied and commanded such that no single source or channel loss disables both (independence requirement, development/PSSA).
• Common-mode susceptibility of the two identical outflow valves (design, manufacturing lot, calibration/maintenance action) shall be assessed and mitigated before the SF-015-TL AND-gate credit is taken.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the redundant ice detectors underpinning MAC clause {min 1 of ITM-021, ITM-022}.. The two ice detectors fail independently, so total loss of icing detection (SF-017-TL) requires both to fail.
cmaData.subject: SF-017 icing detection / probe protection — dual ice detectors (ITM-021 ∧ ITM-022)
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common design — SAME TYPE: SDD states "two ice detectors of the same type" and "their commonality is recorded as an item for examination" | A common specification/hardware/calibration deficiency could fail both simultaneously | Explicitly flagged by the SDD as an unresolved commonality — unmitigated as documented.
(2) Common environment: both are electrically heated and installed "on opposite sides of the forward fuselage" — opposite sides gives some separation, but both share the same forward-fuselage icing, HIRF, lightning and bird-strike environment (all applicable particular risks) | A shared icing/environmental condition, or a common icing-envelope blind spot in the detector type, could defeat both | Left/right separation mitigates a single localized event; it does NOT mitigate a common-design blind spot or a fleet-wide environmental condition.
(3) Common resource — electrical heating power (EPS) to the two detectors: distinct-source allocation not stated | Common heater-power loss could disable both | Not grounded — open independence requirement.
cmaData.mitigation:
The two detectors are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (spatial separation) and the system "may also be selected on manually at any time," giving a crew-selectable independent path around the automatic-detection function (per SDD §5.10.2).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The common-design susceptibility of the two same-type ice detectors shall be assessed (e.g., dissimilar detection principle, or crew procedure independent of automatic detection) before the SF-017-TL AND-gate credit rests on their independence.
• The two ice detectors shall be supplied with heating/electrical power from independent sources such that no single source loss disables both (independence requirement, development/PSSA).
