The two ice detectors shall be supplied with heating/electrical power from independent sources such that no single source loss disables both (independence requirement, development/PSSA).

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual continuous fire/overheat detection loops per zone, routed on opposite sides and separately clipped, with AND logic for warning degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop.. Within each engine-nacelle pair and the APU compartment, detection loops A and B fail independently, so at least one loop remains available (MAC SF-020: 1-of-2 per zone).
cmaData.subject: Fire & overheat detection loop A / loop B independence (SF-020-TL) — dual-loop detection per nacelle (610-640) and APU compartment (zone 800)
cmaData.findings: Common Environment — the monitored volume is a designated fire zone (high energy, flammable fluid); an in-zone fire or overheat is a shared harsh environment that can attack both loops before warning | Effect: the very condition detection exists to sense can degrade both loops together | Mitigating factor: loops routed on opposite sides of the zone and separately clipped (per SDD §5.12.5). Common Resource (power) — detection is supplied from the DC essential bus per SDD §5.12.4 | Effect: loss of DC essential defeats both loops in a zone simultaneously | Mitigating factor: DC essential is the aircraft's final electrical resort with battery backing (SDD §5.5.2); no independent second supply to loop B is stated. Design/Detection logic — degradation to single-loop logic on loss of one loop | Effect: a first, undetected loop failure removes the AND vote and leaves the zone on a single loop, a latent contributor to total loss | Mitigating factor: loss of a loop is annunciated (single-loop degraded logic is a designed reversion, not a silent one). Common Design — the two loops are the same continuous-detection type | Effect: a shared design or material deficiency in the sensing element could affect both loops | Mitigating factor: not stated in the SDD; dissimilarity between loops A and B is not claimed.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain opposite-side routing and separate clipping per zone (SDD §5.12.5) as verified independence provisions; confirm loop A and loop B do not share the single DC essential supply, or model the shared supply as a common-cause contributor in the SF-020-TL tree; confirm loss-of-loop annunciation drives a maintenance action bounding the latent single-loop exposure interval.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fire detection installation shall route loop A and loop B of each monitored zone on physically separated paths, separately clipped, such that no single localised event disables both loops.
• The fire detection design shall bound the latent exposure to single-loop operation following an annunciated loss of one loop by a defined maintenance action interval.
• The applicant shall substantiate that loss of the DC essential bus is either not a single common cause of both detection loops in a zone, or is modelled as an explicit common-cause contributor to SF-020-TL.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to verify, against the as-built installation and ZSA for zones 610-640 and 800: (a) opposite-side routing and separate clipping of loops A/B in each zone; (b) the power source(s) feeding loop A vs loop B and whether they share the DC essential bus; (c) that single-loop degraded logic is annunciated and dispositioned by procedure; (d) whether loops A and B share a common detection-element design/lot such that a common-cause event belongs in the tree.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Loops A and B routed on opposite sides of the zone and separately clipped, with AND warning logic degrading to single-loop.. The two continuous fire-detection loops in each engine nacelle fail independently, so a 1-of-2 minimum holds for SF-020-TL.
cmaData.subject: SF-020 engine fire detection — loop A/B independence per nacelle (MAC-BRCH, 1-of-2 per engine pair)
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Common electrical resource — both loops supplied from DC essential bus | loss of DC essential defeats both loops simultaneously | opposite-side routing does not separate the supply; DC essential is a single common resource. (2) Common environment — both loops installed inside the same nacelle fire zone (610–640, high energy / flammable fluid) | a severe nacelle fire or overheat can damage both same-zone loops before warning | separate clipping limits but does not eliminate a zonal fire striking both; reconcile with ZSA (zone 610 worst severity Catastrophic). (3) Common design / part type — loops A and B are the same detection technology | a common design or manufacturing-lot deficiency latently disables both | dual-loop AND logic and separate routing address random but not systematic common-mode.
cmaData.mitigation:
Opposite-side separate routing and clipping of loops A/B (§5.12.5); AND-then-single-loop warning logic. Common DC-essential supply and common part type remain unmitigated at this level.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fire detection loops A and B of each engine nacelle shall be substantiated to survive the zonal fire/overheat environment such that no single zonal event defeats both loops (verify against ZSA zone 610–640).
• A common-cause contributor for the shared DC essential bus supply and the common detection part type shall be represented in the SF-020-TL fault tree rather than a bare AND of the two loops.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm loop A/B physical separation as-installed and the DC-essential common-supply contributor is modeled; ZSA cross-check that a nacelle fire does not defeat both loops.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Loops A and B routed on opposite sides of the APU compartment and separately clipped, AND warning logic degrading to single-loop.. The two continuous fire-detection loops in the APU compartment fail independently, so a 1-of-2 minimum holds for SF-020-TL.
cmaData.subject: SF-020 APU fire detection — loop A/B independence in the APU compartment (MAC-BRCH, 1-of-2)
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Common electrical resource — both APU loops supplied from DC essential bus | loss of DC essential defeats both loops | opposite-side routing does not separate the common supply. (2) Common environment — both loops inside the single APU compartment (zone 800, designated fire zone) | an APU fire can damage both loops in the one enclosed fire zone | opposite-side routing is the only separation and both remain within the same compartment. (3) Common design / part type — identical loop technology to the engine loops | systematic common-mode disables both | AND logic addresses random not systematic faults.
cmaData.mitigation:
Opposite-side separate routing/clipping of the two APU loops (§5.12.5); AND-then-single-loop logic; automatic APU discharge on ground. Common DC-essential supply and single-compartment co-location remain.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The APU compartment fire-detection loops A and B shall be substantiated to survive the APU-compartment fire environment such that no single event defeats both loops.
• The shared DC essential bus supply to both APU detection loops shall be represented as a common-cause contributor in the SF-020-TL fault tree.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm APU loop A/B separation as-installed within zone 800 and that the DC-essential common-supply contributor is modeled; reconcile with the APU-compartment fire zone in ZSA.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair.. The two extinguisher bottles per engine pair fail/discharge independently, so a 1-of-2 minimum holds for SF-021-TL.
cmaData.subject: SF-021 fire extinguishing — bottle-pair independence per engine pair (MAC-BRCH, 1-of-2 bottles cross-plumbed)
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence :: (1) Common electrical resource — both bottles' discharge circuits supplied from the hot battery bus | loss of the hot battery bus prevents discharge of both bottles of the pair | hot-battery-bus supply is chosen for survivability with generation lost, but is itself a single common resource to both circuits. (2) Common plumbing path — bottles are cross-plumbed into a shared discharge manifold per pair | a blockage/rupture in the shared cross-plumbing defeats both bottles into a nacelle | cross-plumbing provides coverage flexibility but introduces a shared physical path. (3) Common design / part type — the two bottles per pair are the same type | a systematic charge/squib/valve defect disables both | independent squibs per bottle mitigate random but not common-lot faults.
cmaData.mitigation:
Two bottles per pair with cross-plumbing (§5.12.2); discharge circuits on the hot battery bus for availability with all generation lost (§5.12.4). Shared hot-battery-bus supply and shared cross-plumbing manifold remain as couplings.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The shared hot battery bus supply to both discharge circuits of an engine-pair shall be represented as a common-cause contributor in the SF-021-TL fault tree rather than a bare AND of the two bottles.
• The cross-plumbed discharge path per engine pair shall be substantiated so that a single blockage or rupture does not defeat discharge to the affected nacelle.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA to confirm the hot-battery-bus common-supply contributor and the shared cross-plumbing path are modeled in SF-021-TL; verify squib/valve independence and part-lot controls.

cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed so either bottle can discharge into either nacelle of the pair; independent APU bottle.. Within each engine pair the two cross-plumbed bottles fail independently, so at least one bottle remains available to discharge into either nacelle of the pair.
cmaData.subject: SF-021 fire-extinguishing bottle-pair redundancy (MAC clauses: eng 1/2 pair ITM-044/045, eng 3/4 pair ITM-046/047, APU ITM-048)
cmaData.findings: DEVELOPMENT-phase CMA (supports PSSA independence requirement for SF-021-TL). Concern | Effect on the principle | Mitigating factor or lack of independence. (1) Common discharge electrical bus — both bottles of a pair discharge from the hot battery bus | a hot-battery-bus loss removes discharge to both bottles of the pair simultaneously | SDD: 'Discharge circuits are supplied from the hot battery bus'; hot battery bus is retained to survive all generation loss, but it is a single shared resource across both bottles — independence deficiency, DAL reduction resting on bottle pairing is not assured. (2) Common crew command path — discharge is a single crew action through the fire handle for the pair | a fire-handle / command-path fault defeats discharge of both bottles | SDD: 'Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles' — shared command is a common-cause contributor. (3) Common design / part number — the two bottles of a pair are of the same type | a common charge-loss, squib or valve design/lot defect fails both | not grounded in SDD whether bottles are dissimilar or single part number — recorded as an item to substantiate. (4) Common installation zone — cross-plumbing manifold and both bottles co-located in the same nacelle-pair installation | a local event (rotor burst, engine burst, fire) striking the shared plumbing defeats the pair | reconcile with PRA rotor/engine burst — a burst in one nacelle of the pair could sever the cross-plumbing to both.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain hot-battery-bus supply to discharge circuits and substantiate its independence from other loads; provide independent or dual command paths for the pair discharge; establish bottle dissimilarity or staggered lots/maintenance to break common design/lot cause; route cross-plumbing to withstand or be shielded from single-nacelle rotor/engine-burst debris per PRA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fire protection system shall provide a discharge command and electrical discharge path for each bottle of an engine pair such that no single command-path or electrical-bus failure prevents discharge of both bottles of that pair.
• The two extinguisher bottles of each engine pair shall be shown to be free of common design, manufacturing-lot and maintenance/servicing common-cause (dissimilar sourcing, staggered charge intervals, or equivalent substantiation).
• Cross-plumbing between the two bottles of an engine pair shall be routed/protected so a single rotor-burst or engine-burst event within one nacelle of the pair does not defeat discharge to both nacelles.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Closed in the SSA/ASA (verification-phase CMA) once the SF-021-TL fault tree exists: confirm the discharge bus and command-path independence as built, and confirm PRA rotor/engine-burst debris trajectories do not sever the shared cross-plumbing.

alertRows.notes: APU compartment dual-loop detection; automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation on APU fire. Automatic discharge on ground with aircraft unattended. Priority/modality not stated. Cite: §5.12.2, §5.12.4. [drafted from §5.12.2 / §5.12.4]

alertRows.name: Hold smoke detection
alertRows.notes: Smoke detection at nine hold stations; no suppression fitted. Alerting behaviour/priority not stated by document. Cite: §5.12.2. [drafted from §5.12.2]

alertRows.name: Fuel imbalance
alertRows.notes: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg; structurally limited to 3,000 kg. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.2.3, §5.2.4. [drafted from §5.2.3 / §5.2.4]

alertRows.name: Fuel low-pressure / imbalance discrete
alertRows.notes: Low-pressure and imbalance discretes to the flight deck. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.2.4. [drafted from §5.2.4]

alertRows.name: Restraint tension loss — single strap
alertRows.notes: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.8.2. [drafted from §5.8.2]

alertRows.name: Restraint condition — two adjacent stations
alertRows.notes: Loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.8.2. [drafted from §5.8.2]

alertRows.name: Autopilot disengagement
alertRows.notes: Following autopilot disengagement a warning (visual and auditory) must be provided to each pilot, timely and distinct from all other cockpit warnings. Aural component also required. Cite: §25.1329(j). [drafted from 14CFR-25.1329(j)]

alertRows.name: Autopilot disengagement — aural
alertRows.notes: Auditory component of the required autopilot-disengagement warning. Cite: §25.1329(j). [drafted from 14CFR-25.1329(j)]

alertRows.name: Autothrust disengagement
alertRows.notes: Following disengagement of the autothrust function, a caution must be provided to each pilot. Modality not stated by document. Cite: §25.1329(k). [drafted from 14CFR-25.1329(k)]

alertRows.name: Degraded flight control law
alertRows.notes: Degraded control laws are annunciated to the crew. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.3.6. [drafted from §5.3.6]

alertRows.name: Nose door lock status
alertRows.notes: Lock status displayed on the flight deck at all times and included in take-off configuration check; mechanical linkage drives a visual indicator visible from inside the flight deck. Priority not stated. Cite: §5.7.2, §5.7.6. [drafted from §5.7.2 / §5.7.6]

alertRows.name: Crew oxygen low pressure
alertRows.notes: Low pressure alerting; cylinder pressure displayed continuously on flight deck. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.13.4. [drafted from §5.13.4]

alertRows.name: Electrical source loss
alertRows.notes: Bus reconfiguration is automatic and not annunciated unless a source is lost; battery-only endurance is displayed. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.5.6. [drafted from §5.5.6]

alertRows.name: Ice detection advisory
alertRows.notes: Detection is advisory; ice detection advisory to the flight deck. Modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.10.2, §5.10.4. [drafted from §5.10.2 / §5.10.4]

alertRows.name: Ice protection zone loss
alertRows.notes: A lost electrical anti-ice zone is annunciated. Priority/modality not stated by document. Cite: §5.10.3. [drafted from §5.10.3]

taskRows.task: Close the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle to isolate a failed engine
Operate the four thrust levers with autothrottle for normal thrust control
Select manual cross-feed and isolate any tank
Fly through conventional inceptors with envelope protection active in the normal control law
Select the electric hydraulic pumps on or off and command the power transfer unit
Manually override ram air turbine deployment

cdRows.finding: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2).
cdRows.supports: Identifying non-normal system conditions and the associated procedure across every aircraft system

cdRows.finding: Normal control is by four thrust levers with autothrottle; FADEC protects against overspeed and overtemperature without crew intervention (§5.1.6).
cdRows.supports: Normal thrust control for all phases of flight

cdRows.item: Fuel shut-off and fire handle (per engine)
cdRows.finding: No crew action is required to isolate a failed engine other than to close the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle (§5.1.6).
cdRows.supports: Isolating a failed engine

cdRows.finding: Engine parameter data and fire and overheat discretes are provided to the avionics display system and flight deck (§5.1.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of engine parameters and fire/overheat state

cdRows.finding: Low-pressure and imbalance discretes are provided to the flight deck; fuel imbalance is annunciated at 1,200 kg and limited structurally to 3,000 kg (§5.2.3, §5.2.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of fuel feed low pressure and lateral imbalance

cdRows.item: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation selection
cdRows.finding: The system is normally automatic; the crew can select manual cross-feed and can isolate any tank (§5.2.6).
cdRows.supports: Managing fuel distribution and CG when automatic scheduling is not used

cdRows.finding: The crew flies through conventional inceptors with envelope protection active in the normal control law (§5.3.6).
cdRows.supports: Manual flight control in roll, pitch and yaw

cdRows.finding: Degraded laws are annunciated; reversion to mechanical control is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths (§5.3.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of reduced control-law state

cdRows.item: Surface position, asymmetry and jam status display
cdRows.finding: Surface position and system status, flight envelope protection status, and asymmetry and jam discretes are output to the avionics displays (§5.3.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of flight control surface position and faults

cdRows.finding: The crew sees pressure and quantity, can select the electric pumps on or off, and can command the power transfer unit (§5.4.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of hydraulic system state supporting flight controls, gear, brakes and door

cdRows.finding: Ram air turbine deployment is automatic with a manual override (§5.4.6).
cdRows.supports: Managing emergency hydraulic/electrical source deployment

cdRows.item: Electric pump and power transfer unit selection
cdRows.finding: The crew can select the electric pumps on or off and can command the power transfer unit (§5.4.6).
cdRows.supports: Reconfiguring hydraulic power

cdRows.finding: Bus reconfiguration is automatic and not annunciated unless a source is lost; battery-only operation is time-limited and the remaining endurance is displayed (§5.5.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of remaining electrical endurance in battery-only operation

cdRows.finding: Bus reconfiguration is automatic and is not annunciated to the crew unless a source is lost (§5.5.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of loss of an electrical source

cdRows.item: Gear lever and brake pedals with autobrake
cdRows.finding: Normal operation is by gear lever and brake pedals with autobrake available (§5.6.6).
cdRows.supports: Landing gear operation and braking on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces

cdRows.finding: Alternate extension is a crew action from a separate handle, independent of hydraulic pressure (§5.6.3, §5.6.6).
cdRows.supports: Extending the gear independently of hydraulic pressure

cdRows.item: Brake temperature and turnaround limit display
cdRows.finding: Brake temperature is monitored continuously and a turnaround limit is displayed (§5.6.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of brake temperature against turnaround limit

cdRows.finding: Gear position is provided to the flight deck; downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit (§5.6.2, §5.6.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of landing gear position

cdRows.item: Nose door lock status display and mechanical indicator
cdRows.finding: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar circuits — a proximity harness and a mechanical linkage driving a visual indicator visible from inside the flight deck; lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and included in the take-off configuration check (§5.7.2, §5.7.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of nose cargo door lock state before flight

cdRows.finding: The door cannot be opened with the hold pressurised: a pressure interlock vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run (§5.7.2).
cdRows.supports: Preventing door unlock with the hold pressurised

cdRows.finding: The door is operated from a ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or on its gear, and cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.6).
cdRows.supports: Opening and closing the nose cargo door on the ground

cdRows.finding: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight; loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention. In flight the crew has indication only (§5.8.2, §5.8.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of blade restraint tension in flight

cdRows.item: Differential pressure and cabin altitude display
cdRows.finding: Differential pressure and cabin altitude are output to the avionics and to the crew; pressurisation is fully automatic with a manual mode available (§5.9.4, §5.9.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of pressurisation state

cdRows.item: Pack configuration and bleed source selection
cdRows.finding: The crew selects pack configuration and bleed source; there is no routine crew action in normal flight (§5.9.6).
cdRows.supports: Selecting environmental control configuration

cdRows.item: Ice detection advisory and zone health display
cdRows.finding: Ice protection status and zone health are output to the avionics; detection is advisory, a lost electrical zone is annunciated, and the ice detection advisory is provided to the flight deck (§5.10.2, §5.10.3, §5.10.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of ice detection and lost anti-ice zones

cdRows.finding: The crew may select automatic or manual operation; in automatic, detection commands the system on, and the performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically to the displayed performance (§5.10.6).
cdRows.supports: Selecting automatic or manual ice protection

cdRows.finding: Reversionary display selection is manual; network reconfiguration is automatic (§5.11.6).
cdRows.supports: Recovering display presentation after a display-system fault

cdRows.finding: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays (§5.11.2, §5.11.3).
cdRows.supports: Providing attitude, airspeed and altitude independently of the primary displays

cdRows.finding: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles, except for automatic APU discharge on the ground with the aircraft unattended (§5.12.6).
cdRows.supports: Extinguishing engine and APU zone fires

cdRows.finding: Fire and overheat warnings are output to the crew alerting system; dual-loop detection uses AND logic for warning, degrading to single-loop on loss of one loop (§5.12.2, §5.12.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of fire and overheat conditions in monitored zones

cdRows.finding: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression; that decision is recorded and carried forward as an assumption to be substantiated (§5.12.2).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of smoke in the hold

cdRows.finding: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item; low pressure alerting is provided (§5.13.2, §5.13.4).
cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of oxygen availability; dispatch check

cdRows.finding: Four quick-donning full-face masks with integral smoke goggles and demand regulators are provided; masks are donned on crew action with no automatic deployment (§5.13.2, §5.13.6).
cdRows.supports: Crew oxygen supply for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events

cdRows.finding: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve (§5.1.2).
cdRows.supports: Preventing in-flight reverse thrust deployment

cdRows.finding: Lock status is included in the take-off configuration check; nose door lock status and restraint status are output to the take-off configuration monitor (§5.7.4, §5.7.6, §5.8.4).
cdRows.supports: Detecting an unsafe take-off configuration (door lock, restraint status)

saRows.cue: Fire and overheat discretes and engine parameter data on the avionics display; crew alert list
saRows.element: Asymmetric thrust condition following an engine failure
saRows.finding: Document describes engine parameter data and fire/overheat discretes to the flight deck but does not describe an explicit asymmetric-thrust or engine-out alert; cue for direct perception of asymmetry is [not stated]

saRows.cue: Crew alert list with associated procedures; fire handle and fuel shut-off per engine
saRows.element: Which engine has failed and needs isolation
Directional-control demand arising from an outboard engine failure at the 28 m moment arm
saRows.finding: No cue described that projects the directional-control consequence of asymmetric thrust to the crew; the moment-arm case is stated as a sizing case only, not an alert

saRows.element: Undetected partial thrust loss — condition present without crew awareness
saRows.finding: SF-001-M2 posits an undetected partial thrust loss; the document describes engine parameter data to displays but no dedicated partial-thrust-loss alert, so the cue that would make this condition perceptible is [not stated]

saRows.cue: Weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement inhibit; mechanical lock at translating sleeve
saRows.element: Reverser deployment state on landing rollout
saRows.finding: Document describes the in-flight deployment inhibit but does not describe a flight-deck indication of reverser deployed/stowed state; cue for perceiving reverser position is [not stated]
No alert for inadvertent reverser deployment is described in the source; the only protection described is the weight-on-wheels/radio-altimeter inhibit and mechanical lock

saRows.cue: Low-pressure discretes to the flight deck
saRows.element: Fuel low-pressure condition at engine feed
Fuel imbalance between left and right wings

saRows.cue: Imbalance annunciated at 1,200 kg; structural limit stated at 3,000 kg
saRows.element: Approach to the structural imbalance limit of 3,000 kg
saRows.finding: An annunciation at 1,200 kg and a structural limit at 3,000 kg are described, but no cue is described that projects the trend toward the limit; whether the crew is cued to the rate of divergence is [not stated]

saRows.cue: Tank quantity and temperature to avionics; CG contribution to loading computation
saRows.element: Centre-of-gravity state under automatic transfer and cross-feed scheduling
saRows.finding: Transfer and cross-feed are scheduled automatically without crew action; the document does not describe an explicit CG display or an alert for erroneous distribution, so the cue for comprehending a CG excursion is [not stated]

saRows.element: Degraded flight control law in effect

saRows.cue: Asymmetry and jam discretes to the avionics

saRows.element: Reversion to mechanical control following loss of all electrical command paths
saRows.finding: Reversion is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths; the document states degraded laws are annunciated but does not confirm a distinct cue for mechanical reversion, so the cue is [not stated]

saRows.cue: Flight envelope protection status to the avionics displays
Pressure, quantity and temperature to the avionics
saRows.element: Hydraulic system pressure and quantity available to flight controls

saRows.cue: Generator and battery status to the flight deck; source loss is annunciated
saRows.element: Loss of an electrical source affecting control channels
saRows.finding: Bus reconfiguration is automatic and not annunciated unless a source is lost, so the cue exists only for source loss, not for reconfiguration

resourcesData.name: Main AC electrical (4 × 150 kVA, VF)
resourcesData.description: Four engine-driven variable-frequency generators supply four main AC buses feeding aircraft consumers; APU or emergency generator can supplement. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Environmental Control & Pressurisation (ECS)", consumer "Ice Protection (IPS)", consumer "Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI)", consumer "Fire Protection (FPR)"]

resourcesData.name: DC essential / DC main / hot battery (28 VDC)
resourcesData.description: TRUs and two batteries feed DC main, DC essential and hot battery buses; DC essential is the final electrical resort for controls, fire protection and standby instruments. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI)", consumer "Fire Protection (FPR)", consumer "Environmental Control & Pressurisation (ECS)", consumer "Ice Protection (IPS)"]

resourcesData.name: High-pressure engine bleed air (cross-bleed manifold)
resourcesData.description: High-pressure bleed air from the four engines through a shared cross-bleed manifold supplies the air cycle packs and the wing/cowl anti-ice piccolo distribution. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Environmental Control & Pressurisation (ECS)", consumer "Ice Protection (IPS)"]

resourcesData.name: Ram air (heat-exchanger / turbine)
resourcesData.description: Ram air for the ECS heat exchangers; drawn from ambient at aircraft level. (Provider not a listed system in this subset — recorded as a boundary inflow.) [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Environmental Control & Pressurisation (ECS)"]

resourcesData.name: Gaseous crew oxygen (HP cylinders)
resourcesData.description: Crew Oxygen (OXY) is the provider of breathing oxygen, but OXY is not in the supplied system subset; recorded as a boundary resource pending inclusion of the OXY system.

resourcesData.name: Engine parameter / air-data / inertial data (Data bus)
resourcesData.description: Deterministic dual data network carrying air data, inertial data, engine parameters, fire/overheat discretes and alerting between systems. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI)", consumer "Fire Protection (FPR)", consumer "Environmental Control & Pressurisation (ECS)", consumer "Ice Protection (IPS)"]

resourcesData.name: Fire extinguishing agent (bottled)
resourcesData.description: Stored extinguishing agent in bottles cross-plumbed per engine pair, plus a dedicated APU bottle, discharged into the nacelle/APU zones. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Fire Protection (FPR)", consumer "Propulsion (PRP)"]

resourcesData.name: Mechanical accessory-gearbox drive
resourcesData.description: Engine accessory-gearbox mechanical drive turns the AC generators (and hydraulic pumps outside this subset); the electrical resource for AVI/ECS/IPS/FPR ultimately stands on it. [AI noted, unmatched to project: consumer "Avionics & Flight Deck (AVI)"]

hfaRows.text: The Aeolus HL-1 is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at or after V1, so a single-engine partial thrust loss is within the design dispatch case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The asymmetric-thrust case is a single-engine asymmetry within the rudder authority the flight-control sizing provides at the 28 m outboard moment arm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected partial thrust loss is bounded at single-engine scale and its end effect leaves the crew able to reach a suitable aerodrome once inferred.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The certified landing distance on the semi-prepared surface is achievable on wheel braking alone, with reverse thrust credited as margin rather than as a required means.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Reverse thrust is credited only as a supplementary ground-deceleration means and the wheel-brake system alone satisfies the 1,800 m landing requirement.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The classifying case for inadvertent reverse thrust is an in-flight deployment producing thrust opposite to command, notwithstanding the WOW + radio-altimeter inhibits and mechanical sleeve lock.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected reverse asymmetry during landing rollout produces a controllable ground directional excursion that the crew arrests with steering and asymmetric braking, not a departure from the semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial loss of fuel feed starves a bounded subset of the four engines (not all four) and the crew can reconfigure cross-feed, boost pumps and the gravity path to sustain flight to a suitable aerodrome.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous fuel feed pressure is contained to the affected engine and does not propagate to multiple engines through the cross-feed gallery.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The crew can detect and arrest an erroneous fuel distribution before the 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit or an uncontrollable CG is reached, using the 1,200 kg annunciation and manual cross-feed/isolation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit bounds an undetected fuel imbalance short of a hazardous wing-bending exceedance before the crew recognises the asymmetry.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The three dissimilar voting flight control computers bound an erroneous or uncommanded roll input to a transient the crew can detect and arrest without loss of control.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: After a partial loss of pitch control authority the residual authority leaves the aircraft controllable at a large margin reduction rather than uncontrollable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: For an erroneous pitch response the crew detect the malfunction and successfully arrest it before loss of control in every flight phase.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The undetected roll malfunctions have no crew annunciation, so the crew take no corrective action and the condition develops to loss of control.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An uncommanded or undetected-erroneous pitch excursion is, in the worst case, not always arrestable by the fly-by-wire law or the mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion before departure from controlled flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Following total loss of yaw control the aircraft cannot maintain a survivable heading against the sizing asymmetry case and the flight is not recoverable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A significant partial loss of pitch authority is survivable short of loss of control when encountered undetected.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The split-rudder architecture retains sufficient directional authority after a single rudder segment/supply loss to cover the V1 outboard-engine-out with maximum blade payload, so partial loss is a controllable degradation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous or uncommanded yaw input is bounded and arrestable by crew action (not a full-authority, uncountered hardover) so the malfunction rows are credited as recoverable rather than as immediate loss of control.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The undetected variants correctly credit loss of the yaw asymmetry/jam annunciation, leaving the crew to rely on direct aircraft motion cues only.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An uncommanded, unannunciated yaw input builds into a divergent sideslip/heading excursion the crew cannot promptly attribute and counter, especially near the ground.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A flapless/reduced-flap landing at 318,000 kg maximum landing weight remains achievable within the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing-distance requirement, at reduced margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The per-section asymmetry brakes bound a high-lift mismatch, but a credible worst-case asymmetry can still develop near the ground before the brakes arrest it, producing a roll/yaw the crew must counter with limited margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Uncommanded high-lift motion is annunciated and the crew arrest it before a high-speed airload exceedance or a low-speed near-ground lift loss departs controlled flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: For undetected partial high-lift loss, the eroded approach/landing margin without a crew speed correction is a moderate (not large) degradation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The high-lift asymmetry brakes do not fully arrest an undetected asymmetry before it produces a large low-altitude rolling moment.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Partial loss of ground load support leaves a residual footprint that still permits a landing without collapse on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Failure to extend and lock for landing is credited only when the free-fall alternate extension has also failed, leaving no locked support path at touchdown.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The undetected loss in SF-009-M2 is of downlock indication only, with the second independent proximity circuit and any monitor still able to reveal a gear-not-locked state.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Residual reverse thrust and accumulator-supported braking arrest the total-loss-of-deceleration case short of a hull-loss overrun on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Partial loss of deceleration leaves sufficient braking to stop within the 1,800 m available given the ~1,080 m nominal rollout.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The crew can detect and counter braking asymmetry with tiller/pedal steering and rudder before the aircraft departs the semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Aerodynamic rudder and differential (asymmetric) braking provide an independent ground directional-control alternate to nose-wheel steering.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout absorbs a partial (not total) deceleration loss without overrun.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The destination semi-prepared strip is narrow with limited lateral run-off, so a lateral excursion is a credible and adverse ground outcome.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous ground steering input occurs at a ground speed and lateral margin where an aware crew can detect and arrest the deviation on the surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A genuinely crew-unaware erroneous ground steering input exists (no immediate heading/yaw cue) and the uncorrected excursion carries non-benign energy.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The take-off configuration monitor and displayed lock status reliably prevent dispatch with the visor pressure boundary not made.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An inadvertent in-flight loss of the nose visor pressure boundary is physically credible despite the in-flight inoperability and pressure interlock defences.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The nose door's dual dissimilar lock sensing and pressure interlock do not guarantee that a false-secure LOCKED indication is contradicted before take-off, so the erroneous indication can defeat the configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Undetected loss of the nose-door pressure-boundary closure produces a large reduction in structural safety margins at the preliminary hold differential.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An in-flight total loss of restraint of the 72.6 t single blade is not recoverable by crew action, since there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected single or adjacent strap-tension loss on SF-013 remains within the sized "neighbours carry the load" redundancy and does not cascade to an uncontrollable CG excursion.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Crew oxygen is available and independent of the flight-deck air-supply loss, and the emergency-descent diversion time from FL260 is within crew oxygen endurance.

hfaRows.text: At FL260 with the preliminary low hold/cabin differential the crew can detect a cabin-pressure excursion and don oxygen before it becomes physiologically incapacitating, but an UNDETECTED excursion can develop far enough to distress the crew before natural cues appear.

hfaRows.text: Loss of ice-protection results in a large (total loss) or significant (partial loss) reduction in safety margins in the icing envelope rather than an unrecoverable handling loss, given the crew can exit icing on annunciation.

hfaRows.text: The flight crew reliably recognise icing conditions and select ice protection manually when automatic detection or scheduling is degraded or lost.

hfaRows.text: An erroneous or lost protection schedule that leaves a surface or probe unheated in icing is annunciated to the crew or otherwise detectable in time to reselect.

hfaRows.text: Individual probe protection loss affects a single air-data source at a time and is isolable against the three independent air-data reference units.

hfaRows.text: Independent icing cues remain available to the crew after undetected loss of the ice detectors, so accretion is eventually recognised.

hfaRows.text: Probe heating is individually monitored, so undetected loss is limited and air-data reversion to standby remains available.

hfaRows.text: The independent standby instrument is adequate for continued flight and landing across the relevant phases after total loss of primary flight/nav data.

hfaRows.text: The triple dissimilar reference units and independent standby detect and isolate a single erroneous data source before the crew commits an unrecoverable action.

hfaRows.text: The flight crew perform a credited, timely cross-check of primary flight/navigation data against the independent standby instrument, but this is not shown reliably to catch undetected erroneous data before loss of control.

hfaRows.text: The credited partial loss of crew alerting removes only a non-safety-critical subset of alerts, leaving the alerting of the most severe failure conditions intact.

hfaRows.text: A single erroneous alert does not by itself command the crew into an irreversible incorrect procedure (e.g. shutting down a needed system) with no recovery.

hfaRows.text: The standalone undetected loss of crew alerting, un-combined with any concurrent annunciated failure, is classified Major per the §5.4.2 default.

hfaRows.text: An undetected fire in a monitored fire zone (nacelle, APU, bleed duct, gear bay, hold) leads to a large — not necessarily catastrophic — reduction in safety margins given the aircraft's segregation and extinguishing provisions.

hfaRows.text: A single erroneous fire/overheat indication drives at most one engine shutdown and diversion on a four-engine aircraft that continues after loss of one engine.

hfaRows.text: The partial loss of detection is annunciated (dual-loop degrading to single-loop is annunciated) and the retained zones include the higher-consequence engine and APU zones.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An unsuppressed engine-nacelle or APU fire in this configuration can be contained by crew isolation and land the aircraft without propagating to hull loss.

hfaRows.text: The crew can complete an emergency descent to a breathable altitude from FL260 before hypoxia or smoke incapacitates them when no breathing oxygen is available.

hfaRows.text: An undetected total loss of crew oxygen produces a survivable, workload-driven crew-incapacitation risk (Hazardous) rather than certain incapacitation before descent (Catastrophic).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The flight deck cylinder-pressure indication and low-pressure alerting make a partial loss detectable, keeping SF-022-PL an aware condition.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the asymmetry is a single-engine case within the rudder authority the SDD sizes to; a runaway/uncommanded-high asymmetry beyond the sized case, or a second same-side engine (retained as a condition to be studied), could reduce control margins to Hazardous. Flight-control sizing evidence and the maximum credible asymmetry would confirm or overturn the Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the undetected shortfall is a single-engine-scale partial loss whose end effect the crew reach a suitable aerodrome for; if a larger undetected loss combines with a phase where escape is not possible the end state could be worse. Engine parameter display coverage and the smallest undetectable thrust decrement would confirm the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the certified landing distance is achievable on wheel braking alone (reverse credited as margin, not required) on the semi-prepared surface; if the 1,800 m requirement cannot be met without reverse on a degraded/contaminated strip the class rises toward Hazardous (overrun risk). The braking-only certified landing distance on semi-prepared surface would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes reverse thrust is credited only as a supplementary ground-deceleration means and the wheel-brake system alone meets the 1,800 m requirement; the SDD gives the margin (1,080 m vs 1,800 m) but does not state whether reverse is credited in the certified landing distance. If reverse is credited on the semi-prepared surface, partial loss could rise to Major. Confirm against the LDG/braking landing-performance basis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Severity is set for an in-flight inadvertent deployment. The SDD provides two independent in-flight inhibits (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement) plus a mechanical sleeve lock, so the credible severity may be bounded by whether these defeat every deployment path; a purely on-ground inadvertent deployment during landing rollout would be milder. Assumed the classifying case is the in-flight reversal because it is the more severe outcome the function must be shown against. Confirm against the reverser inhibit architecture and any AC 25.933 showing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an undetected reverse asymmetry produces a controllable ground excursion that the crew arrests with steering and asymmetric braking (Major), not a departure from the semi-prepared strip (which would be more severe). The SDD does not state reverser asymmetry magnitude, deceleration split, or the runway lateral margin. Confirm against the directional-control sizing and strip geometry.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classified for a partial feed loss affecting a bounded number of engines that the crew reconfigures around (cross-feed, dual boost pumps, gravity path) with single-engine continuation designed in. The single spanwise cross-feed gallery is the only cross-side path and its loss could expand the number of engines starved toward the total case; the SDD does not bound how many engines a partial feed failure can starve. Confirm against the fuel-feed failure modes and gallery isolation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD does not state how an engine responds to erroneous (as opposed to lost) feed pressure or whether erroneous pressure can propagate to more than one engine through the cross-feed gallery; assumed single-engine containment with FADEC protection. If erroneous pressure can affect multiple engines simultaneously the class would rise. Confirm against FADEC/FUE behaviour and the cross-feed isolation logic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD gives the 1,200 kg annunciation and 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit but not the rate at which an erroneous transfer can drive imbalance or the CG-excursion authority of the transfer schedule, so whether the crew can always arrest before a limit is exceeded is not settled; assumed the credited manual response bounds the effect at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If erroneous distribution can exceed the structural limit or reach an uncontrollable CG faster than crew action, the class rises to Catastrophic. Confirm against transfer rates, CG authority and annunciation timing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the 3,000 kg structural imbalance limit bounds the outcome short of a hazardous wing-bending exceedance before the crew recognises the asymmetry through handling. Confirm against the wing structural bending analysis and the time-to-limit at maximum credible transfer rate; if the undetected imbalance can reach a structural exceedance this would move to Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the voting of the three dissimilar flight control computers bounds an erroneous roll command to a transient the crew can arrest without loss of control, so the credited outcome is Major rather than Hazardous. Confirm against the FCS command-monitoring coverage and the maximum credible surface runaway; an unbounded hardover at low altitude would move this to Hazardous or Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the uncommanded roll is bounded by the three-computer voting and detected/arrested by the crew before loss of control, giving Major. Confirm against the maximum credible uncommanded surface deflection and the time available at the critical phase/altitude; a large uncommanded hardover near the ground would move this to Hazardous or Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The class turns on how much pitch authority remains after a partial loss, which the function objective alone does not settle. Assumed the residual authority leaves the aircraft controllable at a large margin reduction rather than uncontrollable; a fault-tree/architecture count of remaining pitch actuation paths would confirm or move this between Hazardous and Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The class turns on whether the aware crew can detect and arrest an erroneous pitch command before loss of control across all phases; assumed detection and successful correction are credited (Hazardous). If detection/response time is inadequate in a critical phase this becomes Catastrophic. A human-factors detection-and-response record for pitch-response malfunctions would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the crew can arrest the uncommanded motion before departure — the SDD gives only mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder, not the recoverable envelope of an uncommanded runaway. Assumed a worst-case uncommanded excursion is not always arrestable; a handling/failure transient analysis would confirm or reduce the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on how much authority remains and whether the shortfall is encountered before landing; the SDD gives dual actuation per surface (elevators on HYD A and C) but not the degraded handling margin. Assumed a survivable partial degradation short of loss of control; a control-authority analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the crew detect the erroneous (unannunciated) response and revert in time; the three dissimilar voting computers should mask a single erroneous channel, but a common-mode erroneous command is retained. Assumed the undetected erroneous case worst-case is not always recoverable; the FCS voting/monitoring coverage analysis would confirm or reduce the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the crew recognise and arrest the uncommanded motion without an alert; the SDD provides only mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim. Assumed worst-case the unannunciated excursion is not always arrestable; a handling/failure-transient analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on how much authority remains after a single rudder-supply/segment loss and whether it still covers the V1 outboard-engine-out + max-blade sizing case; the SDD states this case sizes rudder area but does not quantify the residual margin. Assumed the design intent (single supply loss leaves sufficient authority) holds; a directional-control margin analysis would confirm or move this toward Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on the magnitude/rate of the erroneous surface motion and whether crew can arrest it before loss of control; the SDD gives fly-by-wire with three dissimilar voting FCCs and asymmetry/jam discretes but no excursion-magnitude data. Assumed a single-channel erroneous command is bounded/recoverable; a full-authority hardover uncountered would drive Catastrophic. Handling analysis would settle it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on the magnitude/rate of the uncommanded motion and whether it is arrestable; the SDD does not quantify a rudder runaway/hardover excursion. Assumed a bounded, recoverable uncommanded input; an uncountered full-segment hardover would drive Catastrophic. Handling/failure-transient analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on whether the residual authority (unknown to crew) still covers the V1 outboard-engine-out + max-blade sizing case when the demand arrives, and on the absence of annunciation; the SDD notes asymmetry/jam discretes exist but this row assumes their loss. Assumed the undetected shortfall becomes critical at the sizing demand; a margin analysis would confirm or reduce to Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on whether the crew can still detect and arrest the erroneous response from aircraft motion cues without alerting, and on the excursion magnitude before recognition; the SDD gives no detection-time or excursion data. Assumed direct motion cues permit recovery; if the erroneous input is a rapid full-authority hardover recognised too late, this becomes Catastrophic. Handling analysis would settle it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD gives yaw architecture (split rudder, two supplies) but not the magnitude or divergence rate of an uncommanded, unannunciated yaw input, nor the crew time-to-detect. Assumed a sustained divergent excursion the crew cannot promptly attribute; a slow, self-limiting or readily-countered input would lower this toward Major. Handling/HF analysis and the yaw-source failure set would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Effects assessed at takeoff/landing where high-lift is used; other phases are No Safety Effect (function not in use, condition escapable). Assumed a flapless landing remains achievable on this basis within the 1,800 m requirement at reduced margin — if the elevated approach speed exceeds the strip's landing-distance capability at max landing weight this rises toward Hazardous. Landing performance analysis against the 1,800 m strip would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the partial loss leaves a usable takeoff/landing setting with margin retained against the 1,800 m requirement; a partial loss that drops below a certifiable takeoff/landing configuration would be Major. Degree of degradation and resulting speeds against the strip would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD provides per-section asymmetry brakes on the common torque shaft to arrest a runaway, but the residual asymmetry magnitude after brake action and its roll/yaw consequence are not stated. Assumed a credible worst-case asymmetry near the ground before the brakes stop it; if the asymmetry brakes bound the mismatch to a readily-countered level this reduces to Major. Handling analysis of the braked-asymmetry case would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the motion is annunciated (asymmetry/jam discretes and high-lift position are stated as FCS outputs) and the crew arrest it before an airload or low-speed exceedance; an uncommanded near-ground retraction that departs controlled flight would be Hazardous. Handling and load analysis of the uncommanded-motion case would confirm the credited outcome.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The class turns on the degree of undetected high-lift loss and whether any residual cue reaches the crew; a small undetected reduction supports Major, a large undetected reduction flown to the flare could reach Hazardous. Assumed a moderate partial loss with no independent cue. Handling-qualities and alerting-coverage analysis for degraded high-lift would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD credits asymmetry brakes at each high-lift section (§5.3.2); whether they arrest an asymmetry before it becomes uncontrollable, and whether any residual roll cue reaches the crew, sets whether this is Hazardous or milder. Assumed an asymmetry that develops without a timely cue. Asymmetry-brake effectiveness and roll-authority analysis against the asymmetry would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The class turns on how much support is lost and whether the residual configuration still permits a landing without collapse on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip; a small partial loss supports Major, a large partial loss approaching an unsupported side could reach Hazardous. Assumed a moderate partial loss (e.g. one bogie) with a landable residual footprint. Structural and flotation analysis of the degraded gear on the semi-prepared surface would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The credited end state assumes BOTH the normal extension and the free-fall alternate have failed — the design carries a free-fall alternate independent of hydraulic pressure (§5.6.3), so failure to extend and lock is Catastrophic only when that backstop is also lost; a failure of only the normal path, recovered by free-fall, would be far milder. Assumed the full failure-to-extend-and-lock condition as stated. Availability/independence of the free-fall path would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the undetected loss is of indication only, with the second independent downlock sensing circuit still available; if both sensing circuits are defeated or the annunciation loss can coincide undetected with a gear-not-locked state, the combination could be more severe and must meet the un-annunciated objective. Confirmed by whether the two proximity circuits are truly independent and whether a comparison/monitor detects total sensing loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed residual deceleration (inboard reverse thrust plus accumulator-supported braking sized to six applications) prevents this from becoming a hull-loss overrun, holding it at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If accumulator braking is not creditable in the total-loss case and reverse thrust alone cannot arrest within the available surface, the end state approaches hull loss and the class rises. Confirmed by braking/reverser stopping-performance analysis on the semi-prepared surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed partial loss leaves enough braking to stop within the 1,800 m available given the ~1,080 m nominal rollout; the class turns on how much braking is lost. If the degradation is severe enough to threaten the overrun margin it approaches Hazardous. Confirmed by degraded-braking stopping-distance analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the crew can detect and counter the asymmetry with steering/rudder before the aircraft departs the semi-prepared strip, holding this at Major. If the asymmetry is large and unrecoverable at speed on the narrow surface the excursion could be Hazardous. Confirmed by directional-control/handling analysis of the braking-asymmetry case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Whether an undetected partial deceleration loss can escalate to overrun/Hazardous depends on the magnitude of the shortfall and the actual runway margin at destination weight; assumed the ~720 m margin absorbs a partial (not total) loss. Braking-performance analysis against the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Escalation to lateral excursion/Hazardous turns on the magnitude of the asymmetry and the strip width, neither given in the SDD; assumed a recoverable asymmetry once the heading deviation develops. Ground directional-control substantiation on the semi-prepared surface would settle it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classified Hazardous, not Catastrophic, by crediting aerodynamic rudder and differential braking as an independent directional alternate; whether a low-speed excursion on the specific strip becomes a collision (Catastrophic) depends on strip geometry/obstacles not in the SDD. Runway-excursion analysis and the directional-control alternates architecture would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classified Hazardous by crediting that the crew can detect and override the uncommanded input (tiller/pedal disconnect and differential braking exist) before an excursion becomes a collision; escalation to Catastrophic depends on override authority/response time and strip geometry not in the SDD. Steering-failure transient analysis and the disconnect provision would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the erroneous input occurs at a ground speed and margin where the crew can detect and arrest the deviation within the available runway/taxiway width; the SDD does not state achievable ground speed at the point of the erroneous command. If the input occurs at high speed with insufficient lateral margin the excursion may not be arrested, driving Hazardous. Confirm with ground handling-qualities analysis and the excursion case for the semi-prepared surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an erroneous ground steering input can occur without cues the crew would notice (heading/side-force), i.e. a genuinely unaware case exists, and that at a plausible ground speed the resulting excursion is not survivable-benign. The SDD does not state steering fault annunciation coverage or the speed at which the input arises. If steering errors are always accompanied by detectable heading/yaw cues the unaware case may be inapplicable; if excursion energy is low the class may fall to Major. Confirm against AVI alerting coverage and the ground excursion case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the take-off configuration monitor and displayed lock status reliably prevent dispatch with the pressure boundary not made, so a total-loss-of-closure aircraft never gets airborne. The SDD states lock status is displayed and included in the take-off configuration check but does not state the monitor's integrity. If dispatch with the boundary not made were possible the in-flight consequence would be a pressure-boundary and structural load-path failure of far higher severity. Confirm the take-off configuration monitor integrity and the interlock.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an inadvertent in-flight loss of closure is physically credible despite the design defences (door not operable in flight, pressure interlock requiring residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run, eight locking pins). If the interlock and in-flight-inoperability defences make in-flight unlock non-credible, this failure condition is architecturally precluded rather than Catastrophic and would be dispositioned by the door structural/interlock substantiation. Confirm the interlock and lock integrity establish the probability rather than the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — SDD gives dual dissimilar lock sensing and a pressure interlock (§5.7.3) but does not state whether these fully arrest the false-secure mis-indication before flight; assumed the erroneous indication can propagate past the config check. Confirmation of interlock/indication independence would lower the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Hold differential is preliminary (§1.2) and the structural consequence of an undetected boundary loss is not quantified in the SDD; assumed a large safety-margin reduction. The frozen differential and structural relief case (§5.9.2) would confirm or revise the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — As SF-012-M2, but with the crew unaware and no detection credited; assumed the dual dissimilar sensing does not force disagreement to the crew in this case. Substantiating that the mechanical indicator always contradicts a false-secure electrical reading would lower the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the undetected erosion stops at one station or can cascade to adjacent stations before manifesting; assumed the sized single-strap redundancy holds and no further loss occurs undetected. The restraint loads/redundancy substantiation would confirm or move this to Hazardous if adjacent-station loss is credible.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on crew oxygen being available and independent when flight-deck air supply is lost, and on the emergency-descent diversion time from FL260 being within oxygen endurance. Assumed both hold; if crew oxygen shares a common cause with the air-supply loss, or diversion time exceeds oxygen reserve, this rises toward Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on how extreme the erroneous conditioning can be (e.g. gross over-temperature) and whether the crew can detect and reconfigure before it impairs task performance. Assumed the erroneous state is recoverable via manual mode within crew capability; an undetectable or extreme thermal excursion impairing the crew would push toward Hazardous.
