hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the hold has no crew or occupants in flight and no payload requiring active conditioning; SDD states the hold is unoccupied and carries a single blade. If a payload conditioning requirement exists the aircraft effect could rise; confirm against the payload/ECS conditioning schedule.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on how far an erroneous flight-deck conditioning excursion can go before crew efficiency is impaired vs merely uncomfortable (Minor). Assumed a credible excursion reaching significant workload; a demonstrated bounded excursion with manual reversion would lower this to Minor. Confirm the conditioning fault envelope.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on time-of-useful-consciousness at FL260 vs quick-donning mask time and whether independent positive/negative relief valves bound the differential. SDD credits independent mechanical relief and quick-donning crew oxygen; if TUC is shorter than credited mask-don time the crew axis could reach incapacitation and the class Catastrophic. Confirm cabin-altitude-at-FL260 depressurisation profile and mask-don timing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes a partial loss leaves a working outflow valve / controller or the pneumatic backup, so pressurisation is maintained (SDD: two controllers, two valves either sufficient, pneumatic backup). If the partial loss instead progressed to inability to hold differential it would trend toward the total-loss class; confirm the partial-loss end state.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on the rate an erroneous control command can drive cabin altitude before independent relief and crew reversion arrest it, and on crew detection time. SDD credits independent mechanical relief; if an erroneous command can exceed relief capacity and outpace crew oxygen/reversion the class could be Catastrophic. Confirm the maximum erroneous-command excursion rate and relief-valve authority.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the aware crew detect and revert (manual mode + quick-donning oxygen credited) before a large-differential excursion, and that maximum cabin-altitude excursion at FL260 with the preliminary low differential stays within crew-oxygen-manageable bounds. Hold differential is stated preliminary; a higher frozen differential or a slower detection case would move this toward Hazardous. Confirmed by ECS excursion analysis and the crew-oxygen diversion-time sizing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the aware crew detect the erroneous schedule and revert to manual before the independent relief valves and crew oxygen are exceeded. If erroneous control could drive an excursion the crew cannot arrest within crew-oxygen limits at FL260, this moves to Hazardous. Confirmed by ECS controller-failure analysis and relief-valve sizing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the crew-unaware case allows a physiologically significant excursion to develop undetected before symptoms cue donning. Turns on the maximum cabin altitude reachable at FL260 with the preliminary low differential and the time-to-symptom margin; a benign low differential that cannot produce hypoxia before natural cues would reduce this to Major. Confirmed by cabin-altitude excursion analysis, time-of-useful-consciousness assessment, and the annunciation coverage for cabin altitude.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the aircraft can be operated in the icing envelope of its certification basis and that total loss with icing encountered produces a large safety-margin reduction rather than an unrecoverable one. Turns on the handling/performance degradation from unprotected accretion, which is not quantified in the SDD; if accretion could preclude continued safe flight this moves to Catastrophic, if the crew can reliably exit icing before margins erode it stays at Hazardous. Confirmed by icing performance/handling analysis and the crew ice-exit procedure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes partial loss leaves enough coverage that the crew can manage or exit icing without a large safety-margin reduction. Turns on how much protection is lost and whether the remaining coverage protects the critical surfaces; loss of a critical surface's only protection path would move this to Hazardous. Confirmed by the ice-protection zonal coverage analysis and the degraded-coverage handling case.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the crediting end state is unprotected surface/probe in the icing envelope with degraded-but-detected coverage, not undetected total probe loss; the class turns on whether the erroneous schedule is annunciated (SDD states electrical zone loss is annunciated but does not confirm bleed-side or probe coverage). Confirm annunciation coverage of an erroneous schedule; an undetected loss of probe heat in icing could support Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the crew reliably recognise icing conditions and select protection manually without the detectors; the class turns on that credited crew action. Per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 loss of annunciation is at least Major unless shown otherwise — confirm the crew can detect icing without the detectors and that the loss is itself annunciated; if manual recognition cannot be credited this rises to Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a single probe/source affected and detected via individual monitoring against three air-data references; class turns on the affected source being isolable. Confirm which probes lose heat together and that no common route takes multiple air-data sources; simultaneous loss of protection to multiple air-data sources in icing could support Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Two detectors are the same type (recorded commonality); assumed a false negative is detectable by cross-check with conditions and the manual path, so the crew recover protection. Class turns on whether a common-type erroneous detection can go unreconciled — confirm detector dissimilarity/cross-monitor; an undetected false negative in icing could support Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD states detection is advisory with automatic and manual activation and two detectors, but does not establish how reliably the crew recognises icing without the detector, which sets whether this is Major or Hazardous; assumed independent icing cues remain, to be confirmed by the icing HF/detection analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD says probes are heated and monitored individually, so an UNDETECTED loss conflicts with that monitoring; class turns on how many probes could be lost undetected before air data is corrupted and whether crew air-data cross-check catches it. Assumed reversion to standby remains; confirm against the air-data / probe-heat monitoring analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class credits the independent standby instrument (shares no supply, sensor or processing) as sufficient for continued flight and landing; if the standby cannot be relied on in the relevant phases/conditions the class rises toward Catastrophic. Confirm standby adequacy and coverage in the AVI SSA.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class credits crew and system detection of the erroneous source (triple ADIRU vote plus independent standby) as arresting the error before an unrecoverable outcome; if a single misleading source can defeat the cross-check undetected in a critical phase the class rises toward Catastrophic. Confirm in the AVI data-integrity / monitoring analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The class turns on whether the crew's cross-check against the independent standby instrument (SDD §5.11.2, on the DC essential bus, sharing no supply/sensor/processing) reliably catches the erroneous primary data before loss of control; if a credited, timely standby cross-check is substantiated the aircraft effect could reduce below hull loss. Human-factors detection analysis would confirm or overturn Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on how much of the alert set is lost in the credited partial case; the SDD states two independent alerting processing channels but does not scope a representative partial degradation. If a partial loss removes a safety-critical alert whose absence is itself Major (per §5.4.2), that subset would be Major. Definition of the credited partial extent would confirm Minor.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on whether a single misleading alert can drive the crew to a procedure that shuts down a needed system or provokes an unsafe action; if a false alert can command an irreversible incorrect response with no recovery the condition could be Hazardous. Identifying the worst credited procedure invoked by an erroneous alert would confirm or overturn Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classification assumes the standalone loss of alerting, un-combined, is Major per §5.4.2 default and that no single concurrent failure elevated by loss of alerting is more severe than Major. Confirmed or overturned by the combination assessment (FHA/CMA) of alerting loss against each annunciated failure condition; a concurrent failure whose un-annunciated effect is Hazardous would drive the combination higher.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classification assumes the concurrent occurrence of an actual fire is not credited into the detection-loss condition itself (which alone gives no aircraft effect), and that an undetected fire in a fire zone leads to a large — not necessarily catastrophic — reduction in margins given the segregation and extinguishing provisions. Confirmed or overturned by the combination assessment of detection loss with an in-zone fire in the CMA/PRA; an undetected uncontained nacelle fire propagating to structure or fuel could be Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classification assumes the partial loss is annunciated (dual-loop detection degrading to single-loop is annunciated per the SDD) and that the retained zones cover the higher-consequence areas. Confirmed or overturned by the zonal extent of the credited partial loss; loss of all engine-nacelle detection while retaining only hold smoke detection would be more severe.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classification assumes a single erroneous engine-fire indication drives at most one engine shutdown and diversion on a four-engine aircraft with engine-out continuation capability, which is Major rather than Hazardous. Confirmed or overturned by whether erroneous detection can trigger multiple simultaneous responses or an in-flight extinguisher discharge that meaningfully degrades a live engine.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Classification assumes the latent loss of detection combined with a subsequent in-zone fire is credited as a large — not catastrophic — reduction, consistent with the total-loss row, and that no compensating latency-limiting check (e.g. periodic loop test) reveals the loss. Confirmed or overturned by the CMA latency treatment and the combination assessment with an in-zone fire; §25.4 significant-latent-failure handling applies if this contributes to a catastrophic combination.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether an unsuppressed nacelle/APU fire in this configuration propagates to hull loss within the time to land; SDD gives detection and two-bottle cross-plumbed suppression but not the fire-containment/burn-through substantiation. Assumed containment permits a Hazardous landing outcome; §25.851–869 fire test / burn-through analysis would confirm or push the class to Catastrophic (CAT-1).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class of the combined condition mirrors SF-021-TL and turns on the same fire-propagation-to-hull-loss question, plus the latency itself which §25.4 flags as a significant latent failure; SDD does not state the exposure interval or the CMR/pre-flight check that bounds the latency. Assumed the combination lands at Hazardous; fire test/burn-through substantiation and the latency-bounding maintenance task would confirm or push to Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the crew can complete an emergency descent to a breathable altitude before hypoxia impairs them and on the diversion time at FL260; SDD sizes the system for four occupants for the diversion time at max operating altitude but does not state that time or the descent capability with oxygen absent. Assumed the exposure supports Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; descent-profile and time-of-useful-consciousness analysis would confirm the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The Hazardous/Catastrophic line turns on whether the low pressurisation differential (≈8,800 m hold equivalent, FL260 max) shortens time-of-useful-consciousness enough to incapacitate the crew before descent; I assumed a survivable, workload-driven outcome (Hazardous), which pressurisation and diversion-time data would confirm or overturn to Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the total loss becomes evident and the reject is initiated before V1; if the loss occurs at/after V1 in the take-off roll the escape is defeated and the row carries the airborne end effect. Confirm against the RTO timeline.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the outboard-engine asymmetry at the 28 m arm during the take-off roll reduces directional margin to the Hazardous band before the crew arrests it; the SDD names this as the sizing case but gives no handling-quality result. Rudder authority analysis and the RTO handling data would confirm or lower this to Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an undetected partial thrust shortfall would be revealed by take-off performance monitoring before commit; if not, an erroneous performance basis carries into the take-off. Confirm the take-off performance monitoring / annunciation coverage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the undetected partial loss degrades performance margins to the Major band with the crew taking no action; the SDD does not state the annunciation coverage for a partial thrust shortfall. Annunciation/detection coverage analysis confirms or escalates this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the ~1,080 m predicted rollout against the 1,800 m requirement leaves sufficient margin to absorb loss of reverse thrust with wheel braking alone on a semi-prepared, possibly contaminated surface. hfaRows.text: Aircraft effect level for SF-002-PL in Standing, Taxi, Takeoff, Initial Climb, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Rejected Takeoff, Go-around assumed pending a MAC rule for SF-002 in those phases.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level 'large' is the derived MAC level for landing (1 of 2 inboard reversers lost); crew level 'significant' is assumed pending the HF workload task analysis, and whether wheel braking alone preserves the ~720 m margin without a reverser would confirm or lower the class. Occupant axis set by judgement as downstream of a possible low-speed overrun.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — In-flight deployment is inhibited by WOW + radio-altimeter agreement plus a mechanical sleeve lock (SDD 5.1.2); classified Hazardous rather than Catastrophic on the assumption that the interlocks make single-fault deployment credible-but-recoverable and that residual rudder/roll authority allows the crew to arrest the excursion. If deployment is shown unrecoverable at the inboard moment arm this becomes Catastrophic; a fault-tree/handling study confirms. Crew level assumed pending HF workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Ground-roll asymmetry from a single inboard reverser is assumed controllable by nose-wheel steering and differential braking at ground speed; if controllability on the low-flotation semi-prepared surface is worse than assumed this rises toward Hazardous. Crew level assumed pending HF workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Undetected asymmetry on reverse selection is assumed correctable by steering/differential braking at ground speed, holding the class at Major consistent with the §5.4.2 loss-of-annunciation default; if the uncorrected excursion on the low-flotation strip threatens an overrun it rises to Hazardous. Crew level assumed pending HF workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Ground-phase effect judged Minor as the aircraft simply stops; aircraft and crew levels pending the MAC and HF workload respectively. Escape 'stop on the ground' is available and not defeated.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Take-off row credits reject before V1 as the escape; after V1 total loss of feed to all engines would be catastrophic, but that portion is captured by the in-flight rows below. Levels pending the MAC and HF workload.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Ground-phase effect judged Minor; aircraft and crew levels pending the MAC and HF workload. Escape 'stop on the ground' available and not defeated.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level 'significant' is assumed pending the MAC for SF-003 — the number of independent feed means remaining after the partial loss governs the class; the SDD credits dual boost pumps, cross-feed and gravity feed below FL150, supporting Major, but the count of engines lost per partial-loss case is not yet fixed. Crew level assumed pending HF workload. If a partial loss can propagate to all engines the class rises.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew-workload level assumed pending the HF timed task; whether erroneous feed pressure can propagate to more than one engine (shared cross-feed gallery) and cause multi-engine rollback would raise the class — confirm from the fuel FMEA and the cross-feed isolation architecture.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class assumes the partial loss is single-engine and that a redundant feed path remains after it; if the undetected loss can affect feed to multiple engines through the shared cross-feed gallery the latent condition trends Hazardous — confirm from the fuel architecture and the annunciation coverage of boost-pump/feed-pressure monitoring.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level assumed pending the MAC and crew level pending the HF timed task; class assumes manual cross-feed/isolation is sufficient to hold imbalance below the 3,000 kg structural limit for the sector — if the manual means cannot arrest the drift within limits the end state is loss of control and Catastrophic. Confirm from the fuel MAC and a workload/timeline for manual fuel management.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level assumed pending the MAC and crew level pending the HF timed task; class assumes at least one transfer/cross-feed means remains after the partial loss so imbalance stays within the 3,000 kg limit. Confirm from the fuel MAC.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew level assumed pending the HF timed task; class turns on whether crew recognition (annunciation at 1,200 kg) and manual override arrest the excursion before the 3,000 kg structural imbalance or CG limit is exceeded — if they cannot within available time the end state is loss of control and Catastrophic. Confirm with a detection/response timeline against the imbalance rate and the CG/structural limits.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew-workload level assumed pending the HF task analysis (no timed crew task yet); confirmed by demonstrating imbalance-management workload and the exposure time before the 3,000 kg limit is reached. Would move toward Hazardous if the imbalance can reach the structural limit undetected within a sector.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level assumed pending the MAC rule for SF-005 (no MAC yet); the joint top step follows from loss of a primary control axis regardless. Class would only move down if a survivable degraded roll means (e.g. differential thrust / spoiler-only) is credited as retaining control, which the SDD does not state for roll.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft level assumed pending the MAC rule and crew level pending the HF workload (no MAC and no timed crew task yet). hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew level assumed pending the HF workload (no timed crew task yet); crew detection/arrest at altitude credited from the dissimilar-FCC architecture. Confirmed by the FCS voting/monitoring coverage and handling assessment; would move to Catastrophic if the erroneous output cannot be detected and arrested before loss of control.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

Would move down if the monitor guarantees detection and cutout within the low-altitude margin.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

HF workload analysis showing timely independent detection would move this below the top step.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew workload/detection level is recorded as assumed pending the HF task analysis (no timed crew task yet). The undetected variant is classified separately under SF-006-M3.

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

Because the condition is undetected, no crew correction is credited; if the erroneous pitch is unrecoverable in critical phases the aircraft axis reaches hull loss and this becomes Catastrophic (CAT-1). Per AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2 the loss-of-annunciation combination must meet the un-annunciated objective. Confirm with the FCS voting/monitoring coverage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

Confirm with the FCS pitch-monitor coverage and any independent stabiliser-runaway detection.

Aircraft level otherwise recorded as assumed pending the MAC for yaw. If a MAC/architecture review shows a survivable degraded yaw means after this failure this falls to Hazardous. Confirm with the FCS rudder split-segment and hydraulic supply analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

If ground handling in fact relies on rudder at high taxi speed the class could rise. Confirm with the ground directional-control analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

If HF analysis shows the erroneous transient exceeds the time available to recognise and counter, particularly in a low-altitude or asymmetric-thrust phase, this moves to Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Crew axis assumed 'significant' pending HF timed-task workload. An uncommanded hardover on the ground at speed (takeoff/RTO) or at low altitude may exceed recovery time or margins; if HF/handling analysis shows that, the affected phases become Hazardous and split onto their own row.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Aircraft axis assumed 'large' pending the SF-007 MAC and crew axis 'significant' pending HF workload; the escalation over the detected SF-007-PL rests on the loss of annunciation per §5.4.2. A MAC/architecture showing the reduction stays within margins even undetected, or evidence the loss is inherently perceptible in handling, would move this to Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

If the erroneous response is inherently perceptible in aircraft handling regardless of annunciation, or FCS voting/monitoring bounds the error magnitude, this reduces to Major — confirm against the FCS monitor coverage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — No timed crew task / HF workload record exists yet for detecting and arresting an undetected yaw excursion; crew level set assumed to 'large' pending the HF task analysis. hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes ground steering/braking remain available to arrest a low-speed yaw excursion (no timed HF task yet). If ground correction cannot be credited the ground rows rise to Major.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — No MAC rule for SF-008 and no timed HF task yet; aircraft and crew levels assumed. Confirm with performance analysis and the high-lift MAC.

Confirm with landing performance.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — End-effect class inherited from the landing-phase asymmetry assessment; same asymmetry-brake and HF caveats apply.

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — No MAC rule for high-lift yet and no timed crew task; aircraft and crew levels assumed pending the MAC and HF workload analysis. hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — No MAC rule and no timed crew task yet; levels assumed pending the MAC and HF workload. Resolve against the LDG MAC and ground-ops exposure analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Judged as a total loss with no alternative touchdown means credited; if a controllable belly/emergency landing with survivable deceleration is creditable the aircraft axis may reduce below hull loss. hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — No MAC rule and no timed crew task yet; levels assumed pending the MAC and HF workload. Six main bogies plus a nose unit give distributed redundancy; a partial loss is judged to leave the aircraft supported. If the degradation defeats flotation on the semi-prepared strip to the point of surface failure, the aircraft axis rises. Resolve against the LDG MAC and flotation sizing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Same judgement as the in-flight rows; levels assumed pending the MAC and HF workload. Resolve against the LDG MAC and flotation/landing-distance analysis.

Aircraft level Major credits the free-fall alternate extension and dual downlock sensing as an independent means the crew can work before touchdown. If both normal and alternate extension are lost, the landing rows below govern. Resolve against the LDG architecture and the alternate-extension task time.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

Resolve against the LDG architecture and structural crashworthiness analysis.

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the redundant lock sensing (dual proximity plus mechanical visual indicator) remains partly available so the crew can still establish gear state — if this failure removes ALL indication with no alternate, and the gear is in fact unlocked, the landing outcome could be Hazardous. hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

Confirm the SF-010 MAC and whether reverse thrust is credited as an independent deceleration means; if credited and sufficient, this may reduce.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Inadvertent in-flight reverse deployment, despite the WOW/radio-altimeter inhibit and mechanical sleeve lock, is credited as a controllable single-engine asymmetry rather than loss of the aircraft.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the asymmetric moment is within the sized rudder authority (outboard-engine case per §5.1.3) and the crew arrest the excursion; if the uncommanded thrust exceeded controllable authority or occurred at low speed on takeoff the class would rise. Directional-control margin data and a low-speed handling case would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes wheel braking with the 1,080 m predicted rollout against the 1,800 m requirement leaves sufficient margin on the semi-prepared surface without reverse; if braking degradation on a contaminated strip erodes that margin the class could rise. Wet/contaminated semi-prepared landing performance data would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the credited outcome is an in-flight inadvertent deployment on one inboard engine that the crew fight to control rather than a loss of the aircraft, matching the AFHA Hazardous anchor; if the asymmetry exceeded controllable authority the class would rise to Catastrophic. The rudder-authority margin against inboard-reverser asymmetry would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes nose-wheel steering and differential braking give the crew adequate directional authority to arrest the reverse asymmetry within the semi-prepared strip; if the excursion exceeded the strip or lateral control the class could rise. Ground directional-control authority against inboard reverser asymmetry would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Single-pack operation with a reduced hold conditioning schedule is a permitted dispatchable degraded mode that retains flight-deck distribution.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes flight-deck habitability degrades gradually and the crew retain crew oxygen and can descend/divert, keeping this Major rather than Hazardous; whether flight-deck conditioning loss becomes distressing within diversion time at the low FL260 ceiling would confirm or overturn the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and carries only flight crew, so no passenger conditioning or depressurisation exposure exists for any ECS failure condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Crew oxygen (quick-donning masks) is available and, with the FL260 ceiling and emergency descent, keeps crew capability sufficient after total loss of pressure control so the outcome is Hazardous not Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Independent positive and negative mechanical pressure relief protects the fuselage structure regardless of control-system state, so erroneous pressure control does not produce structural over/under-pressure failure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the error is detectable via displayed cabin-conditioning parameters and the crew can select the alternate pack or manual mode; if a hot-air overtemperature could progress to smoke/fumes on the flight deck before detection the class would rise, which the design description does not settle.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the undetected error does not progress to a flight-deck smoke/fume or overtemperature hazard the crew cannot recover from; if an undetected duct overtemperature could reach the flight deck the class would be higher, which the description does not resolve.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes crew oxygen is available and the FL260 ceiling plus emergency descent keep crew capability sufficient to avoid a Catastrophic outcome; the modest maximum altitude is favourable, but the time-to-incapacitation at the hold/flight-deck differential is not stated in the description and would confirm the class. During Standing/Taxi/Takeoff/Landing the effect is not realised and is a lower class; a per-phase split is deferred pending the pressurisation schedule.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the excursion is annunciated and the crew arrest it via manual mode before it reaches the depressurisation end-state, and that mechanical relief bounds any over-pressure; if the excursion could reach rapid depressurisation faster than crew response, this approaches the Total-loss Hazardous class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an independent cabin-altitude warning still triggers before crew incapacitation, holding this at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; the description does not state whether the excursion annunciation and the cabin-altitude warning are independent, and shared loss would raise the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The flight crew are alerted to a detected total or partial loss of surface/inlet ice protection and can exit the icing envelope before accretion becomes unrecoverable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Bleed protection remains available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold so a partial loss still holds the SF-017 MAC (at least one of the credited protection means available).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the crew are alerted and can escape icing before accretion becomes unrecoverable; if timely exit cannot be shown across all phases the outcome could approach Catastrophic. Icing-performance test/analysis per 14CFR-25.1419 would confirm the credited margins.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The independent integrated standby instrument provides valid air data if probe icing corrupts the primary air-data sources.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed erroneous heating does not damage surfaces or drive an undetected performance shortfall; if erroneous activation could mask a real need or overheat a component the class could rise. Design substantiation of the heater control logic would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed handling cues eventually alert the crew short of loss of control; if accretion can reach an unrecoverable state before any cue this approaches Catastrophic. Icing envelope test/analysis per 14CFR-25.1419 would settle whether recovery remains available.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the erroneous state degrades performance without causing structural overheat; if undetected overheat of a heated surface is credible the class could rise. Heater-control failure analysis and thermal substantiation would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed erroneous/unreliable airspeed from probe icing is manageable with standby data and manual anti-ice selection; if simultaneous air-data corruption across displays and standby is credible this approaches Catastrophic. Probe-heat and air-data independence analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the crew can recognise a false detection state from other cues and select protection manually, bounding the worst case (false-off) at Major; if a false-off is credibly undetected the appropriate row is the undetected variant. Detection-logic and crew-cue analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the standby air-data source stays valid so misleading airspeed is recoverable; if undetected probe icing can drive consistent erroneous airspeed across all sources this approaches Catastrophic. Air-data source independence and probe-heat monitoring analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the identical-type detectors could present a common erroneous 'no-ice' the crew trust; if an independent cross-cue (TAT, handling, redundant dissimilar means) reliably breaks the deception the class could be Major. Detector commonality analysis (recorded as an item for examination) would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A true total loss of all flight and navigation data presentation defeats the independent standby instrument at the same time as the primary displays.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Erroneous flight/navigation data is normally detectable through disagreement between the three reference units and the independent standby, giving the crew a valid comparison source.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed that a true total loss of presentation defeats the independent standby instrument simultaneously; the SDD states the standby shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, so a common cause taking all three at once is the credited condition for a total loss. If the standby is shown to remain independently available in this condition, this reduces toward partial loss and a lower class; architecture/common-mode analysis would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The loss of the crew alerting function is itself annunciated to the crew when at least one alerting channel remains or its health is monitored.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The alerts silently lost or misrepresented in the undetected alerting conditions do not include the most time-critical alerts whose un-actioned outcome is immediately catastrophic (fire, control, configuration).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No passengers are carried and the hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects fall on the flight crew only.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the erroneous data is presented in common across the primary sources with the comparison monitor also defeated, so the crew have no cue; if the architecture guarantees an independent comparison or standby that always flags the disagreement, the condition becomes detectable and reduces to the Major of SF-029-M. Common-mode and monitoring-coverage analysis would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed that with alerting undetected-lost, a following hazardous-but-not-catastrophic system failure goes unwarned so the combined effect reaches a large reduction in margins rather than an unrecoverable state; if a subsequent unwarned failure could itself be catastrophic (e.g. a fire or a control failure the crew must act on immediately), the compound condition rises toward Catastrophic. The FHA/FTA of the alerting-dependent conditions would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the silently-lost subset excludes the most time-critical alerts (fire, control, configuration), keeping the undetected gap at Major; if the lost subset includes an alert whose un-annunciated failure is hazardous or catastrophic, the specific compound condition rises accordingly. Identification of which alerts fall in the lost partition, via FHA of alerting-dependent conditions, would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the misleading alert does not by itself suppress a condition whose immediate un-actioned outcome is catastrophic; if it can suppress or misdirect the crew away from a catastrophic condition (e.g. a fire or an impending control loss requiring immediate action), the specific compound condition rises to Catastrophic. The two-channel independence argument and FHA of alerting-dependent conditions would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An established nacelle or APU fire can be starved and contained by engine/APU shutdown and fuel isolation within the fire-resistant zone even without extinguishant discharge, keeping loss-of-extinguishing and undetected-detection outcomes survivable rather than hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the total detection loss is annunciated to the crew (detection self-monitoring), making this the loss-of-function case rather than the undetected case; if detection loss were itself silent the severity rises, which is covered separately by SF-031-TL2. Fault-tree exposure and coincident-fire probability would confirm the class.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so no passenger or hold-occupant injury axis applies to any Fire Protection failure condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the degradation is annunciated and that the loss affects a subset of zones with the dual-loop AND-to-single-loop degradation being the credited partial case per §5.12.2; broader multi-zone loss would approach the total-loss case. Definition of what fraction constitutes partial would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a single erroneous warning on one zone with three engines remaining after any precautionary shutdown; a false warning during a critical phase (takeoff/go-around) or driving a same-side second shutdown could be more severe. Phase-specific analysis and the shutdown decision logic would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the credited outcome is a delayed but eventually recognised fire that remains survivable via extinguishing once cued, not an uncontrolled hull fire; if an undetected nacelle fire in this installation could not be contained the class would approach Catastrophic. The nacelle fire-containment analysis and secondary-cue timing would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the affected zone is one that still admits eventual secondary-cue detection and extinguishing; if the silently unmonitored zone were one where a fire could go directly to uncontrolled the class would rise. Which zones are covered by the partial-loss set and their containment margins would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed an undetected nacelle or APU fire remains within the fire-resistant zone long enough for secondary cues to prompt eventual extinguishing, keeping the outcome survivable rather than Catastrophic; if the specific zone cannot contain an undetected fire to safe flight and landing the class would be Catastrophic. Nacelle fire-zone burn-through and containment analysis would settle this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed that shutdown, fuel isolation and the fire-resistant zone design allow an established fire to be starved and contained without extinguishant in the credited case, keeping the outcome short of hull loss; if a nacelle fire without bottle discharge could not be contained the class would be Catastrophic. Fire-zone burn-through timing against fuel-isolation effectiveness would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the partial case is loss of one bottle of a pair with the cross-plumbed second bottle available, so a single-shot capability into the affected nacelle remains; loss reducing an engine pair to no discharge would be the total-loss case. The MAC set membership defining partial vs total would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — This condition string joins inadvertent discharge and failure-to-discharge, which are different failure conditions with potentially different severities; I classified the milder credited case with reserve remaining, but the engineer should split them, and a commanded-failure coincident with an actual fire that removes the last discharge would be Hazardous. Splitting the FCIM condition and analysing each would settle this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed shutdown and fuel isolation can still starve the fire in the credited case, keeping this short of hull loss as with SF-032-TL; if a nacelle fire cannot be contained without discharge the class rises to Catastrophic. Fire-zone containment analysis would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the silent partial loss leaves a working first-shot discharge into the affected zone via the cross-plumbed reserve; if the silent loss removed all discharge to a zone it becomes the undetected total-loss case. The MAC partial-vs-total set and which paths are lost would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the fire remains containable by delayed shutdown and isolation once the crew recognise the discharge did not work, keeping this Hazardous rather than Catastrophic; if the delay from the false belief in a successful discharge allows an uncontainable fire the class rises. Discharge-status indication coverage and containment timing would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the SFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm
